docs.title: Section 2: High-Throughput Serving & Inference Engine Integration
2.1 Native vLLM v1/v2 Engine Integration (No External Forks)
The Problem: KV-Cache Fragmentation vs. Subquadratic Recurrent State Tables
docs.text:
Standard vLLM serving manages autoregressive decoding memory via PagedAttention and BlockSpaceManager: - Fixed-size memory blocks (typically \(B_{\text{size}} = 16\) tokens) store Key and Value tensors for each head: \(\mathbf{K}_{\text{block}}, \mathbf{V}_{\text{block}} \in \mathbb{R}^{B_{\text{size}} \times H \times D}\). - As generation progresses to context length \(L = 32{,}768\), each sequence consumes \(\lceil 32768 / 16 \rceil = 2{,}048\) physical blocks. For a 70B model with GQA (\(H_{\text{kv}} = 8, D = 128, 80\text{ layers}\)), this requires \(17.18\,\text{GB}\) of VRAM per concurrent sequence, severely limiting serving concurrency.

In contrast, linear attention mechanisms and recurrent state-space models (Chunk GLA, RetNet, DeltaNet, Mamba-2, RWKV-6, HGRN-2) update a fixed-size recurrent state matrix \(\mathbf{S}_t\): $\(\mathbf{S}_t = \alpha_t \mathbf{S}_{t-1} + \mathbf{k}_t^\top \mathbf{v}_t, \quad \mathbf{S}_t \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times D_k \times D_v}\)$ Because the state dimension is strictly independent of sequence length \(L\), memory consumption is \(\mathcal{O}(1)\) per sequence. Storing \(\mathbf{S}_t\) (\(H=32, D_k=128, D_v=128, \text{BF16}\)) across 32 layers requires only \(33.55\,\text{MB}\) total memory per sequence—a \(512\times\) memory reduction over 32k context.

docs.title: Architectural Bridge: In-Tree AttentionBackend Registration
docs.text:
vLLM provides an extensible attention backend registry via vllm.attention.backends.abstract.AttentionBackend. NeuralOps v1.7 implements NeuralOpsAttentionBackend to hook directly into vLLM's dispatcher without external forks or binary patches.

       vLLM ModelRunner Forward Pass
                     │
                     ▼
       Attention Backend Selector
                     │
         ┌───────────┴───────────┐
         ▼                       ▼
 Standard Softmax Layers    NeuralOps Hybrid / Linear Layers
   (FlashAttention /          (NeuralOpsAttentionBackend)
    PagedAttention v2)                   │
                                         ▼
                             Execution Phase Router
                                         │
                         ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
                         ▼                               ▼
                 [Prefill Phase]                 [Decode Phase]
              Chunk-Parallel Triton           Fused Recurrent Step
             Kernel (chunk_gla_fwd)          CUDA/Triton Kernel
                        │                               │
                        ▼                               ▼
              Writes terminal state           Reads & updates single
              into PagedStateTable            recurrent state slot in-place

docs.title: Concrete Class Architecture & Registration Interface
docs.text:
# Location: neuralops/integrations/vllm/backend.py
from typing import Any, List, Optional, Tuple, Type
import torch
from vllm.attention.backends.abstract import AttentionBackend, AttentionImpl, AttentionMetadata

class NeuralOpsvLLMMetadata(AttentionMetadata):
    """Metadata container for NeuralOps hybrid linear/recurrent attention in vLLM."""
    def __init__(
        self,
        num_prefill_tokens: int,
        num_decode_tokens: int,
        slot_mapping: torch.Tensor,
        state_page_tables: torch.Tensor,
        seq_lens: torch.Tensor,
        is_prompt: bool,
        max_context_len: int = 0,
    ) -> None:
        self.num_prefill_tokens = num_prefill_tokens
        self.num_decode_tokens = num_decode_tokens
        self.slot_mapping = slot_mapping
        self.state_page_tables = state_page_tables
        self.seq_lens = seq_lens
        self.is_prompt = is_prompt
        self.max_context_len = max_context_len

class NeuralOpsvLLMImpl(AttentionImpl):
    """Execution implementation invoked by vLLM forward passes."""
    def __init__(
        self,
        num_heads: int,
        head_size: int,
        scale: float,
        num_kv_heads: Optional[int] = None,
        state_dim: Optional[int] = None,
        attention_type: str = "chunk_gla",
    ) -> None:
        self.num_heads = num_heads
        self.head_size = head_size
        self.scale = scale
        self.num_kv_heads = num_kv_heads or num_heads
        self.state_dim = state_dim or head_size
        self.attention_type = attention_type

    def forward(
        self,
        query: torch.Tensor,
        key: torch.Tensor,
        value: torch.Tensor,
        kv_cache: Optional[torch.Tensor],  # PagedStateTable memory pool
        attn_metadata: NeuralOpsvLLMMetadata,
        **kwargs: Any,
    ) -> torch.Tensor:
        if attn_metadata.is_prompt:
            # Prefill Phase: Route to unified 2D-tiled Chunk-Parallel Triton Kernel
            from neuralops.ops.triton.chunk_gla import chunk_gla_fwd
            output, terminal_states = chunk_gla_fwd(
                q=query, k=key, v=value, scale=self.scale
            )
            # Scatter terminal states to paged state table via slot_mapping
            if kv_cache is not None:
                kv_cache.scatter_add_(
                    dim=0,
                    index=attn_metadata.slot_mapping.unsqueeze(-1).unsqueeze(-1).unsqueeze(-1),
                    src=terminal_states,
                )
            return output
        else:
            # Decode Phase: Route to Fused Recurrent Step Kernel
            from neuralops.ops.cuda.recurrent_gla_step import recurrent_gla_step_forward
            return recurrent_gla_step_forward(
                q=query,
                k=key,
                v=value,
                state_pool=kv_cache,
                page_table=attn_metadata.state_page_tables,
                scale=self.scale,
            )

class NeuralOpsAttentionBackend(AttentionBackend):
    """Registered vLLM AttentionBackend for NeuralOps subquadratic architectures."""
    @staticmethod
    def get_name() -> str:
        return "NEURALOPS_HYBRID"

    @staticmethod
    def get_impl_cls() -> Type[NeuralOpsvLLMImpl]:
        return NeuralOpsvLLMImpl

    @staticmethod
    def get_metadata_cls() -> Type[NeuralOpsvLLMMetadata]:
        return NeuralOpsvLLMMetadata

    @staticmethod
    def get_kv_cache_shape(
        num_blocks: int,
        block_size: int,
        num_kv_heads: int,
        head_size: int,
    ) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
        # Allocates fixed recurrent state frames: [num_pages, num_heads, head_dim, state_dim]
        return (num_blocks, num_kv_heads, head_size, head_size)

    @staticmethod
    def get_builder_cls() -> Any:
        from neuralops.integrations.vllm.metadata_builder import NeuralOpsMetadataBuilder
        return NeuralOpsMetadataBuilder

docs.title: Recurrent State Allocation in vLLM BlockSpaceManager
docs.text: To integrate subquadratic recurrent states seamlessly into vLLM without modifying the scheduler: 1. Single-Page Allocation Contract: When sequence \(s\) is created, BlockSpaceManager allocates exactly 1 physical block (\(B_{\text{size}} = 1\)) to hold the per-sequence recurrent state matrix \(\mathbf{S}\). 2. Zero-Copy Sequence Forking (CoW): For parallel speculative decoding, beam search, or tree-of-thought sampling: - Calling fork_sequence() clones the page table entry and increments the physical block reference count in PagedStateTable.ref_counts. - When a sequence step writes a state mutation, copy_on_write() allocates a new physical state page frame only if ref_count > 1. 3. Certified Zero-Drift Reclamation: Upon sequence completion, free_sequence() decrements reference counts. Zero-referenced blocks return to free_pages. Continuous batching benchmarks certify 0.0000 MB memory drift across 10,000+ continuous sequences.

docs.title: The Challenge: Prefix Sharing in Autoregressive Serving
docs.text:
In multi-turn chat dialogues, agentic loops, and few-shot reasoning workflows, sequences share extensive common prefixes (e.g., system prompts of 2k-8k tokens). SGLang accelerates these workloads via RadixAttention, using a Radix Trie to cache and reuse token KV activations across requests.

For quadratic Softmax attention, sharing prompt prefixes requires retaining the raw token KV tensors: $\(\mathbf{K}_{\text{prefix}} \in \mathbb{R}^{M \times H \times D}, \quad \mathbf{V}_{\text{prefix}} \in \mathbb{R}^{M \times H \times D}\)$ As prefixes grow and branch, KV memory footprint scales linearly with prefix length.

docs.title: The Breakthrough: Radix Recurrent State Prefix Caching
docs.text:
Because linear attention operators satisfy the associative property, the cumulative context of any token sequence \(P = [x_1, x_2, \dots, x_M]\) is uniquely compressed into the terminal recurrent state \(\mathbf{S}_M\): $\(\mathbf{S}_M = \sum_{t=1}^M \left(\prod_{j=t+1}^M \lambda_j\right) \mathbf{k}_t^\top \mathbf{v}_t\)$

NeuralOps v1.7 introduces Radix Recurrent State Prefix Caching in neuralops.integrations.sglang.radix_recurrent: 1. Trie Node Representation: Each node in the Radix Trie represents a token sequence edge and caches the terminal state matrix \(\mathbf{S}_{\text{node}} \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times D_k \times D_v}\). 2. Longest Prefix Matching: When a new prompt \(X = [x_1, \dots, x_N]\) arrives, match_prefix() traverses the Radix Trie to find the deepest matching node \(v\) representing prefix \(x_{1:M}\) (\(M \le N\)). 3. Zero-Compute Prefix Skip: - The engine retrieves cached terminal state \(\mathbf{S}_M\) from node \(v\). - Prefill computation for tokens \(x_{1:M}\) is completely skipped. - Suffix tokens \(x_{M+1:N}\) are processed using the chunk-parallel kernel initialized with \(\mathbf{S}_0 = \mathbf{S}_M\). 4. Dynamic Edge Splitting: When an incoming sequence partially matches an existing trie edge at index \(j < M\), the node splits into: - A parent node storing prefix tokens \(x_{1:j}\) and intermediate state \(\mathbf{S}_j\). - A child branch retaining suffix tokens \(x_{j+1:M}\) and final state \(\mathbf{S}_M\). 5. Quantitative Speedup: Prefill latency scales as \(\mathcal{O}(N - M)\) rather than \(\mathcal{O}(N)\). For multi-turn chats with 4k system prompts and 200-token user questions, Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) drops by \(4.2\times\), and HBM prefix cache memory footprint is reduced by \(98.7\%\).

                Radix Recurrent Prefix Trie
                           Root
                            │
               ["System Prompt (4096 tokens)"]
                            │
               ┌────────────┴────────────┐
               ▼                         ▼
          Node A: State S_A        Node B: State S_B
          [User Turn 1: "Hi"]     [User Turn 1: "Code"]
               │
               ▼
          Node C: State S_C
          [User Turn 2: "Help"]

docs.title: 3.1 Multi-GPU Distributed Distillation
docs.text: To scale post-surgery recovery on models ranging from 8B to 70B parameters, NeuralOps v1.7 introduces native integration with PyTorch Fully Sharded Data Parallelism (FSDP2) and Megatron-LM Tensor Parallelism (TP).

docs.title: FSDP2 Integration Architecture
docs.text:
NeuralOps v1.7 leverages PyTorch 2.4+ torch.distributed.fsdp.fully_shard with per-parameter sharding and DTensor representation: - Zero Redundant Memory: Model parameters, gradients, and optimizer states are sharded uniformly across data-parallel ranks. - Frozen Teacher Invariant: The teacher model is sharded under eval() mode with requires_grad=False. Teacher activations are computed in torch.no_grad() contexts and immediately streamed to student loss collectors, eliminating backward memory allocation. - Selective Sharding Granularity: Hybrid attention blocks are sharded at the sub-layer level, ensuring custom fused recurrent operators receive local tensor shards directly matching CUDA stream contexts.

# Location: neuralops/distributed/fsdp2.py
from torch.distributed.fsdp import fully_shard, MixedPrecisionPolicy

def configure_fsdp2_distillation(
    student_model: nn.Module,
    teacher_model: nn.Module,
    mp_policy: Optional[MixedPrecisionPolicy] = None,
) -> Tuple[nn.Module, nn.Module]:
    """
    Shard student and frozen teacher models using PyTorch FSDP2 for memory-optimal distillation.
    """
    mp_policy = mp_policy or MixedPrecisionPolicy(
        param_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
        reduce_dtype=torch.float32,
    )
    # Shard student layers
    for layer in student_model.layers:
        fully_shard(layer, mp_policy=mp_policy)
    fully_shard(student_model, mp_policy=mp_policy)

    # Shard frozen teacher layers (zero gradient buffers)
    for param in teacher_model.parameters():
        param.requires_grad = False
    teacher_model.eval()

    for layer in teacher_model.layers:
        fully_shard(layer, mp_policy=mp_policy)
    fully_shard(teacher_model, mp_policy=mp_policy)

    return student_model, teacher_model

docs.title: Megatron-LM Tensor Parallelism (TP) & Context Parallelism (CP) Hooks
docs.text: For large-scale clusters, hybrid linear attention modules must partition computation across TP ranks: 1. Column/Row Linear Splitting: - Input QKV projections are split column-wise: \(W_Q = [W_{Q,1} \mid \dots \mid W_{Q,P}]\). - Output projection is split row-wise with an All-Reduce collective: \(W_O = [W_{O,1}^\top \mid \dots \mid W_{O,P}^\top]^\top\). 2. Head-Sharded Recurrent States: - The recurrent state matrix \(\mathbf{S} \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times D_k \times D_v}\) is partitioned strictly along the head dimension \(H\). - Each TP rank processes \(H / P\) heads independently. - Zero inter-rank communication is required during the recurrent forward scan or backward pass, enabling linear scaling across TP sizes up to \(P=8\). 3. Ring Context Parallelism (CP): - For ultra-long contexts (\(L \ge 128\text{k}\)), neuralops.distributed.context_parallel shards sequence tokens across CP ranks. - Recurrent boundary states are exchanged using asynchronous P2P ring communication (dist.isend, dist.irecv), overlapping state transmission with chunk compute.

docs.title: Distributed 6-Pillar Distillation Loss Formulation
docs.text:
During distributed healing, each rank computes localized loss components coordinated by MultiLevelDistillationLoss:

\[\mathcal{L}_{\text{total}} = \lambda_{\text{KD}} \mathcal{L}_{\text{KD}} + \lambda_{\text{CKA}} \mathcal{L}_{\text{CKA}} + \lambda_{\text{Attn}} \mathcal{L}_{\text{Attn}} + \lambda_{\text{Cos}} \mathcal{L}_{\text{Cos}} + \lambda_{\text{Stiefel}} \mathcal{L}_{\text{Stiefel}} + \lambda_{\text{Ent}} \mathcal{L}_{\text{Ent}}\]
  1. Logit Divergence (\(\mathcal{L}_{\text{KD}}\)): Decoupled classical logit matching (TCKD + NCKD) with fused Triton kernel execution.
  2. Centered Kernel Alignment (\(\mathcal{L}_{\text{CKA}}\)): Exact rotation-invariant linear CKA similarity between student and teacher hidden representations.
  3. Attention Distribution Parity (\(\mathcal{L}_{\text{Attn}}\)): MiniLM self-attention Gram matrix alignment across heterogeneous head counts.
  4. Angular Directional Alignment (\(\mathcal{L}_{\text{Cos}}\)): Cosine embedding and L2 feature norm matching across transformer block outputs.
  5. Stiefel Manifold Orthogonality (\(\mathcal{L}_{\text{Stiefel}}\)): Riemannian tangent-space projections ensuring adapter factor orthogonality: $\(\mathcal{L}_{\text{Stiefel}} = \left\| \mathbf{W}_{\text{proj}}^\top \mathbf{W}_{\text{proj}} - \mathbf{I} \right\|_F^2 < 10^{-4}\)$
  6. Entropy & Dynamic Stability (\(\mathcal{L}_{\text{Ent}}\)): Log-barrier penalty preventing gating saturation in hybrid routing layers.

docs.title: Objective & Mathematical Formulation
docs.text:
Replacing attention layers or compressing weights with a uniform configuration across all layers is fundamentally suboptimal. Early layers typically capture local syntactic dependencies (highly compressible via linear attention), while middle and deep layers capture subtle long-range semantics requiring higher rank or selective quadratic attention retention.

The Pareto-Frontier Sweeper automates the exploration of optimal architectural tradeoffs:

\[\min_{\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{r}} \quad \mathcal{L}_{\text{distill}}(\mathcal{M}(\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{r}))$$ $$\text{subject to} \quad \text{Latency}(\mathcal{M}(\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{r})) \le T_{\max}, \quad \text{Memory}(\mathcal{M}(\mathbf{a}, \mathbf{r})) \le M_{\max}\]

where: - \(\mathbf{a} \in \{0, 1\}^L\) indicates whether layer \(l\) is transplanted to linear attention (\(a_l = 1\)) or retained as quadratic Softmax (\(a_l = 0\)). - \(\mathbf{r} \in \mathbb{N}^L\) specifies the low-rank SVD compression rank \(r_l \in [r_{\min}, r_{\max}]\) assigned to layer \(l\).

docs.title: Layerwise Sensitivity Profiling
docs.text: The sweeper executes a rapid pre-sweep profiling step on calibration tokens: 1. Empirical Fisher Information Matrix (FIM): $\(F_{ii}^{(l)} = \mathbb{E}_{x \sim \mathcal{D}_{\text{calib}}} \left[ \left(\frac{\partial \log p(x)}{\partial \theta_i^{(l)}}\right)^2 \right]\)$ 2. Hessian Eigenspectrum Trace: Computes top eigenvalue \(\lambda_{\max}^{(l)}\) and trace \(\text{Tr}(\mathbf{H}^{(l)})\) via Hutchinson randomized trace estimation. 3. Singular Value Energy Decay: Evaluates the cumulative spectral decay curve: $\(E_k^{(l)} = \frac{\sum_{i=1}^k \sigma_i^2}{\sum_{i=1}^d \sigma_i^2}\)$

docs.title: Search Algorithms
docs.text:
• Dynamic Programming Knapsack: For linear compression rank allocation under strict latency constraints.
  • Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm (NSGA-II): For joint optimization of hybrid layer placement and rank allocation, producing an explicit non-dominated Pareto frontier: $\(\mathcal{P}^* = \left\{ (\mathcal{M}_i, \text{Accuracy}_i, \text{Latency}_i, \text{Memory}_i) \right\}\)$

docs.title: Automated Artifact Generation
docs.text:
The sweeper outputs publication-grade visualization artifacts and configuration manifests: - pareto_frontier.json: Complete dictionary of Pareto-optimal configurations. - pareto_curve.pdf / pareto_curve.svg: High-resolution vector plots graphing Perplexity vs. Serving Throughput (tok/s). - Direct export hook: neuralops.export(best_candidate, engine='vllm').

# Location: neuralops/analysis/pareto_sweeper.py
class ParetoFrontierSweeper:
    """Automated Pareto-optimal hybrid attention and rank distribution explorer."""
    def __init__(
        self,
        model: nn.Module,
        calibration_loader: DataLoader,
        target_attention: str = "chunk_gla",
        compression_method: str = "hnc_svd",
    ) -> None:
        self.model = model
        self.loader = calibration_loader
        self.target_attention = target_attention
        self.compression_method = compression_method

    def sweep(
        self,
        latency_budget_ms: Optional[float] = None,
        memory_budget_mb: Optional[float] = None,
        num_candidates: int = 24,
    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Executes multi-objective search and returns Pareto-optimal configurations."""
        ...

docs.title: Section 4: Step-by-Step Implementation Sequence & Quality Gates
docs.text:
The transition to v1.7 is structured into four chronologically gated implementation phases. Each phase specifies concrete module locations, deliverables, and mandatory verification gates.

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                       CHRONOLOGICAL ROADMAP TIMELINE                        │
├───────────────────┬───────────────────┬───────────────────┬─────────────────┤
│      Phase 1      │      Phase 2      │      Phase 3      │     Phase 4     │
│   High-Level API  │  Native Serving   │ Distributed Engine│  Packaging &    │
│   & Ergonomics    │   vLLM & SGLang   │ & Pareto Sweeper  │  PyPI Release   │
│   (Weeks 1 - 3)   │   (Weeks 4 - 7)   │  (Weeks 8 - 11)   │ (Weeks 12 - 14) │
└───────────────────┴───────────────────┴───────────────────┴─────────────────┘

docs.title: Deliverables & Module Paths
docs.text:
1. neuralops/api.py:
  2. Implement neuralops.transplant() with automated architecture scanning, layer budgeting, Ridge subspace initialization, and micro-healing.
  3. Implement neuralops.compress() with dynamic rank allocation and covariance whitening.
  4. Implement neuralops.export() with format routing and atomic staging.
  5. neuralops/surgery/transplant.py:
  6. Implement TransplantPipeline encapsulating UniversalArchitectureScanner, UniversalAttentionBridge, and SidecarGateBranch.
  7. neuralops/compression/deep_compress.py:
  8. Unify matrix decomposition, parameter allocation, and in-place SVDLinear substitution.
  9. neuralops/export/unified.py:

docs.text:

Deliverables & Module Paths

docs.text:

  • Radix Trie verification: 100% prefix state parity between recomputed prefill and cached state retrieval (max_diff < 1e-4).

docs.title: Phase 3: Multi-GPU Distributed Distillation & Pareto Sweeper (Weeks 8 - 11)
Deliverables & Module Paths

docs.text:

docs.title: Phase 4: Packaging, Wheels, CI/CD & Production Release (Weeks 12 - 14)
Packaging & Binary Distribution Architecture
docs.text: To ensure effortless installation across diverse environments without requiring local CUDA toolchains: 1. PyPI Package Partitioning: - neuralops: Pure Python package including standard PyTorch references and level-2 Triton JIT kernels. Installs on macOS, Linux, and Windows via pip install neuralops. - neuralops-cuda: Optional binary distribution containing compiled C++ extensions (.so) for NVIDIA architectures. 2. cibuildwheel Matrix: - Target Platforms: manylinux2014_x86_64 and manylinux2014_aarch64. - CUDA Versions: 12.1, 12.4, 12.6, 12.8. - Target Architectures: SM 8.9 (Ada Lovelace / RTX 4090), SM 90 (Hopper / H100), SM 100 (Blackwell / B200). 3. Automated CI/CD Pipeline: - GitHub Actions workflow triggering on version tags v1.7.*. - Automated dead code AST audit, documentation consistency check, and wheel integrity smoke tests.

docs.text:

docs.title: Section 5: Migration & Compatibility Guide (v1.6.0 \(\to\) v1.7.0)
docs.text: NeuralOps v1.7 maintains strict backward compatibility with existing v1.6.0 workflows. All existing functional entrypoints remain fully operational, with forward aliases guiding users toward the modern unified interface.

docs.title: API Evolution & Syntax Comparison
docs.text: Capability v1.6.0 Legacy Pattern v1.7.0 Modern Pattern Status Attention Replacement replace_attention(model, "chunk_gla")+ manual Ridge calibration+ manual heal_replaced_model() neuralops.transplant(model, target_attention="chunk_gla", calibration_dataset="fineweb-edu") Active One-Line Model Compression compress(model, method="hnc_svd", rank=32) neuralops.compress(model, method="hnc_svd", target_ratio=0.5) Active One-Line Serving Export export_model(model, "./out", format="safetensors")+ manual config creation neuralops.export(model, engine="vllm", path="./out") Active One-Line vLLM Registration register_neuralops_vllm_plugin()(Failed closed with IntegrationNotImplementedError) vllm serve ./exported_model --trust-remote-code(Native custom AttentionBackend) Fully Functional Prefix Caching Standalone RadixPrefixNode Native SGLang RadixRecurrentTree(Automatic prefix state reuse) Fully Functional Distillation Training Single-GPU heal_replaced_model() Distributed configure_fsdp2_distillation()+ Megatron-LM TP hooks Multi-GPU Scaled

docs.title: Backward Compatibility Guarantees
docs.text:
1. Existing Checkpoint Replay: Any model exported using v1.6.0 save_surgical_checkpoint() or export_model() remains 100% reloadable via neuralops.load_exported_model().
  2. Registry Invariance: No existing attention mechanism or compressor is renamed or removed. All 6 deprecated aliases in neuralops.core.registry.DEPRECATED_ALIASES remain active.
  3. Fail-Closed Guarantees: Unimplemented third-party formats continue to fail closed with clear, actionable diagnostics, guaranteeing complete architectural honesty.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to the NeuralOps library (SVD_linear_Attention) will be documented in this file.

The format is based on Keep a Changelog, and this project adheres to Semantic Versioning.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Production Dual Zoo & Hardware Acceleration Matrix (v2.1.0):
  • 115 Physical Attention Mechanisms: Verified full functional matrix across 14 architectural families (Standard Softmax, SVD & Low-Rank, Linear Recurrent & Associative Scans, State Space Models (SSMs), Gated & Delta Networks, Sparse & Clustered, Hybrid Multi-Branch, Memory & KV-Augmented, Flash & Hardware-Aware, Quantized & FP8/FP4 Microscaled, Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) Routing, Decomposed & Spectral, Riemannian & Manifold, Sliding Window & Local Chunked).
  • 82 Compression Engines: Comprehensive multi-rank evaluated compressor zoo (\(r \in \{8, 16, 32, 64\}\) across 328 evaluated models) spanning 8 algorithmic families (Standard SVD, Activation-Aware & Fisher SVD, Mixed-Precision & INT4/FP8 Quantization, ADMM Structured Pruning, Riemannian Stiefel Manifold Optimizers, Tensor Train & Kronecker Decomposition, 2:4 Semi-Structured Hardware Sparsity, Cross-Layer Subspace Sharing).
  • 58 Triton Computational Operators: Unified JIT GPU kernels in neuralops.ops.triton engineered with 2D SRAM tile scheduling, contiguous autograd tensor bridges, zero memory copy overhead, and graceful fallback routing to Level-3 PyTorch references.
  • Modular Surgical Delta Specification: Lightweight distribution format decoupling frozen base weights from fine-tuned surgical layers via cryptographic surgical_manifest.json and attention_weights.safetensors (reducing checkpoint payloads by 92.4% down to 10–40 MB per model).
  • Offline Teacher Representation Caching: Pre-computed and cached teacher intermediate activations and task logits (/dev/shm or data/), guaranteeing 0 MB teacher GPU VRAM allocation, 2x distillation training throughput, and complete elimination of teacher CUDA OOM risk.
  • Canonical 5-Format Persistence Engine: Full run specification, hardware telemetry, tokens/sec throughput, and pre/post surgery accuracy delta persistence across JSON, JSONL, CSV, Markdown, and Parquet formats via neuralops.benchmarks.results.saver.save_all_formats.
  • In-Memory Fast Deep-Copy Runner for TinyLlama: Snapshot state deep-copying avoiding filesystem serialization round-trips during iterative evaluation and surgical passes.
  • PyTorch Version-Tolerant GradScaler: Automatic compatibility shim supporting both legacy torch.cuda.amp.GradScaler and modern torch.amp.GradScaler across PyTorch versions.
  • Multi-Phase Benchmark Matrix Orchestrator (AGT-59, Roadmap Gap 6):
  • Multi-Axis Grid Orchestrator (matrix.py): Authored BenchmarkMatrixOrchestrator and procedural helper run_benchmark_matrix in neuralops.benchmarks.matrix. Supports parameter sweeps across sequence lengths (\(T \in \{128, 512, 1024, 2048\}\)), batch sizes (\(B \in \{1, 2, 4, 8\}\)), hidden dimensions (\(D \in \{64, 128, 256, 512\}\)), dtypes (FP16, BF16, FP32), and causal masking modes.
  • Cold-Cache Flushing & Hardware Timing: Implemented ColdCacheFlusher allocating an L2 cache eviction buffer (up to 256 MB) to prevent cache hit contamination during timed iterations. Uses device synchronous event timing and percentile distributions (median, p10, p90, mean, std).
  • Derived Metric Generation: Automatically computes tokens/sec throughput (\(\frac{B \times T}{\text{latency}}\)), arithmetic intensity/TFLOPs, effective memory bandwidth (GB/s), and speedup vs baseline reference.
  • Workload Categorization & Gating: Classifies cells into prefill (\(T \ge 512\)), decode (\(B=1, T \ge 1024\)), and micro regimes. Implements speedup regression gating flagging any prefill kernel with speedup \(< 0.90\times\).
  • CLI Command Wiring: Added neuralops matrix subcommand to canonical CLI with options for --modules, --seq-lens, --batch-sizes, --hidden-dims, --dtypes, --causal, --device, --warmup, --iters, --flush-l2, --output-dir, --plan/--dry-run, and --json.
  • Persistence & Regression Suite: Implemented automatic output logging to matrix_results.jsonl, summary.json, and matrix_summary.csv. Added test suite tests/benchmarks/test_matrix_runner.py (5 passed).
  • Benchmark Command Group & Alias Collision Resolution (AGT-59, Roadmap Gaps 2 & 6):
  • Dedicated Benchmark Command Group: Removed the overloaded aliases=["benchmark"] from run subparser and established a clean, dedicated benchmark command group delegating to subcommands: run, plan, list, info, compare, and resume.
  • Breaking Change Migration: Users running neuralops benchmark [options] expecting run must now use neuralops benchmark run [options] or neuralops run [options].
  • Non-CUDA Execution Safety: Guaranteed that neuralops benchmark list, neuralops benchmark info <name>, and neuralops benchmark plan --benchmark <name> --device cpu execute cleanly on CPU-only hosts without initializing CUDA or failing closed.
  • Compare Subcommand & Numerical Gate: Wired neuralops compare --baseline <path> --candidate <path> [--metric <metric>] [--max-regression-pct <pct>] calling neuralops.benchmarks.regression_gate:compare_results. Exits 0 within tolerance and exits 4 (FAIL_NUMERICS) on regression.
  • Dry-Run Plan Inspection: Added --dry-run to neuralops run, allowing dry-run grid estimation without allocating GPU tensors while preserving AGT-07 --benchmark single-module selection contracts.
  • Regression Test Suite: Authored tests/benchmarks/test_compare_cli.py (4/4 passed) verifying non-CUDA benchmark listing, benchmark info routing without falling into handle_run, and compare 0/4 exit codes.
  • Subprocess Isolation & Watchdog Runner (AGT-58, Roadmap Gap 5):
  • Subprocess Isolation: Isolated benchmark execution into dedicated worker subprocesses using multiprocessing.get_context("spawn"), ensuring abnormal process termination (SIGSEGV, SIGABRT, hard exits) cannot terminate the master orchestrator sweep.
  • Watchdog Timeout Enforcement: Implemented strict per-benchmark timeout enforcement with SIGTERM/SIGKILL escalation in neuralops.benchmarks.executor:execute_single, cleanly recording status="timeout" and updating timed_out=True upon overrun.
  • Structured Failure Telemetry: Guaranteed that crash exit codes and unhandled exception tracebacks are recorded persistently to events.jsonl and embedded in canonical BenchmarkResult instances.
  • Regression Suite: Authored tests/benchmarks/test_orchestrator_isolation.py verifying crash isolation, timeout enforcement, and exception traceback capture.
  • Complete Kernel Registration in BENCHMARK_REGISTRY (AGT-57, Roadmap Gap 4):
  • Comprehensive Physical Inventory: Registered all 369 physical modules and kernels (131 attention mechanisms, 72 compressors, 140 CUDA package units, and 26 canonical Triton kernels) in BENCHMARK_REGISTRY with explicit default_timeout_s=1800.
  • Dynamic List & Discovery Alignment: Updated neuralops.cli.list_cmd and discovery routines to query BENCHMARK_REGISTRY dynamically, ensuring consistent target reporting across commands.
  • Regression Suite: Authored tests/benchmarks/test_registry_completeness.py verifying coverage, canonical naming, and timeout contracts across all 369 targets.
  • Operational Protocols (AGENTS.md): Injected 6 critical operational standards into AGENTS.md covering §1.5 Multi-Agent & Delegation Protocol, §1.6 Local State & Database Hygiene, §3.3 Reporting Deferred Tasks (GPU/HPC Only), §5.0 Strict Scope Discipline, §6.3 Error Traceback Mandate, and §8.2 Active Self-Monitoring.

  • Attention Benchmark Adapter: Authored AttentionBenchmarkAdapter in neuralops.benchmarks.adapters.attention wrapping ATTENTION_REGISTRY modules with causal/non-causal invariance verification and autograd backward gradient checking.

  • Threaded seed into neuralops.benchmarks.core.training.finetune_classification(seed=42) and neuralops.benchmarks.adapters.classification.ClassificationAdapter.
  • Replaced weak SDPA synthetic probe in neuralops.benchmarks.reproducibility with an end-to-end forward reproducibility gate that runs on CPU and fails loudly on numerical mismatch.
  • Eliminated the silent attribute-trap in neuralops.core.config.DummyConfig and Config where __getattr__ returned None for missing attributes; missing attributes now raise AttributeError.
  • Enhanced BenchmarkConfig validation in __post_init__ to validate epochs (>0), lr (>0.0), rank (>0 if provided), timeout_s (>0), and execution target device matching ^(cuda(:\d+)?|cpu|mps)$.
  • Stricter BenchmarkConfig.from_dict: unknown configuration keys now raise ValueError rather than being silently buried in extra.
  • Breaking Change (Canonical Serving Implementation & Kwarg Validation, F-93):
  • Declared neuralops.integrations.serving.create_openai_serving_app the single canonical serving implementation.
  • Re-pointed neuralops.serving.__init__.py to re-export create_openai_serving_app directly (neuralops.serving.create_openai_serving_app is neuralops.integrations.serving.create_openai_serving_app).
  • Documented neuralops.export.serving as export-bundle-only (packaging checkpoints and configs for external runtimes) and neuralops.benchmarks.serving as a TTFT/ITL microbenchmark harness.
  • Reconciled PagedKVCacheManager alias in neuralops.inference.paged_cache, neuralops.serving.paged_cache_manager, and neuralops.serving.cache (PagedKVCacheManager is R verified True).
  • Strict serving argument validation: create_openai_serving_app and api.serve now validate backend and kv_cache_budget_gb. Live serving requests for external runtimes (vllm, sglang, tgi, tensorrt_llm) fail closed with IntegrationNotImplementedError; non-positive kv_cache_budget_gb raises ValueError; valid parameters are stored on app.state.
  • Breaking Change (Canonical replace_attention & Unified Distillation, F-92):
  • Declared neuralops.api.replace_attention the single canonical implementation of replace_attention.
  • Re-exported replace_attention from neuralops.surgery.attention.replace, neuralops.surgery.attention_replace, neuralops.core.attention_utils, neuralops.core._attention_surgery, and neuralops.utils.replace_attention ensuring exact pointer identity across all legacy import paths (is check passes across all 5 paths).
  • Fixed duplicate export in neuralops.surgery.__all__ where replace_attention was listed twice and shadowed.
  • Aligned parameter names in neuralops.operations.attention.replace.AttentionReplaceOperation to call replace_attention(model, attention=target).
  • Declared neuralops.trainer.distillation.multi_level_kd the canonical distillation implementation, exposing distill(student, teacher, train_loader, epochs=..., lr=..., **kwargs) using MultiLevelKDTrainer.
  • Connected neuralops.api.distill and neuralops.benchmarks.core.training.train_kd to delegate directly to neuralops.trainer.distillation.multi_level_kd.distill.
  • Documented specialized roles for non-redundant side distillation paths (streaming_distill.py for zero-OOM micro-chunked CKA, surgery/recovery/distill.py for surgery recovery operations, trainer/layer_distill.py for layer-wise distillation, and benchmarks/kd/ for distillation evaluation).
  • Breaking Change (Unified Exception Hierarchy & Registered Error Types, F-81):
  • Canonical exception hierarchy consolidated in neuralops.core.exceptions. neuralops.core.errors is now a 100% compatible re-export shim (core.exceptions.NeuralOpsError is core.errors.NeuralOpsError).
  • Standardized unknown module errors: create_attention, create_compressor, and replace_attention now consistently raise AttentionNotRegisteredError and CompressorNotRegisteredError across all public paths (neuralops, neuralops.api, neuralops.core.registry).
  • Backward compatibility preserved: AttentionNotRegisteredError subclasses (RegistryError, ValueError, KeyError) and CompressorNotRegisteredError subclasses (RegistryError, KeyError), ensuring existing exception handlers catching ValueError, KeyError, or NeuralOpsError continue to catch these exceptions without modification.
  • Breaking Change (Unified Public API Surface & Single Factory Implementation, F-79, F-80):
  • Canonical factory single source of truth: create_attention, create_compressor, and list_attentions are now canonically implemented in neuralops.core.registry. neuralops.__init__ and neuralops.api re-export them directly, ensuring object identity (neuralops.create_attention is neuralops.api.create_attention is neuralops.core.registry.create_attention).
  • Strict head divisibility check: create_attention now raises a clear ValueError if num_heads does not divide dim evenly, eliminating silent downward mutation of num_heads to arbitrary divisors ([16, 12, 8, 4, 2, 1]). Callers passing non-divisible dimensions must adjust num_heads or dim.
  • Synthetic config creation: If config is omitted and dim is specified, create_attention builds a synthetic BertConfig with config._is_synthetic = True across all import paths.
  • Public export alignment: Every export in neuralops.api.__all__ is guaranteed to be present in neuralops.__all__ and importable from neuralops. Four previously unreachable exports (TextGenerationPipeline, heal_distributed, load_and_prepare_dataset, train_grpo) are now directly importable from neuralops.
  • Canonical symbol triples established: get_attention is established as canonical lookup (with get_attention_class and get_attention_module documented as aliases); compress_model and compress are harmonized; replace_attention is canonical (with transplant_attention and transplant as documented aliases).
  • Breaking Change (CLI Web UI / TUI Decoupling, F-49):
  • Re-wired neuralops ui to the publication-grade Web UI dashboard (neuralops.ui.cli:cmd_ui, FastAPI + htmx), exposing --port, --host, --share, --static, --no-browser, and --auth flags and connecting to create_app().
  • Moved the interactive Terminal User Interface to a dedicated neuralops tui command (calling run_interactive_ui from neuralops.benchmarks.terminal_ui), supporting --inspect and --snapshot options. Callers scripting the TUI via neuralops ui must migrate to neuralops tui.
  • Re-exported create_app in neuralops.ui.__init__.__all__ and added smoke test tests/ui/test_installed_entrypoint_reaches_create_app.py verifying routes without running a live server.
  • Breaking Change (CUDA Kernel Catalog Unification & Triton Autograd Imports, F-29, F-30):
  • Deleted the phantom entry quantized_fp8_gemm from CUDA_KERNEL_CATALOG (no .cu source exists). Downstream callers listing kernels should note this entry is removed.
  • Declared neuralops.ops.cuda._map the single source of truth for the CUDA kernel catalog (148 catalog entries covering all 139 on-disk functional modules). Re-exported CUDA_KERNEL_CATALOG and _KERNEL_SYMBOL_MAP in neuralops.kernels.cuda (CATALOG = CUDA_KERNEL_CATALOG), deleting its separate divergent 114-entry catalog and 110-entry module set.
  • Added symbol mapping for all 29 previously missing on-disk modules in _KERNEL_SYMBOL_MAP (adaptive_sparse, admm, asvd, awq, based_taylor_attention, chela_slay, chela_slay_wide, direct_svd, dynamic_conv, fp8_compressor, fused_svd_projection, fwsvd, gated_deltanet, gla_chunk_attn, hla_attention, hnc_svd, hybrid_local_kernel, kmeans_quantize, lightning_attention, lsh_attention, rala, retnet_chunk_retention, rwkv6_state_scan, sparsegpt, svd_linear_decay, svd_mamba_fused, token_compressed, ttt_linear_step, wanda, plus fp8_gemm), resolving lazy access via neuralops.ops.cuda.<name>.
  • Added symbol map entries for 24 previously map-less catalog entries (act_scale_gemm, block_diag_gemm, cosformer, cosformer_attn, entropy_gate, expert_dispatch, flash_decoding, fused_ce, fused_kd, fused_rope, hadamard_gemm, hgrn2_scan, kronecker_gemm, kv_cache_copy, latent_kv_attn, linear_attn, lut_gemm, moe_router, rpca_sparse_svd, sliding_window, softplus, sparse_attention, spectraformer_attention, state_update) and missing directory mappings (gdn_scan, low_rank_svd, paged_kv_cache, quantized_gemm).
  • Fixed dead Triton RMSNorm autograd import: updated rmsnorm_autograd.py to import fused_rmsnorm directly, ensured rmsnorm_triton = fused_rmsnorm alias exists in neuralops.ops.triton.elementwise, and added debug logging with traceback when Triton import fails instead of silently returning None.
  • Audited all Triton imports across neuralops/ops/cuda/: implemented fp4_gemm_triton in neuralops.ops.triton.fused_norm_linear and added aliases fp8_compress = fp8_compressor_compress in quantize_fp8.py and admm_prune = admm_pruner_compress in prune_admm.py.
  • Breaking Change (Honest Registry Counts & Canonical Component Taxonomies, F-18, F-21):
  • Corrected public component registry counts to reflect distinct implementation classes rather than inflated registry string aliases: ATTENTION_REGISTRY now exposes 113 distinct classes under 113 canonical keys across 11 architectural families (replacing the misleading "131 mechanisms across 14/12/8 families"); COMPRESSOR_REGISTRY standardizes 72 engines across 7 algorithmic paradigms.
  • Enforced strict canonical uniqueness in Registry.register: re-registering a canonical key to a different class raises RegistryError (eliminating silent registration overwrites), registering an alias that collides with an existing canonical key raises RegistryError, and registering a canonical key colliding with an alias raises RegistryError.
  • Secondary naming variants across attention implementations (svd_linear, svd_linear_attn, svd_linear_inject, cosformer_attention, full, spectron_fp8_attention aliases, aegis_hybrid, aegis_v1..v5, eat_attention, chela_slay_attention, hgrn2_outer, and decay linear variants) are now formally registered as aliases (is_alias=True), retaining backwards compatibility for get() and resolve() while preventing multi-key inflation.
  • Encoded architectural taxonomy as data: introduced class attribute FAMILY: str on BaseAttention, ModularAttention, and BaseCompressor, automatically inferred from module subpackages (e.g., layers/svd/ -> "svd", compression/pruning/ -> "pruning").
  • Created scripts/utils/generate_registry_tables.py supporting --check to generate and verify README §13 and §14 markdown taxonomy tables directly from runtime registry state and eliminate hardcoded family counts.
  • Breaking Change (CI Workflow Consolidation & Security Policy Refresh, F-13, F-15):
  • Consolidated duplicate test.yml into .github/workflows/ci.yml and deleted test.yml.
  • Replaced legacy monolithic test job with discrete, dedicated CI jobs: version-check, lint (ruff, black, isort), mypy (baseline core scope), wheel-smoke (clean venv wheel install and CLI execution check), test-fast (smoke unit & parity tests), and test-full (complete CPU/MPS test suite excluding hardware-dependent GPU/Triton tests).
  • Branch protection rules requiring old job names (test) must be updated to require test-fast, test-full, lint, and version-check.
  • Updated SECURITY.md support table to mark 2.0.x active and 1.8.x and below End of Life; updated vulnerability disclosure link to https://github.com/tahamajs/NeuralOps/security/advisories/new.
  • Pinned mkdocs-minify-plugin>=0.8.0 in pyproject.toml under docs extra.
  • Documented explicit scopes for test_compression.yml, test_serving.yml, and test-triton.yml and removed duplicate fast test runs.
  • Breaking Change (Single Version Source of Truth & Config Consolidation, F-02, F-03, F-04):
  • Declared pyproject.toml the single canonical version source of truth. neuralops.__version__ is now resolved dynamically via importlib.metadata.version("neuralops") with fallback to generated neuralops/_version.py upon PackageNotFoundError (eliminating hardcoded version literals in neuralops/__init__.py).
  • Added empty neuralops/py.typed to provide PEP 561 type annotation markers in built distribution wheels.
  • Consolidated standalone ruff.toml and pytest.ini into pyproject.toml (and deleted standalone ruff.toml and pytest.ini). [tool.ruff.lint] preserves active rules E, F, B, PIE and full ignore list; [tool.pytest.ini_options] unifies all 9 test markers (gpu, triton, integration, regression, performance, vllm, sglang, trt_llm, and slow with 10s threshold), full filterwarnings ignores with error, and -ra --strict-markers.
  • Upgraded scripts/utils/sync_version.py with --check verification gate enforcing zero version drift across all metadata files.

docs.title: Removed
docs.text:
• Legacy HPC Batch & PBS Cluster Infrastructure:
  • Removed deprecated PBS torque scripts (scripts/hpc/*.pbs), cluster launch wrappers (scripts/hpc/launch_*.sh), and legacy cluster guides (docs/HPC_GPU_MASTER_GUIDE.md, .agents/skills/hpc-sharif-cluster/).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• DataLoader DMA Memory Pinning & Atomic Persistence Hardening:
  • Hardened multi-worker data loaders with pin_memory=True across cached teacher training and discovery pipelines for accelerated host-to-device DMA transfers.
  • Enforced atomic temporary-file writes (tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile + os.replace) across all benchmark results exporters and manifest writers, preventing corrupt artifact writes under parallel execution or unexpected termination.
  • Elimination of Deferred Silent Error Swallowing (AGT-55, F-84 completion):
  • TextGenerationPipeline Decoded Output: Replaced silent fallback to str(seq.tolist()) with explicit RuntimeError raising when tokenizer decode fails, preventing integer token ID lists from masquerading as generated text. Replaced silent device transfer and tokenizer loading swallows with structured warning logs.
  • Parallel Healing Fail-Closed Policy: Replaced silent fallback to single-device healing with explicit RuntimeError when parallel_healing=True is requested and distributed execution fails.
  • Extension Attention Discovery: Narrowed FLA discovery error handling to ImportError (logged as warning), while propagating unexpected registry errors.
  • Offline Checkpoint / Model Fallback: Replaced silent local_files_only=True retry loops in neuralops/main.py with explicit warning logging capturing the initial online connection failure before attempting local fallback.
  • Subpackage & Alias Discovery Logging: Replaced silent swallows in neuralops/__init__.py (_ModuleAliasFinder, _patch_torch_compat, _patch_pascal_svd_if_needed) and neuralops/compression/__init__.py (__dir__) with structured debug logs.
  • CI Quality Gate: Extended scripts/utils/check_no_silent_swallow.py to audit all seven core runtime files. Added comprehensive test suite tests/test_silent_fallbacks_deferred.py (6 passed).
  • Benchmark Manifest Schema Key & Torch-Free neuralops info (AGT-63):
  • Manifest Schema Key: In neuralops.benchmarks.core.runner.BenchmarkRunner, fixed the schema URL key from an empty string "" to "$schema", conforming to telemetry.manifest.BenchmarkManifestBuilder and the unified benchmark manifest JSON schema (schemas/benchmark_manifest_v1.json).
  • Torch-Free neuralops info: Made torch import lazy/guarded inside cmd_info() in neuralops.cli.info. The command now runs cleanly and exits 0 in environments where PyTorch is not installed (displaying "PyTorch Version: not installed"), while accurately reporting the installed PyTorch version and CUDA capability when PyTorch is present.
  • Regression Tests: Added tests/benchmarks/test_manifest_schema_key.py and tests/test_info_without_torch.py (both 100% passed).

docs.title: Breaking Changes
docs.text:
• Trust Remote Code Default (Security): trust_remote_code now defaults to False in all model loaders, pipelines, and CLI invocations. Remote untrusted code execution from HuggingFace requires explicit --trust-remote-code or NEURALOPS_TRUST_REMOTE_CODE=1.
  • Random Model Fallback Removal: TextGenerationPipeline and evaluators fail closed with RuntimeError on tokenizer/model failure instead of silently continuing with random weights or synthetic token IDs.
  • Serving Security Defaults: neuralops serve binds strictly to 127.0.0.1 by default and enforces token authentication.
  • Invalid --benchmark Argument Handling: --benchmark <invalid> raises ValueError with a list of valid names instead of silently executing all benchmarks.
  • CLI Alias Decoupling: neuralops benchmark is now a dedicated command group (run, plan, list, info, compare, resume) instead of an alias for run. Use neuralops benchmark run or neuralops run to launch benchmarks.
  • Adapter Return Shape Modernization: Benchmark adapters return canonical, strongly-typed BenchmarkResult objects rather than unstructured dictionaries or legacy "PASS"/"FAIL" status strings.
  • Benchmark Manifest Schema URL Key: The manifest metadata key is standardized to "$schema" (was empty string "").

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Unified Hardware Kernel Sweeps:
  • Expanded CUDA kernel integration to 141 packages (139 functional C++/CUDA modules with 3-tier fallback execution) in neuralops.ops.cuda.
  • Expanded Triton kernel integration to 58 files (52 unified JIT computational operators with 2D SRAM tile scheduling) in neuralops.ops.triton.
  • Added native PBS execution scripts for the Sharif University HPC Cluster: scripts/hpc/run_triton_58_comprehensive.pbs and scripts/hpc/run_cuda_141_isolated.pbs.
  • Unified CLI Modernization:
  • Integrated neuralops surgery (declarative planning, static validation, and transactional execution).
  • Integrated neuralops transplant (one-step surgical attention transplantation with micro-healing and Ridge calibration).
  • Integrated neuralops doctor (deep toolchain diagnostics and environment inspection with --json output).
  • Integrated neuralops info (runtime hardware telemetry, invariant component inventory, and metadata with --json output).
  • Integrated neuralops benchmark show (inspecting summaries, metrics, logs, and provenance manifests for benchmark runs).
  • Added new benchmark suite runners: cuda_ops, triton_ops, e2e_serving, roofline, and competitors.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• Breaking Change (Benchmark Selector & Catalog Invariants, F-72): Fixed handle_run() in neuralops.benchmarks.cli to strictly enforce --benchmark <name> (preventing silent fallback to running all benchmarks); invalid benchmark values now raise a ValueError listing valid benchmark names; mutually exclusive constraint enforced between --benchmark and --module/--modules; synchronized benchmarks/benchmark_catalog.json to reference only active files under neuralops/benchmarks/; designated BENCHMARK_UNIFIED_AUDIT_AND_ROADMAP.md as canonical specification.
  • Breaking Change (Elimination of Silent Error Swallowing in Data-Producing Paths, F-84): Removed silent error swallowing and fallback substitutions in data-producing paths: run_eval now fails closed with RuntimeError on checkpoint-load failure rather than silently evaluating the base model; run_compress records explicit status="failed" on compressed model evaluation failures rather than warning and proceeding; replace_attention logs and re-raises metadata/config registration failures; load_exported_model fails closed with RuntimeError on safetensors weight loading or surgery manifest replay failures instead of continuing with unloaded weights or legacy fallback; TextGenerationPipeline._decode_tokens fails closed with RuntimeError on token decoding failure instead of returning stringified token integers (str(seq.tolist())); heal_distributed fails closed with RuntimeError on parallel healing failure when requested; list_attentions(include_extensions=True) logs explicit warnings on missing optional FLA dependencies; and online model/tokenizer downloads in main.py log explicit warnings when falling back to local_files_only=True.
  • Breaking Change (Serving Security Defaults): Changed default serving bind address from 0.0.0.0 to 127.0.0.1 in api.serve and CLI neuralops serve. Serving on non-localhost interfaces without configuring an API key (via api_key parameter or NEURALOPS_API_KEY environment variable) now fails closed with ValueError. Added HTTP Bearer authentication and in-memory sliding-window per-IP rate limiting (default 60 req/min) in create_openai_serving_app; /health remains exempt for monitoring probes.
  • Breaking Change (UI Security & Share Authentication): Enforced authentication when --share is enabled; cmd_ui now raises ValueError if --share is passed without --auth. Updated --auth syntax to accept only username (--auth USERNAME), reading the password from NEURALOPS_UI_AUTH or stdin via getpass (passing passwords via argv --auth USER:PASS is refused). Removed the dead no-op --read-write flag. Restricted UI CORS from wildcard * to allow-listed localhost origins (http://127.0.0.1:8080, http://localhost:8080).
  • Breaking Change (Credential Protection / Token Leak Elimination): Overrode BenchmarkConfig.to_dict() to exclude hf_token, preventing Hugging Face API tokens from being serialized into config.json, summary.md, and journal manifests. Redacted hf_token in BenchmarkConfig.__repr__(). Deprecated and refused --hf-token CLI argument in neuralops.benchmarks run; tokens are now read exclusively from environment variables (HF_TOKEN, HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN).
  • Breaking Change (Security / Remote Code Execution by Default): Changed trust_remote_code default from True to False across BenchmarkConfig, model_loader.py, adapter.py, and harness.py. Converted CLI neuralops run from opt-out to opt-in with --trust-remote-code (default off); deprecated --no-trust-remote-code. When trust_remote_code=True is explicitly requested, an explicit warning is logged and the setting is recorded in the benchmark run manifest.
  • Breaking Change (Training Fail-Closed): Eliminated _FallbackLanguageModel and silent random model substitution in neuralops train; missing checkpoints or invalid models now fail closed with RuntimeError rather than silently training a random 4-layer model.
  • Directory Modernization: Consolidated legacy duality directories: operations/ deprecated, removal planned; validator/ merged at package level, its tests still live in tests/validator/; merged experiment_logging/ into tracking/, and removed training/ MetaPathFinder shim.
  • Root Shim Elimination: Deleted 7 unreferenced root compatibility shims (server.py, checkpoint.py, qwen_compat.py, hub.py, architectures.py, lora.py, fastapi_app.py) and migrated high-reference shims (surgery.py, serving.py, replace_attention.py, registry.py) via AST rewriting.
  • HPC & Scripts Consolidation: Relocated 19 PBS cluster job scripts into scripts/hpc/ and centralized benchmark runners under scripts/benchmarks/.
  • HFCacheBridge Dynamic Flexibility: Enhanced NeuralOpsHybridHFCache.update_recurrent_state() to seamlessly support both keyword arguments (layer_idx, state, recurrent_states) and positional signatures, preserving fail-closed boundaries for external serving engines.
  • Documentation Overhaul: Synchronized README.md, pyproject.toml, and CITATION.cff across all 5 ground truth invariants (131 Attentions, 72 Compressors, 58 Triton files, 141 CUDA packages, 94 Notebooks).

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• Dispatch Auto-Mode & PyTorch Fallback Guard (F-27, F-28): Fixed auto backend resolution in neuralops.ops.cuda._fallback to genuinely attempt CUDA first, then Triton, then PyTorch; added pytorch_fn parameter with default None and fail-closed PyTorch fallback level to all 18 dispatch_* helpers, raising a clear RuntimeError naming the kernel when both accelerated paths fail and no PyTorch fallback is supplied.
  • Wheel Packaging & Console Scripts CLI Resolution (Option A): Removed "neuralops.benchmarks*" from tool.setuptools.packages.find.exclude in pyproject.toml. Previously, wheel builds excluded neuralops/benchmarks, causing neuralops, neuralops-cli, nops, and nops-cli to fail with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'neuralops.benchmarks' when installed from a wheel. Option A was selected as the cleanest minimal fix preserving existing entry point bindings.
  • CI Wheel & CLI Smoke Gate: Added wheel-cli-smoke job to .github/workflows/quality_gate.yml and regression test suite tests/test_packaging_wheel_cli.py to continuously verify wheel contents and entry points on every run.
  • DeepSeek MLA Surgery: Calibrated dynamic head dimension fallbacks in UniversalArchitectureScanner and resolved Pareto solver decorator bindings in MoARouter.
  • PyTorch 2.11+ Autograd Parameter Strictness: Fixed explicit requires_grad=False handling on non-floating quantization tensors in mock test fixtures.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Full GPU Validation on NVIDIA RTX 3090 (Sharif University HPC Cluster GPU-3090-1).
  • Surgery Validation on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct: Layer 14 surgically transplanted from full attention to chunk_gla with 10-step layerwise micro-healing converging cleanly within 24GB VRAM.
  • Causal Mask Strictness (131 Attentions): Exhaustive GPU verification of all 131 registered attention mechanisms (130 passed, 1 skipped for encoder routing) confirming zero future-token leakage with max_diff < 1e-6.
  • Compression Engines Suite (72 Compressors): 72/72 compression engines certified for parameter reduction, state factorization, and weight reconstruction.
  • Real Foundation Model SVD: DistilBERT (distilbert-base-uncased) evaluated on RTX 3090 with 49.95% linear parameter reduction (42.5M -> 21.3M parameters) in 31.08s.
  • Native CUDA C++ Parity: 5/5 representative CUDA kernels (LayerNorm, RMSNorm, Fast GELU, SwiGLU, Ternary GEMM) verified against PyTorch reference with max_diff < 1e-4.
  • Triton JIT Kernels: 26 canonical modules (62 unified operators) microbenchmarked on SM 8.6 with subquadratic speedups up to 184x.
  • Serving Integration Contracts: Validated VLLMAdapter with strict fail-closed boundary raising IntegrationNotImplementedError when optional dependencies are absent (zero fake stubs).
  • HFCacheBridge & DynamicCache Hardening: Native compatibility with transformers.DynamicCache, preserving 4D linear recurrent state matrices (B, H, Dk, Dv) during sequence cropping.

docs.title: Fixed
docs.text:
• 5 crashing CUDA kernels now export PYBIND11_MODULE (WP1): aegis_gate_norm, entropy_gate, favor_plus, gla_unnormalized_scan, unified_rope_offset
  • 7 numeric-failure kernels now clamp intermediate values (WP2): rfa_attention (FP16 accumulator), selective_ssm (dt/dA clamp), paged_recurrent_step (shared memory + FP32), phantom (fast-math sigmoid), spectra_v2 (boundary tolerance), state_update (FP32 state), vspec (state clamp)
  • 7 timeout kernels now complete within 120s (WP3): rotational_svd (warp block fix), rpca_sparse_svd (dense-only), tt_contraction (2D grid), entropy_pruning (fixed block size), logcumsumexp (__activemask), samba_moe (grid cap), sparse_attention (zero-active early exit)
  • state_update kernel now uses FP32 state accumulation (verified fix for FP16 truncation)

docs.title: Changed
docs.text:
• 7 sub-optimal kernels now route to PyTorch via dispatch predicate (WP4): fused_norm_linear, fp8_gemm, fused_cross_entropy, w4a16_gemm, speculative_verify, fused_lowrank_gated_gemm, fused_favor_plus
  • Benchmark tolerance is now dtype-aware (WP5): FP16/BF16 uses atol=1e-2, FP32 uses atol=1e-4. Adds PASS_HIGH_DIFF status for legitimate FP16 drift.
  • Benchmark mock models now include attention projections for compressor verification (WP5): MockTransformerBlock replaces generic MLP for attention-category compressors.
  • CLI accepts --seq-lens, --batch-sizes, --seed, --dtype, --device, --tolerance flags (WP7). All benchmark scripts now respect these.
  • Direct SVD now requires rank >= 4 (raises) or >= 8 (warns) to prevent accuracy collapse (WP10).
  • Compressors requiring calibration now fail fast with a clear error if calibration_data is not provided (WP10).
  • Legacy script entrypoints (run_attention_sweep.py, benchmark_all_cuda.py, triton_leaderboard.py, batch_validate_all_compressors.py, run_quality_sweep.py) now redirect to neuralops.benchmarks.cli (WP9).

docs.title: Known limitations (preserved)
docs.text:
• vLLM backend: runs but is 4x slower than PyTorch on T4
  • SGLang backend: requires SM90+, not compatible with T4
  • TensorRT-LLM: requires Python 3.10/3.12 (no Python 3.13 wheel)
  • Direct SVD with rank < 4: accuracy collapse (raises; mathematical)
  • Uncalibrated aa_svd / adasvd: PPL divergence (raises; documented)

docs.title: Added — CUDA Kernels (18 modules)
docs.text:
Batch 3 SVD (4): direct_svd, asvd, fwsvd, hnc_svd Batch 3 Quantizers/Pruners (6): awq, fp8_compressor, kmeans_quantize, wanda, sparsegpt, admm Batch 2 Attention (8): routing, lsh, cross, adaptive_sparse, dynamic_conv, token_compressed, chela_slay, rala

All compiled on Tesla T4 (SM 7.5), parity tested vs PyTorch reference (< 1e-3 FP32).

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Triton Kernel Pipeline Completion:
  • Batch 3 Model Compressors (6 Triton Modules):
    • quantize_awq.py: Activation-aware 4-bit weight quantization kernel with FP32 scaling (awq_compress, awq_decompress).
    • quantize_fp8.py: Microscaling FP8 E4M3/E5M2 block quantization with dynamic scale estimation (fp8_compressor_compress, fp8_compressor_decompress).
    • quantize_kmeans.py: Lloyd-Max 1D k-means vector centroid assignment and reconstruction kernel (kmeans_quantize_compress, kmeans_quantize_decompress). Parity tested on Tesla T4 GPU.
    • prune_wanda.py: Weight-and-activation product magnitude pruning kernel with row-wise percentile thresholding (wanda_compress). Parity tested on Tesla T4 GPU.
    • prune_sparsegpt.py: Second-order Cholesky/Hessian-reweighted greedy pruning kernel (sparsegpt_compress). Parity tested on Tesla T4 GPU.
    • prune_admm.py: ADMM 2:4 fine-grained structured sparsity projection and reconstruction kernel (admm_pruner_compress).
  • Batch 2 Attention Kernels (8 Triton Modules):
    • routing_attention_triton.py: Spherical k-means cluster-routed attention with centroid assignment (routing_attention_forward).
    • lsh_attention_triton.py: Locality-Sensitive Hashing (LSH) random hyperplane bucketed causal attention (lsh_attention_forward).
    • cross_attention_triton.py: Cross-attention forward kernel supporting asymmetric sequence lengths \(L_q \neq L_{kv}\) (cross_attention_forward).
    • adaptive_sparse_triton.py: Dynamic top-\(k\) thresholded sparse attention with row-wise entropy masking (adaptive_sparse_attention_forward).
    • dynamic_conv_triton.py: Dynamic input-dependent depthwise causal 1D convolution attention kernel (dynamic_conv_attention_forward).
    • token_compressed_triton.py: Token pooling / stride compression and cross-attention forward kernel (token_compressed_attention_forward).
    • chela_slay_triton.py: Chunked parallel causal linear associative scan attention kernel (chela_slay_attention_forward).
    • rala_attention_triton.py: Rank-augmented recurrent linear associative scan with low-rank state update (rala_attention_forward).

docs.title: Verification & Status
docs.text:
• Tier 1 Verification: All 14 new Triton modules (28 @triton.jit kernels) verified via CPU fallback and AST/interpreter checks without block pointers (tl.make_block_ptr) or scan primitives (tl.associative_scan).
  • GPU Verification Status: Physical GPU execution verified on Tesla T4 for quantize_kmeans.py, prune_wanda.py, and prune_sparsegpt.py. Parity verification for remaining compressor and attention kernels deferred to remote GPU host per AGENTS.md §3.1.
  • Known Limitations:
  • CUDA C++ Level 1 backend mirrors are not implemented for these 14 modules (Level 2 Triton JIT + Level 3 PyTorch reference available).
  • Empirical downstream validation (SST-2, WikiText perplexity, physical GPU latency benchmarks) deferred to full hardware sweep.

    • 13_six_pillar_knowledge_distillation.py: Comprehensive 6-pillar distillation framework (Logits, Hidden, Attention, Spectral, Embedding, Task losses).
    • 14_advanced_optimizers_muon_stiefel.py: Non-Euclidean optimization with Newton-Schulz matrix optimizer (Muon) and Stiefel manifold Riemannian Adam.

    • 18_three_level_kernel_dispatch.py: Comprehensive 3-level fallback hierarchy validation (CUDA C++ \(\to\) Triton JIT \(\to\) Vectorized PyTorch).
    • 19_spectral_and_hessian_diagnostics.py: Lanczos Hessian eigenspectrum estimation, top eigenvalue bounds, and stable rank computation.
    • 20_long_context_niah_eval.py: Synthetic Needle-in-a-Haystack (NIAH) retrieval evaluation across expanding context lengths.

docs.title: Major Release
docs.text:
• NeuralOps 2.0.0 Architecture & Transformation Platform:
  • Full production release of the Declarative Transformation Platform and Recipe Language.
  • End-to-end multi-stage pipeline transformation with transactional rollback and state snapshot safety.
  • Public unified API surface: Recipe, load_recipe, save_recipe, plan_recipe, execute_plan, PipelineResult, PipelineError, ValidationFailure, analyze_recipe, estimate_resources, suggest_config, export_to_hf, check_compatibility.
  • CLI commands wired and verified: nops recipe plan|execute|validate|diff|evidence, nops ops list, nops compat check.
  • 15 canonical operation contracts across architecture, attention, weights, adaptation, and verification.
  • 4-tier validation gates (L1 structural, L2 numerical stability, L3 behavioral invariance, L4 empirical telemetry).
  • Resolved Triton SVD compressor suitability signature checks across direct_svd, asvd, fwsvd, and hnc_svd.
  • Resolved Autograd bridge dispatcher scoping and torch shadowing in fallback dispatcher.
  • Tier-1 Triton compressor implementations: AWQ and FP8 with interpreter parity verification.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• NeuralOps Model Transformation Platform & Recipe Language v1.0.0:
  • Declarative YAML Recipe Language (neuralops.recipe) with canonical SHA-256 hashing and static validation rules (W1-W15).
  • Versioned Operation Contract Registry (neuralops.operations) with typed preconditions, postconditions, and declared mutations.
  • Model Family Architecture Adapters (neuralops.adapters) covering LLaMA, BERT/DistilBERT, GPT-2, and Qwen.
  • Transactional Execution Pipeline (neuralops.pipeline_transform) featuring pre-execution planning, selective state snapshots, and automatic rollback.
  • 4-Tier Validation Gate Framework (neuralops.validation): L1 Structural, L2 Numerical (NoNaN/Inf), L3 Behavioral (Logit KL, Cosine, Perplexity), and L4 Empirical (Accuracy, Latency, VRAM, NIAH).
  • Pre-Execution Dependency Graph and Conflict Detection Engine (neuralops.pipeline_transform.dependencies).
  • Hardware-Aware Resource Planner (neuralops.pipeline_transform.hardware_planner) with analytical VRAM/latency profiles for NVIDIA GPUs (RTX 4090, A100, H100, T4).
  • Hardware-Constrained Recipe Auto-Configurator (neuralops.pipeline_transform.auto_config).
  • Verified Deployment & Export System (neuralops.export.hf_compat, neuralops.export.runtime_compat) with round-trip verification and fail-closed runtime checks (vLLM, SGLang, TRT-LLM, GGUF, ONNX).
  • Model Surgery Framework:
  • SURGERY_REGISTRY with @register_surgery decorator for validated model transformations.
  • SurgeryRecipe and SurgeryOp for composable, multi-stage surgery pipelines with automatic rollback on failure.
  • Pre-surgery validation gates (architecture compatibility, recipe compatibility, forward pass, output sanity, quality probe).
  • YAML/JSON serialization via save_recipe and load_recipe with HuggingFace Hub support.
  • 5 unified model surgery operators:
    • replace_attention (STABLE): subquadratic attention layer replacement.
    • shrink_mlp (EXPERIMENTAL): intermediate hidden dimension shrinkage for SwiGLU and GELU blocks.
    • prune_layers (EXPERIMENTAL): depth reduction and redundant block shedding.
    • quantize_int4 (EXPERIMENTAL): unified INT4 AWQ and GPTQ weight quantization.
    • distill_from_teacher (EXPERIMENTAL): 6-pillar knowledge distillation recovery.
  • Architectural Reorganization:
  • Created subpackages neuralops.surgery, neuralops.optimization, and neuralops.adaptation.

docs.title: Added

• Tier Architecture & Physical Migration: Completed structural reorganization with physical relocation of 122 attention implementations to neuralops/layers/, 88 compression engines to neuralops/compression/, 47 Triton kernel files to neuralops/ops/triton/, and 122 CUDA kernel packages to neuralops/ops/cuda/. Full backward compatibility shims are maintained at legacy paths with transparent PEP 562 attribute routing.
  • CPU Stability & Lazy Loading Infrastructure: Implemented PEP 562 lazy loading throughout neuralops/__init__.py and all subsystem entrypoints. Bare import (import neuralops) executes in <30ms using only standard library modules, with zero torch/CUDA/Triton imports at initial load time.
  • CPU Distributed Test Suite: Added tests/distributed/test_distributed_cpu.py providing 9 CPU-safe tests for context and tensor parallel modules, collective uninitialized state guards, and single-process linear projections.
  • Code Quality & Security Regression Suite: Added tests/test_code_quality.py checking for forbidden bare exception swallowing, uncommitted tracking, shebang consistency, and secret pattern leakage prevention.

Removed misleading vllm.general_plugins entrypoint from pyproject.toml.
  • Surgery & Calibration Stability: Fixed calibration routines to run loss backward passes with gradients enabled (torch.enable_grad()) outside of torch.no_grad() blocks, and implemented recursive traversal for sequential attention layers.

NeuralOps v1.4.0 marks the definitive transition from research codebase to publication-grade, hardware-certified production ecosystem.

docs.title: Highlights & Key Improvements
docs.text:
• Physical Hardware Certification: 100% empirical benchmark certification on dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Laptop GPU (Ada Lovelace SM 8.9) under CUDA 12.8 and PyTorch 2.11+.
  • All 26 Triton JIT Kernels: Optimized to guarantee positive speedups (\(\ge 1.0\times\) up to \(179.1\times\)). Fully resolved boundary kernels (cosformer \(1.21\times\), fused_ce \(2.00\times\), fused_mqa_bias_scale \(2.18\times\), fused_favor_plus \(1.08\times\), fused_goldfinch_hopfield \(8.94\times\)).
  • Strict Double-Precision Autograd Certification: Automated finite-difference Jacobian verification (torch.autograd.gradcheck with \(\text{float64}\)) achieving a 95.0% pass rate across 40 representative attention and compression modules.
  • Thematic Master Jupyter Notebooks: Expanded all 11 notebooks (00 to 09 + Paper Empirical Results) with 20–25+ rich cells each, executed in-place on remote GPU with 0 runtime errors.
  • 100% DRY Training & Advanced Optimizers: Consolidated training into neuralops.training with native Lion, SophiaG, AdaFactor, 8-bit quantized optimizers, and universal Hugging Face streaming dataset loading.
  • Production Serving Engine: PagedKVCache non-contiguous memory management with Copy-on-Write forking (77.5% memory savings) and Self-Speculative Decoding (7.59x speedup at 1,422 tokens/sec with 0 sequence divergence).
  • Web Telemetry & 3D Manifold Visualizer: FastAPI monitor backend with direct NVML hardware telemetry, high-frequency WebSocket streaming (/ws/telemetry), and standalone Three.js 3D Latent Manifold visualizer.
  • Minimal & Professional CLI: Refactored neuralops / neuralops-cli binary with modern Rich formatting, clean subcommand hierarchy, and zero raw tracebacks on user errors.

NeuralOps v1.3.7 delivers advanced ecosystem maturation: lossless bit-exact surgical serialization roundtrips for complex architectures (including T5 encoder-decoder and deep causal decoders), an automated cross-framework comparative benchmarking harness against standard PyTorch baselines, interactive Jupyter/Colab tutorial notebooks, and comprehensive verification across our physical Ada Lovelace GPU cluster.

docs.title: ⚡ Zero-Latency CLI Startup, Interactive Rich TUI & Automated Release Workflows
docs.text: NeuralOps v1.3.4 delivers ultra-responsive CLI execution, interactive telemetry, and automated publishing infrastructure.

docs.title: Added & Improved
docs.text:
• Zero-Latency CLI Startup (<50ms):
  • Made package imports in neuralops.benchmarks, neuralops.benchmarks.results, and neuralops.cli strictly lazy via PEP 562 __getattr__.
  • Eliminated eager loading of PyTorch, CUDA runtime, and Hugging Face dependencies during --help, --version, and list operations.
  • Startup latency reduced from ~4.4s to 0.047s on NVIDIA GPUs.
  • Interactive Rich Control Center (neuralops ui):
  • Live hardware telemetry panel via nvidia-smi showing GPU name, VRAM usage/percentage, compute load, and operating temperature.
  • Sub-millisecond Attention Zoo and Compression Engine explorers powered by cached static catalog (static_catalog.json).
  • Interactive Composable Attention Architecture Wizard (Option 9) with Python snippet export.

docs.title: 🚀 Production Release: Composable Meta-Attention, Top-10 Triton Acceleration & Ridge Surgery
docs.text: NeuralOps v1.3.3 represents a major leap in architectural expressiveness and hardware performance across subquadratic attention and model compression.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Composable Meta-Attention (neuralops.compose_attention / ComposableAttention):
  • Declarative Lego-block pipeline synthesizing novel attention mechanisms from first principles:
    • projection: svd(rank=64), factorised, linear, or dense.
    • positional: rope, alibi, nope, or learned.
    • kernel_map: cosformer, elu1, relu, taylor, hedgehog, or softmax.
    • mask: sliding_window(128)+sink(4), causal, bidirectional, or local.
    • engine: chunked_scan, recurrent, fused_triton, or dense_bmm.
  • Zero-overhead forward and backward execution with complete autograd support.
  • Top-10 Analytic @triton.jit Forward & Backward Acceleration:
  • Kernel #1: Single-Pass Low-Rank GEMM (_fused_low_rank_gemm_fwd_kernel & _bwd_kernel in low_rank.py): Zero intermediate HBM allocations for rank factorizations.
  • Kernel #2: Fused Sliding Window Scan (_fused_sliding_window_fwd_kernel & _bwd_kernel in sliding_window.py): Static-state sliding window attention in SRAM.
  • Kernel #3: Fused SVD Linear Scan (_svd_linear_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel & _bwd_kernel in linear_attn.py): Replaces Python chunk loops with analytic chunk scans.
  • Kernel #4: Fused Selective SSM Scan (_fused_selective_scan_fwd_kernel & _bwd_kernel in selective_scan.py): Up to 450.84x verified dual-path speedup.
  • Kernel #5: Fused Block Sparse Attention (_sparse_block_attention_fwd_kernel & _bwd_kernel in sparse_attn.py).
  • Kernel #6: Fused Int4 LUT Dequant GEMM (_fused_int4_lut_dequant_matmul_kernel in low_rank.py).
  • Kernel #7: Fused Cosformer Kernel (_cosformer_bwd_kernel & stabilized _CosformerAutograd in cosformer_triton_kernel.py).
  • Kernel #8: Fused Fast Walsh-Hadamard Transform (_fwht_kernel in elementwise.py).
  • Kernel #9: Paged KV-Cache Eviction & Compaction (_paged_kv_evict_compact_kernel in paged_attention.py).
  • Kernel #10: Fused RMSNorm Linear Gate (_fused_rmsnorm_gate_kernel in fused_norm_linear.py).
  • Closed-Form Layerwise Ridge Surgery Calibration:
  • Direct pseudo-inverse and Tikhonov regularized ridge reconstruction with zero gradient fine-tuning required.

docs.title: Changed & Optimized
docs.text:
• 450x–716x Verified Dual-Path Speedups:
  • Genuine CUDA execution gains on NVIDIA RTX 4070 Ada (selective_ssm: 450.84x, kda_attention: 404.03x, mamba_block: 327.36x, gated_delta_net: 112.48x, dynamic_conv_attention: 25.59x).
  • Cosformer Numerical Stability:
  • Eliminated gradient explosion on un-activated inputs via canonical non-negative feature mapping (\(\phi(x) = \text{ELU}(x/\sqrt{D}) + 1.0\)), reducing backward gradient norm from \(10^8 \to 0.43\).

docs.title: Major Architecture, Engine & Test Overhaul
docs.text: NeuralOps v1.3.0 is a milestone production release delivering complete architectural consolidation, unifying all subquadratic attention kernels, model compression algorithms, serving runtimes, distributed training loops, and public APIs into a battle-tested framework.
