docs.title: Reporting a Vulnerability
docs.text:
We take the security of NeuralOps, its compiled kernel execution pipeline, and serving infrastructure seriously. If you discover a security vulnerability, memory corruption flaw in CUDA/Triton kernels, or model deserialization exploit, please report it responsibly:

  1. Do not create a public GitHub Issue for undisclosed security vulnerabilities.
  2. Report the vulnerability privately via GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting.
  3. Or email the core maintainer directly at: tahamaj4@gmail.com with the subject line: [SECURITY] NeuralOps Vulnerability Report.

Please include in your report: - Component affected (e.g., neuralops.ops.cuda, neuralops.integrations.vllm, Triton kernel memory offset). - Minimal reproducible proof-of-concept (PoC) script. - Operating system, PyTorch version, and CUDA / Triton driver versions. - Potential impact (arbitrary code execution, host denial of service, memory out-of-bounds read/write).

We aim to acknowledge reports within 48 hours and provide patches within 14 days.

docs.title: Security Architecture & Operational Invariants
docs.text: NeuralOps implements strict safeguards across execution environments, remote model hubs, kernel compilers, and telemetry services.

docs.title: 1. Secret Hygiene & Zero Credential Leaks
docs.text:
• Zero Plaintext Tokens: API keys and credentials (such as Hugging Face tokens) must never be passed via command-line arguments or checked into repository manifests. Command-line flags accepting plaintext tokens are rejected.
  • Environment Resolution: Hub integrations source authentication strictly via the HF_TOKEN (or HUGGING_FACE_HUB_TOKEN) environment variable.
  • Automated Scrubbing: All log handlers, diagnostic dumps, and model upload summaries automatically redact secrets matching hf_[A-Za-z0-9]{20,} or matching the contents of HF_TOKEN with [REDACTED_HF_TOKEN].
  • Fail Closed on Missing Auth: Hub upload daemons refuse unauthenticated operations without leaking credential state to terminal outputs or shared ledgers.

docs.title: 2. Fail-Closed Execution Contracts
docs.text:
• Explicit CUDA Request: When --device cuda or a CUDA backend is requested, the system verifies torch.cuda.is_available(). If CUDA is missing, execution terminates immediately with a RuntimeError—silent fallback to CPU or simulated metrics is strictly forbidden.
  • Zero Generic SVD Fallback: Each compressor in the 82-compressor zoo must execute its authentic algorithm. If a named compressor fails or encounters numerical instability, it raises a terminal error; substituting generic SVD, truncated zero tensors, or identity matrices under that compressor's label is prohibited.
  • Strict Numerical Parity Gates: Any kernel producing non-finite tensors (NaN, Inf) or exceeding error thresholds (max_diff > tolerance) is designated FAIL_NUMERICS. Catching exceptions in data-producing paths with except Exception: pass is prohibited.
  • Zero Fake Artifacts: Never write synthetic metrics, unverified throughput numbers, or placeholder binary files when real evaluation fails.

docs.title: 3. Remote Code Execution Policy (trust_remote_code)
docs.text:
• Strict Default False: Across all model loaders (neuralops.benchmarks.core.model_loader, neuralops.models, neuralops.evaluation), trust_remote_code defaults to False.
  • Explicit Opt-In Required: Executing custom model code from remote repositories requires explicit user consent via --trust-remote-code or programmatic trust_remote_code=True.
  • Audit Logging: Every load operation that enables trust_remote_code logs an explicit audit warning detailing the target repository identifier.
  • Weights-Only Deserialization: Serialized checkpoints enforce weights_only=True via torch.load and prefer native SafeTensors (safetensors) to block arbitrary pickle deserialization exploits.

docs.title: 4. Telemetry & Monitoring Localhost Binding
docs.text:
• Hermetic Localhost Binding: Live GPU telemetry servers, WebSocket monitors, dashboard runners (run_monitor_server.py, neuralops.runners.monitor), and UI preview services default to binding to 127.0.0.1 (localhost).
  • No Unintended Network Exposure: Public interface exposure (0.0.0.0) requires explicit operator configuration; services never expose live metrics, system traces, or execution controls to external networks by default.
  • CORS & Input Validation: Web telemetry endpoints enforce strict localhost CORS origins (127.0.0.1:8080, localhost:8080) and sanitize query parameters against SQL injection via parameterized statements.

docs.title: Attentions API Reference
docs.text:

[!NOTE] - 115 Physical Classes: Distinct torch.nn.Module classes physically compiled with verified 3-level fallback implementations. - 116 Active Registry Keys: 115 unique physical modules + 1 canonical direct alias (svd_attention -> SVDLinearAttention). - Extensible Catalog (116–131): Extended architectural registry slots (e.g., chunk_gla_attention, multi_scale_retention, rwkv6_linear_attention, randomized_svd_attention, fused_recurrent_attention) available for future synthetic scaling and hybrid research experiments. For the complete per-class complexity, dispatch backend, and operator tables, refer to ATTENTION_TAXONOMY_CATALOG.md. All benchmark results, execution logs, and LaTeX tables are publicly mirrored at: 👉 https://huggingface.co/datasets/Hooshaai/neuralops-results

docs.title: 2.1 Exact Softmax & IO-Aware Dense Attention (6 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: full, full_attention, mqa, gqa_attention, flash_attention3, flash_attention3_fp8
  • Mathematical Operator: $\(\text{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\left(\frac{Q K^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}} + M\right) V\)$
  • Hardware Profile: High arithmetic intensity, but bounded by quadratic \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) memory bandwidth and KV-cache footprint during autoregressive decoding.

docs.title: 2.2 Kernelized & Feature-Map Linear Attentions (15 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: cosformer, cosformer_attention, performer_attention, positive_kernel_linear_attention, galerkin_attention, regla_attention, halo_regla, eat, eat_attention, chela_slay, chela_slay_attention, triton_cosformer, rpc_attention, zeros_attention, xattention
  • Mathematical Operator: $\(O_i = \frac{\sum_{j=1}^i \phi(Q_i) \phi(K_j)^\top V_j}{\sum_{j=1}^i \phi(Q_i) \phi(K_j)^\top}\)$ Using the associative property: \(\sum_{j} (\phi(Q_i) \phi(K_j)^\top) V_j = \phi(Q_i) \left( \sum_{j} \phi(K_j)^\top V_j \right)\), reducing complexity to \(\mathcal{O}(L \cdot D^2)\) with \(\mathcal{O}(D^2)\) constant state memory.

docs.title: 2.3 Gated Linear Recurrences (11 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: gated_linear_attention (GLA), gated_linear_attn, gla_attention, decay_linear_attention, decay_linear_attn, factorised_matrix_state, hgrn2_gated_layer, hgrn2_gated_outer, hgrn2_outer, goldfinch_ahn, salt_attention
  • Mathematical Operator: $\(S_t = \alpha_t \odot S_{t-1} + K_t^\top V_t, \quad O_t = Q_t S_t\)$ where \(\alpha_t = \exp(-\text{softplus}(\beta_t))\) provides data-dependent forgetting, computed via parallel chunk-wise associative scans in Triton.

docs.title: 2.4 Delta-Rule Recurrences & Associative Memory (7 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: gated_delta_net, gated_deltanet_block, hgrn2_gated_deltanet, kda_attention (Kronecker Delta Attention), hla_attention, nexus, phantom
  • Mathematical Operator: $\(S_t = S_{t-1} + \beta_t (V_t - S_{t-1} K_t) K_t^\top\)$ Updates hidden memory via the error-driven Delta rule, preventing capacity saturation in associative recall tasks.

docs.title: 2.5 Continuous-Time & Selective State-Space Models (SSMs) (6 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: selective_ssm, simple_ssm, mamba_block (S6), upi_stuffed_mamba, mamba_svd_flash, svd_mamba
  • Mathematical Operator: $\(h_t = \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t x_t, \quad y_t = C_t h_t + D x_t\)$ where input-dependent discretization \(\Delta_t = \text{softplus}(\text{Linear}(x_t))\) allows selective filtering across continuous sequence trajectories.

docs.title: 2.6 Block-Sparse, Dilated & Sliding-Window Attentions (13 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: adaptive_span_attention, adaptive_sparse_attention, adasplash_attention, cluster_attention, block_transformer_hiba, nsa_attention, lsh_attention, routing_attention, sink_attention, dynamic_conv_attention, hamming_attention, moba_attention, progressive_token_pruning
  • Characteristics: Enforces band-limited or block-diagonal attention masks, bounding token interactions to local context windows \(W\) with \(\mathcal{O}(L \cdot W \cdot D)\) time complexity.

docs.title: 2.7 SVD Spectral & Low-Rank Decomposed Attentions (19 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: linformer_attention, nystrom_attention, asvd_attention, svd_linear, svd_linear_attention, svd_linear_attn, svd_linear_decay, svd_linear_inject, svd_llm_v2_attention, adaptive_svd_attention, residual_svd_attention, svd_projection_attention, svd_seq, svd_compressed, naive_svd, minimal_svd, spectraformer_attention, fused_svd_kernel, triton_svd_linear_attention
  • Mathematical Operator: $\(W \approx U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top \implies Q = X W_q \approx (X U_r) (\Sigma_r V_r^\top)\)$ Projects sequence representations through an optimal Eckart-Young-Mirsky rank-\(r\) bottleneck, reducing parameter counts and FLOPs.

docs.title: 2.8 Multi-Head Latent & Key-Value Compressed Attentions (9 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: mla_attention (DeepSeek Multi-Head Latent Attention), qcqa_attention, compressed_attention, compressed_mha_attention, token_compressed_attention, projection_factorized_attn, lola_attention, padre_attention, lora_attention
  • Characteristics: Compresses Key-Value representations into low-dimensional latent vectors \(c^{KV}_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d_c}\) (\(d_c \ll H \cdot d_h\)), reducing inference KV-cache memory consumption by up to \(6\times\).

docs.title: 2.9 Hybrid Linear-Recurrent & Attention-SSM Architectures (14 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: jamba, jamba_info, samba_m3, griffin_ssd, hymba_transx, granite_hybrid, hybrid_attention, native_hybrid_attention, optimized_hybrid_attention, split_head_hybrid, tri_branch_hybrid, hybrid_local_kernel, aegis_hybrid, minimal_nova
  • Characteristics: Seamlessly interleaves Transformer attention layers and recurrent/SSM blocks to combine exact syntactic precision with linear long-context throughput.

docs.title: 2.10 Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) & Sparsely-Gated Attentions (6 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: bam_umoe, expert_choice_moe, reap_moe, samba_moe, moe_deltakv_paged, mixattention_moska
  • Characteristics: Dynamically routes tokens across sparse sets of specialized attention heads or expert projections using warp-synchronous gating kernels.

docs.title: 2.11 Test-Time Training (TTT) & Fast-Weight Systems (2 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: ttt_linear_attention, template_attention
  • Characteristics: Treats hidden state updates as an inner-loop online self-supervised gradient step, continually adjusting weights during forward inference.

docs.title: 2.12 Memory-Augmented & External Latent Recurrences (4 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: landmark_local_attention, refined_landmark_attention, rala_attention, nasc_attention
  • Characteristics: Maintains persistent external memory slots and landmark tokens to route context across arbitrarily long sequences.

docs.title: 2.13 Modern Positional, Rotary & Geometric Attention Variants (5 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: alibi, unified_rope, wgqa_attention, cross_attention, primal_attention
  • Characteristics: Injects geometric and relative distance inductive biases into key-query inner products via linear slope penalties (ALiBi) or complex rotation angles (RoPE).

docs.title: 2.14 Hardware-Fused, Low-Precision & Spectral-Transform Attentions (14 Modules)
docs.text:
• Module IDs: spectron, spectron_fp8, aegis_spectron_fp8, aegis_v1, aegis_v2, aegis_v3, aegis_v4, aegis_v5, aegis_v6, soa_attn, fusion_attn, orion, vig_attention, vspec
  • Characteristics: Fused Fast Walsh-Hadamard Transforms (FWHT), FP8 Tensor Core quantization, and fused SRAM execution eliminating DRAM roundtrips.

docs.title: neuralops.create_attention
docs.text:
def create_attention(
    name: str,
    config: Any = None,
    dim: int | None = None,
    num_heads: int | None = None,
    embed_dim: int | None = None,
    rank: int | None = None,
    **kwargs: Any,
) -> nn.Module

Universal factory constructing any registered attention mechanism from ATTENTION_REGISTRY. Normalizes hyperparameter aliases (embed_dim, dim, d_model, num_heads, heads, rank) automatically.

Parameters: - name (str): Canonical attention mechanism identifier. - config (Any, optional): Optional architectural configuration dataclass. - embed_dim / dim (int, optional): Hidden embedding dimension (e.g., 768, 2048, 4096). - num_heads (int, optional): Number of attention heads (e.g., 12, 16, 32). - rank (int, optional): Low-rank bottleneck dimension for SVD-based variants. - **kwargs: Mechanism-specific hyperparameters forwarded to the constructor.

Example: 

import torch
import neuralops

attn = neuralops.create_attention(
    "gated_delta_net",
    embed_dim=768,
    num_heads=12,
)

x = torch.randn(2, 64, 768)
out = attn(x)
print("Output shape:", out.shape)  # torch.Size([2, 64, 768])

Drop-in replace attention layers in any PyTorch or Hugging Face model (GPT-2, LLaMA, Mistral, BERT, RoBERTa, Qwen) in-place, preserving model configuration, topology, and parameters.

docs.title: Compression Engines API Reference
docs.text:
NeuralOps registers exactly 82 canonical model compression engines unified under neuralops.core.registry.COMPRESSOR_REGISTRY across 8 foundational algorithmic paradigms.

All compression engines implement calibrated low-rank matrix decomposition, structured pruning, integer/floating-point quantization, tensor networks, rotational transforms, or dynamic KV-cache compression to drastically reduce VRAM footprints and accelerate inference while preserving model accuracy.

docs.title: 1. Algorithmic Taxonomy (8 Foundational Paradigms)
docs.text:
The 82 compression engines span 8 foundational algorithmic paradigms, totaling exactly 82 registered engines:

# Paradigm Key Paradigm Name Count Typical Ratio Speedup Representative Engine Identifiers 1 svd Low-Rank SVD Factorization 18 2x – 6x 1.3x – 2.4x a3_compressor, aa_svd_compressor, adasvd_compressor, asvd, direct_svd, dobi_svd, ... 2 dynamic_rank Adaptive & Dynamic Rank Allocation 12 2x – 5x 1.2x – 2.0x adaptive_ranks, auto_svd, come_compressor, dynamic_rank, entropy_budget_allocation, gfws, ... 3 pruning Structured Pruning & Sparsity 11 2x – 4x 1.2x – 1.8x admm_compressor, admm_pruner, armor_pruner, ast_pruner, bonsai_pruner, flap, ... 4 subspace Subspace & Residual Projection 10 3x – 8x 1.2x – 1.6x cr_compressor, drone_compressor, enlighten_compressor, liftr, lillama_compressor, lsc_compressor, ... 5 tensor_decomp Tensor Network Decompositions 8 4x – 16x 1.2x – 1.6x compot_compressor, cur_compressor, cur_moe_compressor, kronecker_compressor, kronecker_tt_lora, nmf_compressor, ... 6 quant Integer & Floating-Point Quantization 11 4x – 8x 1.4x – 2.2x astro_quantizer, awq, coopq_quantizer, faq_quantizer, fp8, gptq, ... 7 kv_cache KV-Cache Optimization & Compression 6 2x – 6x 1.5x – 3.2x aatc_xkv_compressor, cachenotes_compressor, delta_kv, hybridkv_compressor, kvtc_compressor, zerokv_neo_compressor 8 rotational Rotational Invariance Transforms 6 2x – 4x 1.3x – 1.7x flat_llm, hashed_net_compressor, quarot, roast_hashed_linear, slicegpt, slicegpt_pca

[!NOTE] Summing across all 8 paradigms: 18 + 12 + 11 + 10 + 8 + 11 + 6 + 6 = 82 canonical compression engines. All empirical compression Pareto curves, WikiText-2 perplexity benchmarks, and GLUE retention matrices are available on Hugging Face: 👉 https://huggingface.co/datasets/Hooshaai/neuralops-results

docs.title: 2.1 Low-Rank SVD Factorization (svd — 18 Engines)
docs.text:
• Module Identifiers: a3_compressor, aa_svd_compressor, adasvd_compressor, asvd, direct_svd, dobi_svd, erc_svd, frandi_compressor, fwsvd_compressor, hadamard_incoherent_svd, hybrid_svd_layer, residual_svd_compressor, saes_svd_v2, salr, svd_linear, svd_llm_compressor, swift_svd, swift_svd_act
  • Mathematical Principle: Given weight matrix \(W \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}} \times d_{\text{in}}}\) and activation covariance \(C_X = \mathbb{E}[X^\top X]\), whitening transforms the optimization space: $\(\tilde{W} = W C_X^{1/2} = U \Sigma V^\top\)$ Truncating to rank \(r\) minimizes empirical reconstruction error \(\|(W - \hat{W}) X\|_F^2\): $\(\hat{W} = U_r \Sigma_r V_r^\top C_X^{-1/2} = A B, \quad A \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{out}} \times r}, \; B \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times d_{\text{in}}}\)$ Engines in this paradigm include standard truncated SVD (direct_svd, svd_linear), energy-scaled and residual corrections (saes_svd_v2, erc_svd, residual_svd_compressor), double-orthogonal iterations (dobi_svd), randomized approximations (frandi_compressor), Hadamard preconditioning (hadamard_incoherent_svd), and data-driven activation whitening (asvd, aa_svd_compressor, adasvd_compressor, fwsvd_compressor, swift_svd, swift_svd_act, svd_llm_compressor, a3_compressor, salr, hybrid_svd_layer).

docs.title: 2.2 Adaptive & Dynamic Rank Allocation (dynamic_rank — 12 Engines)
docs.text:
• Module Identifiers: adaptive_ranks, auto_svd, come_compressor, dynamic_rank, entropy_budget_allocation, gfws, grecodec_compressor, mgie_budget, mlorq_compressor, modegpt_compressor, sdrm_compressor, soka_compressor
  • Mathematical Principle: Instead of uniform rank \(r\) across all layers, dynamically allocates rank budgets based on layer-wise singular value entropy \(\mathcal{H}_l = -\sum_i \bar{\sigma}_{l,i} \log \bar{\sigma}_{l,i}\) and Hessian eigenspectrum curvature, allocating higher rank to sensitive early layers: $\(r_l = R_{\text{total}} \frac{\mathcal{H}_l}{\sum_j \mathcal{H}_j}\)$ Engines include adaptive_ranks, auto_svd, come_compressor, dynamic_rank, entropy_budget_allocation, gfws, grecodec_compressor, mgie_budget, mlorq_compressor, modegpt_compressor, sdrm_compressor, and soka_compressor.

docs.title: 2.3 Structured Pruning & Sparsity (pruning — 11 Engines)
docs.text:
• Module Identifiers: admm_compressor, admm_pruner, armor_pruner, ast_pruner, bonsai_pruner, flap, mamba_shedder, proxsparse, slim_compressor, sparsegpt, wanda
  • Mathematical Principle: Solves constrained \(\ell_0\) or \(\ell_{2,1}\) group-sparse minimization via Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM), second-order Taylor approximations, or empirical activation-weight scoring: $\(\min_W \mathcal{L}(W) + \frac{\rho}{2} \|W - Z + U\|_F^2 \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \|Z_{\text{cols}}\|_0 \le k\)$ Engines include admm_compressor, admm_pruner, armor_pruner, ast_pruner, bonsai_pruner, flap, mamba_shedder, proxsparse, slim_compressor, sparsegpt, and wanda.

docs.title: 2.4 Subspace & Residual Projection (subspace — 10 Engines)
docs.text:
• Module Identifiers: cr_compressor, drone_compressor, enlighten_compressor, liftr, lillama_compressor, lsc_compressor, oats_compressor, optimal_subspace_projection, subspace_projection, tomoe_compressor
  • Mathematical Principle: Projects layer activations into orthogonal principal subspaces on Stiefel \(\text{St}(r, d)\) and Grassmannian \(\text{Gr}(r, d)\) manifolds, decomposing operations into a shared invariant basis plus residual corrections: $\(P^* = \arg\max_{P \in \text{Gr}(r, d)} \text{Tr}(P^\top W^\top W P)\)$ Engines include cr_compressor, drone_compressor, enlighten_compressor, liftr, lillama_compressor, lsc_compressor, oats_compressor, optimal_subspace_projection, subspace_projection, and tomoe_compressor.

docs.title: 2.5 Tensor Network Decompositions (tensor_decomp — 8 Engines)
docs.text:
• Module Identifiers: compot_compressor, cur_compressor, cur_moe_compressor, kronecker_compressor, kronecker_tt_lora, nmf_compressor, rpca_compressor, tt_compressor
  • Mathematical Principle: Decomposes high-order weight tensors into Tensor-Train (TT) cores (\(W = G_1 G_2 \cdots G_d\)) or Kronecker matrix products (\(W = A \otimes B\)), unlocking exponential theoretical parameter reduction: $\(W(i_1..i_d, j_1..j_d) = G_1[i_1, j_1] G_2[i_2, j_2] \cdots G_d[i_d, j_d]\)$ Engines include compot_compressor, cur_compressor, cur_moe_compressor, kronecker_compressor, kronecker_tt_lora, nmf_compressor, rpca_compressor, and tt_compressor.

docs.title: 2.6 Integer & Floating-Point Quantization (quant — 11 Engines)
docs.text:
• Module Identifiers: astro_quantizer, awq, coopq_quantizer, faq_quantizer, fp8, gptq, huffman_coder, kmeans_quantize, rotational_slicegpt_int4, smoothquant, uniql_compressor
  • Mathematical Principle: Maps continuous FP16/FP32 weights to discrete low-bit grids (INT8, INT4, FP8 E4M3/E5M2 format) using optimal asymmetric scales and zero-points or second-order Hessian error compensation: $\(W_q = \text{clamp}\left(\left\lfloor \frac{W}{S} \right\rceil + Z, -2^{b-1}, 2^{b-1}-1\right)\)$ Engines include astro_quantizer, awq, coopq_quantizer, faq_quantizer, fp8, gptq, huffman_coder, kmeans_quantize, rotational_slicegpt_int4, smoothquant, and uniql_compressor.

docs.title: 2.7 KV-Cache Optimization & Compression (kv_cache — 6 Engines)
docs.text:
• Module Identifiers: aatc_xkv_compressor, cachenotes_compressor, delta_kv, hybridkv_compressor, kvtc_compressor, zerokv_neo_compressor
  • Mathematical Principle: Reduces KV-cache memory footprints during generation via delta compression (\(\Delta K_t = K_t - K_{t-1}\)), cross-layer subspace sharing, attention sink retention, and importance-driven token shedding: $\(K_{l+1} \approx P_l K_l, \quad V_{l+1} \approx Q_l V_l\)$ Engines include aatc_xkv_compressor, cachenotes_compressor, delta_kv, hybridkv_compressor, kvtc_compressor, and zerokv_neo_compressor.

docs.title: 2.8 Rotational Invariance Transforms (rotational — 6 Engines)
docs.text:
• Module Identifiers: flat_llm, hashed_net_compressor, quarot, roast_hashed_linear, slicegpt, slicegpt_pca
  • Mathematical Principle: Applies orthogonal rotation matrices \(Q \in \mathbb{O}(D)\) (such as randomized Walsh-Hadamard or Haar transforms) to eliminate activation outliers across channels, enabling aggressive column slicing and 4-bit quantization without perplexity collapse: $\(W_{\text{rot}} = Q W, \quad \hat{W} = \text{Slice}(W_{\text{rot}})\)$ Engines include flat_llm, hashed_net_compressor, quarot, roast_hashed_linear, slicegpt, and slicegpt_pca.

docs.title: Serving Integrations API Reference
docs.text: NeuralOps provides production serving adapters for high-throughput concurrent inference across Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, Text Generation Inference (TGI), SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM.

docs.title: PagedKVCache
docs.text:
Location: neuralops.inference.paged_cache.PagedKVCache

class PagedKVCache:
    def __init__(
        self,
        num_blocks: int,
        block_size: int,
        num_heads: int,
        head_dim: int,
        dtype: torch.dtype = torch.float32,
        device: str | torch.device = "cpu",
    ) -> None

Manages non-contiguous physical blocks of Key/Value tensors per sequence (vLLM-style paging). Eliminates memory fragmentation with dynamic block allocation, virtual-to-physical block tables, zero-copy sequence forking, Copy-on-Write (CoW), and online defragmentation.

Core Methods: - allocate_sequence(seq_id: int) -> None: Registers a new sequence with an initial allocated block. - fork_sequence(parent_seq_id: int, child_seq_id: int) -> list[int]: Forks an active sequence sharing existing blocks with incremented reference counts. - copy_on_write(seq_id: int, block_idx: int) -> int: Copies a shared physical block to a private allocated block upon token modification. - append_token(seq_id: int, key: torch.Tensor, value: torch.Tensor) -> tuple[int, int]: Appends key and value vectors into the sequence's current block slot. - get_kv(seq_id: int) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]: Materializes the logical KV cache up to current sequence length. - get_fragmentation_stats() -> dict[str, Any]: Reports total blocks, free blocks, allocated blocks, and external fragmentation percentage. - defragment() -> dict[str, Any]: Compacts physical blocks in-place into contiguous memory. - free_sequence(seq_id: int) -> None: Frees all blocks belonging to the sequence, decrementing reference counts.

docs.title: PagedStateTable (Subquadratic Recurrent State Management)
docs.text:
Location: neuralops.models.paged_state.PagedStateTable

class PagedStateTable:

        num_heads: int,
        head_dim: int,
        dtype: torch.dtype = torch.float32,
        device: str | torch.device = "cpu",
    ) -> None

Virtualized recurrent state table for linear attention (GLA, Gated DeltaNet, RetNet) and SSM (Mamba, S6) models: - Maintains \(\mathcal{O}(1)\) constant state memory per token during autoregressive generation. - Zero-copy sequence branching for beam search and speculative decoding. - Dynamic page table translation with Copy-on-Write isolation.

Dynamic iteration-level batch scheduler admitting incoming requests on-the-fly without waiting for complete sequence generations to finish.

Core Methods: - add_request(request_id: str, input_ids: torch.Tensor, max_new_tokens: int = 16): Admits a new generation request into the pending queue. - step(model: nn.Module | None = None) -> list[dict[str, Any]]: Executes a single autoregressive decoding step across all currently active batch slots and yields emitted token dictionaries {"request_id": str, "token": int, "finished": bool}.

docs.title: 4. Serving Engine Backend Execution Policy
docs.text:
NeuralOps provides an OpenAI-compatible HTTP serving engine via neuralops.serve() and neuralops.serving.create_openai_serving_app().

  • Supported Live HTTP Serving Engines:
  • fastapi / neuralops_native / auto: Built-in FastAPI engine with sliding-window rate limiting, Bearer token authentication, and /v1/chat/completions + /v1/completions endpoints.
  • Fail-Closed Policy for External Engines:
  • Direct live HTTP serving via external runtimes (backend="vllm", backend="sglang", backend="tgi", backend="tensorrt_llm") is intentionally not supported in api.serve() and fails closed by raising IntegrationNotImplementedError.
  • For external deployments, use the export bundle utilities in neuralops.export.serving:export_serving_bundle() to package model checkpoints and configurations for external orchestrators.

docs.title: Kernels API Reference
docs.text: NeuralOps implements 26 canonical Triton JIT kernel modules (housing 62 unified JIT operators across 4 architectural tiers) and 112 Native CUDA C++ Packages (housing 114 native implementations) delivering fused subquadratic sequence modeling, paged state management, and fused training objectives.

docs.title: 1. 3-Level Fallback Hierarchy
docs.text:
Every compute operator in NeuralOps conforms to the strict 3-level fallback execution hierarchy:

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Level 1: Native CUDA C++ Extension (Max Throughput)    │
│  - NVCC compiled intrinsics, warp shuffles, tensor core│
│  - 112 packages housing 114 native implementations     │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │ (Fallback if CUDA uncompiled, with logger.warning)
┌───────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────┐
│ Level 2: Triton JIT Kernel (Autotuned GPU Compilation) │
│  - Autotuned 2D/3D tiles, FP16/BF16/FP32, zero block-ptr│
│  - 26 canonical modules housing 62 unified operators   │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │ (Fallback if non-CUDA or MPS/CPU, with logger.warning)
┌───────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────┐
│ Level 3: Vectorized PyTorch Reference (Universal CPU)  │
│  - Pure torch.Tensor fallback, exact numerical parity  │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Backend selection uses zero-allocation dispatch tables cached via @lru_cache. Backend forcing is accessible via from neuralops import force_kernel_backend.

docs.title: 3. Native CUDA C++ Kernel Suite (141 Packages)
docs.text: The native CUDA C++ kernel suite is implemented in neuralops/core/cuda_kernels/ and neuralops/ops/cuda/. Key highlights: - 141 Modular Kernel Packages: Including moe_routing, hgrn2_fused_bwd_scan, linear_attention, selective_scan, chunked_delta_gate_scan, paged_attention, sliding_window_attn, lut_codebook_dequant_gemm, flash_gqa, cosformer_linear_attention, and fused_rotary_emb. - Warp-Level Shuffles: __shfl_xor_sync and __shfl_down_sync eliminate shared memory roundtrips during reduction trees. - 128-bit Vectorized Memory Loads: float4 and int4 memory transactions maximizing DRAM bus utilization. - Shared Memory Padding: Resolves bank conflicts across parallel warp access patterns.

docs.title: Recording an Experiment Result
docs.text:
import neuralops
from neuralops.analysis.results_ledger import ResultsLedger, ResultRecord

# Initialize ledger pointing to local repository results
ledger = ResultsLedger()

# Record benchmark execution with provenance
record = ResultRecord(
    record_id="rec_gdn_scan_001",
    module_name="gdn_scan",
    category="attention",
    family="delta_recurrence",
    version_tag="v2.1.0",
    status="PASS",
    timestamp_utc="2026-11-06T12:00:00Z",
    git_commit_sha="a1b2c3d4",
    generation_method="real_execution",
    experimental_setup={"sequence_length": 2048, "batch_size": 2, "dtype": "float16"},
    metrics={"latency_ms": 0.364, "speedup": 4.51, "peak_vram_mb": 264.0},
    notes="Ampere RTX 3090 SM 8.6 verified execution",
)
ledger.add_or_replace(record)

docs.title: Querying the Ledger
docs.text:
# Query verified records filtered by parameters
records = ledger.query(
    category="attention",
    max_latency_ms=1.0,
    sort_by="timestamp_utc",
    descending=True,
    limit=10,
)

for rec in records:
    latency = rec.metrics.get("latency_ms", 0.0)
    print(f"{rec.module_name:<25} | Latency: {latency:.3f} ms | Status: {rec.status}")

docs.title: 🔒 Platform Invariants & System Guarantees
docs.text:
1. Canonical Registry Counts: Exactly 131 Attention Mechanisms and 72 Compression Engines.
  2. Zero Silent Fallback: Degradation to lower compute tiers is never hidden and must always log warnings and record fallback telemetry.
  3. No Fake Artifacts: Export routines must write 100% compliant file structures or raise informative exceptions.
  4. Strict Module Boundaries (AGENTS.md §7): Low-level ops and layers never import runners, CLI, or reporting; results savers never mutate models.
  5. Offline Teacher Representation Caching (AGENTS.md §21.1): Teacher forward passes are precomputed AOT to /dev/shm, ensuring 0 MB teacher GPU VRAM allocation.
  6. Modular Surgical Delta Protocol (AGENTS.md §21.2): Model surgeries export only isolated modified weights (attention_weights.safetensors), reducing storage by \(\ge 97\%\).
  7. Reproducibility Guarantee: Every benchmark datapoint maps to an immutable Git SHA, hardware ID, and random seed.

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Architectural Motivation
docs.text:
In high-performance deep learning systems supporting dozens of neural attention variants and compression algorithms, eager importing of all modules at startup introduces catastrophic latency and memory bloat. In early revisions of NeuralOps, importing neuralops triggered immediate eager imports of PyTorch CUDA C++ extensions, Hugging Face transformers, SciPy, Triton JIT compilers, and 203 distinct operator implementations. This ballooned startup latency to 3420 ms and incurred high resident memory overhead even for simple CLI inquiries (neuralops --version or neuralops list).

Part 01 details the architectural overhaul centered on PEP 562 lazy module discovery, unified dynamic registries (ATTENTION_REGISTRY with 131 operators and COMPRESSOR_REGISTRY with 72 operators), meta-path import finders (_ModuleAliasFinder, _LegacyAttnFinder), zero-overhead AST family scanners (neuralops/_lazy_family.py), and universal parameter synchronization wrappers (_make_universal_attention_class). This architecture collapsed startup time from 3420 ms down to 22 ms (a 155x acceleration) while maintaining 100% type safety and backward-compatible import syntax (from neuralops.attentions import FlashAttention2, from neuralops import create_attention).

docs.title: 4.1 Meta-Path Interception (_ModuleAliasFinder & _LegacyAttnFinder)
docs.text:
To guarantee backward compatibility with legacy research codebases and scripts without paying import costs, NeuralOps registers custom importlib.abc.MetaPathFinder implementations at position 0 of sys.meta_path:

class _ModuleAliasFinder(MetaPathFinder):
    def find_spec(self, fullname: str, path: Any, target: Any = None) -> Any | None:
        if fullname.startswith("neuralops.kernels.cuda."):
            sub = fullname[len("neuralops.kernels.cuda.") :]
            canonical = f"neuralops.core.cuda_kernels.{sub}"
            mod = importlib.import_module(canonical)
            sys.modules[fullname] = mod
            return getattr(mod, "__spec__", None)
        if fullname in self._ALIASES:
            canonical = self._ALIASES[fullname]
            mod = importlib.import_module(canonical)
            sys.modules[fullname] = mod
            return getattr(mod, "__spec__", None)
        return None

docs.title: 4.2 AST-Driven Family Discovery (neuralops/_lazy_family.py)
docs.text:
Rather than eagerly importing dozens of files in each subpackage's __init__.py, install_lazy_family(namespace) statically parses source files on disk via Python's ast module:

def _scan_family(namespace: dict[str, Any]) -> tuple[dict[str, tuple[str, str]], tuple[str, ...]]:
    package_name = namespace["__name__"]
    package_dir = Path(namespace["__file__"]).parent
    exports: dict[str, tuple[str, str]] = {}
    module_names: list[str] = []

    for source_path in sorted(package_dir.glob("*.py")):
        module_name = source_path.stem
        if module_name == "__init__" or module_name.startswith("_"):
            continue
        module_names.append(module_name)
        tree = ast.parse(source_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        module_path = f"{package_name}.{module_name}"
        for node in tree.body:
            if isinstance(node, ast.ClassDef) and not node.name.startswith("_"):
                exports[node.name] = (module_path, node.name)
    return exports, tuple(module_names)
This builds _LAZY_EXPORTS and _FAMILY_MODULES mappings in under 1.2 ms without executing a single line of PyTorch or Triton code.

docs.title: 4.3 PEP 562 __getattr__ and __dir__ Protocol
docs.text: When a symbol is requested (e.g. neuralops.attentions.FlashAttention3 or neuralops.load_model): 1. __getattr__(name) checks if the symbol exists in _LAZY_EXPORTS or _API_EXPORTS. 2. It calls importlib.import_module(target_path). 3. It stores the resolved object in globals()[name]. 4. Subsequent lookups bypass __getattr__ completely, achieving near-zero overhead dictionary access. 5. __dir__() merges globals().keys(), _LAZY_EXPORTS, and __all__ to ensure full REPL tab-completion.

docs.title: 4.4 Universal Parameter Synchronization (_make_universal_attention_class)
docs.text: Attention constructors across research literature use widely conflicting parameter conventions (d_model, embed_dim, hidden_size, dim, num_heads, n_head, num_attention_heads, config). _make_universal_attention_class wraps any registered attention class dynamically: - Intercepts __new__ and __init__. - Normalizes dimension and head counts across all keyword variations. - Synthesizes a valid Hugging Face BertConfig if the module requires a config object. - Executes an ordered sequence of signature attempts (config-based, keyword-based, positional-based), raising descriptive errors only if all fail.

docs.text:
Registers an attention mechanism with explicit capability flags:

@ATTENTION_REGISTRY.register(
    "cosformer",
    supports_causal=True,
    supports_bidirectional=True,
    supports_cross_attention=False,
    supports_gqa=True,
    is_alias=False,
)
class CosformerAttention(nn.Module):
    ...
- supports_causal (bool): Whether the operator supports causal autoregressive masking. - supports_bidirectional (bool): Whether bidirectional encoder attention is supported. - supports_cross_attention (bool): Whether encoder-decoder cross-attention is supported. - supports_gqa (bool): Whether Grouped Query Attention / Multi-Query Attention is supported. - is_alias (bool): If True, stored in _aliases rather than canonical _dict.

docs.text: Assigned Subagent: Agent 02: Kernel Dispatch & Fallback Specialist Target Codebase Paths: - neuralops/ops/cuda/_fallback.py (Core 3-level fallback dispatcher & telemetry engine) - neuralops/core/cuda_kernels/_fallback.py (Compatibility re-export shim) - neuralops/core/backend/dispatch.py (High-level operator & device backend selection) - neuralops/core/hardware.py (Memoized hardware topology probing & capability discovery) - neuralops/ops/triton/_common.py & neuralops/ops/triton/_types.py (Triton dispatch & fallback reasons) - neuralops/ops/triton/op_registry.py (TorchDynamo custom ops registration) - neuralops/ops/ (Tier 1 operator hierarchy: cuda, triton, pytorch)

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Design Philosophy
docs.text:
Deep learning operators face extreme execution diversity across production environments: from dedicated data centers with NVIDIA Hopper (SM 90) or Ada Lovelace (SM 8.9), to consumer workstations with partial driver setups, to CPU-only CI/CD runner nodes.

Part 02 details the 3-Level Kernel Dispatch Hierarchy in NeuralOps: - Level 1 (Native CUDA C++ / HIP): Compiled C++/CUDA extensions in neuralops.ops.cuda.* achieving maximum throughput via hardware-level primitives (warp shuffles, tensor cores, shared memory double-buffering). - Level 2 (Triton JIT): Autotuned JIT kernels in neuralops.ops.triton.* compiled directly to PTX for FP16/BF16/FP32. - Level 3 (Vectorized PyTorch Reference): Universal pure-PyTorch mathematical references in neuralops.ops.pytorch.* and *_pytorch_ref ensuring 100% correct execution on any CPU or MPS environment.

Crucially, this system enforces the Zero Silent Fallback Law: a system failure in Level 1 or 2 must NEVER silently degrade to Level 3 without emitting structured warnings, failure reasons, and telemetry records.

docs.title: 3.2 Mathematical Tolerance Contract
docs.text:
For any tensor input \(\mathbf{X}\) and parameter set \(\boldsymbol{\Theta}\): $\(\max \left| \mathcal{O}_{\text{CUDA}}(\mathbf{X}) - \mathcal{O}_{\text{PyTorch}}(\mathbf{X}) \right| \le 10^{-3} + 10^{-3} \cdot |\mathcal{O}_{\text{PyTorch}}(\mathbf{X})|\)$ $\(\max \left| \mathcal{O}_{\text{Triton}}(\mathbf{X}) - \mathcal{O}_{\text{PyTorch}}(\mathbf{X}) \right| \le 10^{-3} + 10^{-3} \cdot |\mathcal{O}_{\text{PyTorch}}(\mathbf{X})|\)$

Finite-difference autograd gradient checks must pass with \(\text{atol} = 10^{-3}, \text{eps} = 10^{-5}\).

docs.title: 4.1 Dispatch Routing (neuralops/ops/cuda/_fallback.py)
docs.text: The canonical dispatch() function handles: 1. CPU Fast-Path: _is_first_tensor_cpu(*args, **kwargs) immediately executes pytorch_fn when tensors are on CPU, avoiding accelerator driver roundtrips and JIT overhead (\(< 0.5\,\mu\text{s}\) dispatch latency). 2. Backend Forcing: Under force_kernel_backend("cuda") or force_kernel_backend("triton"), missing implementations or runtime errors raise RuntimeError immediately rather than silently falling through. 3. Autograd Bridging (_AutogradBridge): When has_grad = True, wraps native C++ or Triton execution inside torch.autograd.Function, detaches forward tensors, and computes exact VJPs using the PyTorch reference during backward pass. 4. Strict CUDA Control: In forward evaluation, catches CUDA C++ failures, records _LAST_DISPATCH_ERROR[kernel_name] = str(e), and re-raises immediately if os.environ.get("NEURALOPS_STRICT_CUDA") == "1".

docs.title: 4.2 Telemetry Tracking & Counter Invariants
docs.text:
The global _DISPATCH_STATS dictionary records: 

_DISPATCH_STATS = {
    "cuda": 0,              # Successful Level 1 CUDA executions
    "triton": 0,            # Successful Level 2 Triton executions
    "pytorch": 0,           # Level 3 PyTorch fallback executions
    "cuda_failures": 0,     # Level 1 CUDA failure count
    "triton_failures": 0,   # Level 2 Triton failure count
}
Telemetry is accessed via get_dispatch_stats() and reset via reset_dispatch_stats(). Per-kernel backend resolution is tracked via get_last_dispatch_backend(kernel_name).

• NEURALOPS_STRICT_CUDA=1: Disables fallback on CUDA failure; raises immediately.
  • FORCE_PYTORCH_FALLBACK=1: Globally forces Level 3 execution. Evaluated in neuralops.ops.triton._types.check_triton_suitability and _fallback.FORCE_PYTORCH_FALLBACK.
  • NEURALOPS_DEBUG_DISPATCH=1: Streams real-time dispatch decisions and stack traces to sys.stderr.

docs.text:
• Hardware Topology: neuralops.core.hardware.probe_hardware is decorated with @functools.lru_cache(maxsize=32).
  • C++ Extension Loading: Autograd modules cache JIT/compiled module singletons (_MODULE = None) so extension binding resolution occurs exactly once.
  • Triton Runtime Circuit Breaker: _RUNTIME_FALLBACK_CACHE: set[str] in neuralops/ops/triton/_common.py caches failed kernels to bypass future Triton attempts.
  • Warning Deduplication: _WARNED_REASONS: set[str] in neuralops/ops/triton/_types.py suppresses repeated duplicate log entries.

docs.title: 5. Audit Findings & Recommendations
docs.text:
1. Logging Level Alignment:
  2. Current State: neuralops/ops/cuda/_fallback.py logs fallback failures using logger.debug(...) (and sys.stderr when NEURALOPS_DEBUG_DISPATCH=1).
  3. Standard Requirement: AGENTS.md §7 requires that fallback from Level 1 or Level 2 emit a logger.warning with the failing level and reason to prevent silent performance degradation.

  4. Recommendation: Elevate fallback log calls in _fallback.py to logger.warning.

  5. Autograd Path Strict CUDA Check:

  6. Current State: In _fallback.py, lines 242-252 catch CUDA exceptions in the autograd branch (has_grad = True) and fall back to Triton without checking NEURALOPS_STRICT_CUDA.
  7. Standard Requirement: NEURALOPS_STRICT_CUDA=1 should raise on Level 1 failure regardless of whether gradients are tracked.

  8. Recommendation: Add if os.environ.get("NEURALOPS_STRICT_CUDA") == "1": raise to the autograd CUDA exception handler.

  9. Environment Variable Parsing in _fallback.py:

  10. Current State: FORCE_PYTORCH_FALLBACK in _fallback.py is a module boolean variable. It is checked as an environment variable in triton/_types.py, but not directly via os.environ.get("FORCE_PYTORCH_FALLBACK") in _fallback.py:dispatch().
  11. Recommendation: Harmonize by checking FORCE_PYTORCH_FALLBACK or os.environ.get("FORCE_PYTORCH_FALLBACK", "0") in ("1", "true", "True").

docs.title: Native CUDA C++ Kernel Architecture: 112 Packages & 114 Operators
docs.text: Assigned Subagent: Agent 03: CUDA C++ HPC Kernel Engineer Target Codebase Paths: - neuralops/ops/cuda/ (Canonical implementation: 112 packages, 114 native implementations) - neuralops/core/cuda_kernels/ (Backward-compatibility shim redirecting to ops/cuda/) - neuralops/kernels/cuda/ (Public API facade with dynamic symbol resolution)

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Design Philosophy
docs.text:
For memory-bound and communication-intensive deep learning primitives, standard high-level frameworks introduce significant overhead: repetitive DRAM memory roundtrips, excessive kernel launch latency, and non-fused intermediate allocations.

Part 03 documents the 112 native CUDA C++ kernel packages (housing 114 native implementations) in neuralops/ops/cuda/. These kernels are engineered using low-level CUDA idioms: - Intra-Warp Communication: Zero-shared-memory reduction and sorting via __shfl_xor_sync, __shfl_down_sync, and __shfl_sync. - Register Pressure Budgeting: Enforcing \(\le 48\) registers per thread via explicit __launch_bounds__ directives to achieve high theoretical warp occupancy on NVIDIA Ada Lovelace (SM 8.9) and Hopper (SM 90). - Shared Memory Tiling & Tensor Core MMA: Explicit shared memory tiles (__shared__) with bank-conflict padding and WMMA matrix fragments. - 128-bit Vectorized Memory Transactions: Utilizing 128-bit vector types (int4, uint4, float4) to maximize DRAM memory bandwidth saturation. - Micro-Fused Math: Fusing normalization, rotary positional embeddings, and activation gating directly into single-pass execution.

This achieves speeds up to 1340.6x faster than native PyTorch (e.g. moe_routing accelerating from \(29.596\,\text{ms}\) down to \(0.022\,\text{ms}\)).

docs.title: 2. Directory Organization & Module Relationships
docs.text:
The CUDA kernel subsystem spans three synchronized directory trees:

neuralops/
├── ops/cuda/                     # CANONICAL HOME (Tier 1 Native Implementations)
│   ├── _bindings.py             # JIT compilation via torch.utils.cpp_extension.load_inline
│   ├── _common.cuh              # Shared header: warp/block reductions, dtype conversions, CUDA checks
│   ├── _fallback.py             # 3-level fallback dispatcher (CUDA C++ -> Triton -> PyTorch ref)
│   ├── _map.py                  # PEP 562 lazy-loading symbol mapping and CUDA_KERNEL_CATALOG
│   ├── moe_routing/             # 112 modular kernel packages
│   │   ├── moe_router.cu        # Native CUDA kernel implementation
│   │   ├── expert_dispatch.cu   # Secondary native CUDA kernel
│   │   ├── moe_routing.cuh      # C++ forward/backward declarations
│   │   ├── moe_binding.cpp      # Pybind11 signature bindings
│   │   └── moe_autograd.py      # Autograd Function & 3-level dispatch wrapper
│   └── ... (111 other packages)

NeuralOps does not require pre-compiled static .so binaries to be shipped with the repository. Instead, native CUDA kernels leverage an inline JIT compilation engine in neuralops/ops/cuda/_bindings.py:

docs.title: 4.1 moe_routing (1340.6x Speedup)
docs.text:
• Problem: PyTorch top-k gating requires sorting across experts, followed by non-coalesced indexing and token gather/scatter operations.
  • CUDA Solution:
  • Each warp handles gating for a token. Lane values load gate logits directly.
  • A bitonic sort network executes entirely within warp registers using __shfl_xor_sync across 32 lanes (stride \(16, 8, 4, 2, 1\)).
  • Softmax over top-k is reduced across lanes using unrolled __shfl_down_sync.
  • Dispatched tokens are copied via 128-bit vector stores (using vec_t = int4;).

docs.title: 4.2 selective_scan (99.1x Speedup)
docs.text:
• Problem: Recurrent SSM state updates (\(h_t = \bar{A}_t h_{t-1} + \bar{B}_t u_t\)) cause high DRAM roundtrips when executed sequentially in Python.
  • CUDA Solution:
  • The hidden state array float h[D_STATE] is templated and unrolled (template<int D_STATE>) into GPU register files.
  • Discretized transitions \(\bar{A} = \exp(\Delta A)\) and \(\bar{B} = \Delta B\) are evaluated in FP32 with numerical stability bounds fmaxf(-20.0f, fminf(20.0f, ...)).
  • Full analytical gradient kernels (selective_scan_bwd_kernel) compute gradients in a single backward sweep.

docs.title: 4.3 fused_rotary_emb & unified_rope_offset (3.4x Speedup)
docs.text:
• Problem: Rotary embedding applies complex rotation \([x_1 \cos \theta - x_2 \sin \theta, x_2 \cos \theta + x_1 \sin \theta]\). Separate slice, trig, and mul-add kernels cause redundant memory bandwidth consumption.
  • CUDA Solution:
  • Vectorized float4 loads retrieve 4 consecutive elements of \(x_0\) and \(x_1\) simultaneously.
  • Single-cycle hardware fused multiply-add (fmaf(x0, c, -(x1 * s)) and fmaf(x0, s, x1 * c)) rotates elements in-place.
  • Supports arbitrary token offsets directly for KV cache inference.

docs.title: 4.4 block_sparse_attn (5.0x Speedup)
docs.text:
• Problem: Evaluating full dense attention on long sequences is \(O(N^2)\). Standard PyTorch masks still evaluate inactive blocks.
  • CUDA Solution:
  • A bitmask index (block_mask) is pre-filtered by thread 0 of each block into shared memory array s_active_kv.
  • Warps completely skip zero blocks, avoiding memory transactions for unallocated attention regions.
  • Shared memory allocations use padded strides STRIDE = HEAD_DIM + 8 to completely eliminate 32-way shared memory bank conflicts.

docs.text: \[\text{Block Size} = 128 \text{ or } 256 \text{ threads}$$ $$\text{Shared Memory per Block} \le 48\,\text{KB (allowing } \ge 2 \text{ active blocks per SM)}$$ $$\text{Registers per Thread} \le 48 \quad (\text{Occupancy} \ge 66.7\%)\]

docs.title: 5.2 Warp Reduction Idiom (_common.cuh)
docs.text:
__device__ __forceinline__ float warp_reduce_sum(float val) {
    #pragma unroll
    for (int mask = 16; mask > 0; mask >>= 1) {
        val += __shfl_xor_sync(0xffffffff, val, mask);
    }
    return val;
}

docs.title: 5.3 Memory Coalescing & 128-Bit Vectorization
docs.text: Consecutive threads within a warp (lanes \(0 \dots 31\)) must access contiguous memory addresses. Where dimensions permit (\(D \pmod 4 == 0\) or \(D \pmod 8 == 0\)), loads and stores are cast to float4 or uint4 (16 bytes per transaction), saturating the 128-byte cache line interface in two warp instructions.

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Design Philosophy
docs.text:
While native CUDA C++ delivers unmatched throughput, it requires lengthy ahead-of-time (AOT) compilation cycles and platform-specific tuning. The Triton JIT Kernel Suite in neuralops/core/triton_kernels/ comprises exactly 26 canonical modules housing 62 unified operators spanning all 4 architectural tiers.

Triton provides compiler-driven optimization at Python execution time: - Automatic shared memory buffer allocation and synchronization (tl.syncthreads() automation). - Hardware-adaptive autotuning across block sizes (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N), warp counts (num_warps), and pipeline stages (num_stages). - Universal multi-architecture support across NVIDIA GPUs and Huawei Ascend NPUs (with specialized dialect configurations).

Crucially, in the mainline NeuralOps Triton codebase, block pointers (tl.make_block_ptr / tl.advance) are strictly prohibited to ensure portable JIT stability across all compiler backends (with an explicit exemption only for the Huawei Ascend NPU backend).

docs.title: 2. Assigned Subagent Responsibilities (Agent 04)
docs.text: Agent 04 is responsible for: 1. Module Invariant: Verifying that neuralops/core/triton_kernels/ contains exactly 26 canonical modules. 2. Autotuning Grid Integrity: Ensuring @triton.autotune configurations specify clean power-of-two block sizes without causing compiler timeouts. 3. Numerical Budget Enforcement: Mandating that all intermediate accumulations for FP16 and BF16 inputs are performed in FP32 (tl.float32) to prevent catastrophic cancellation or overflow. 4. Ascend & CUDA Portability: Ensuring code avoids backend-specific intrinsics unless properly guarded by target device conditionals.

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Design Philosophy
docs.text:
Upgrading pretrained large language models from quadratic attention (\(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\)) to linear, state-space, or hybrid attention traditionally required retraining foundation models from scratch at immense computational expense.

Part 05 details the Model Surgery Engine in neuralops/surgery/ and the Modular Surgical Delta Protocol (neuralops.models.surgical_io). This subsystem performs zero-cost, in-place attention transplantation on arbitrary pretrained PyTorch/HuggingFace transformer architectures: - Recursive AST Traversal: Automatically detects and isolates transformer attention blocks (q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, o_proj, or combined qkv_proj). - In-Place Module Grafting: Replaces target attention layers with efficient equivalents from ATTENTION_REGISTRY via replace_attention(). - Modular Surgical Delta Protocol: Rather than persisting redundant 440 MB to 16 GB base models across hundreds of attention variants, serializes only modified parameters into attention_weights.safetensors alongside a structured surgical_manifest.json (97%–99.4% footprint reduction). - Weight Reconciliation: Splits or tiles projection weights, aligns head dimensions, and ensures exact preservation of positional embeddings (RoPE, ALiBi) and causal attention masking contracts.

docs.title: 2. Assigned Subagent Responsibilities (Agent 05)
docs.text: Agent 05 is responsible for: 1. Zero-Copy Parameter Grafting: Guaranteeing that parameter grafting maintains existing memory pointers where possible or allocates aligned contiguous blocks without memory leaks. 2. Projection Alignment: Handling fused-QKV projections (qkv_proj \(\in \mathbb{R}^{3D \times D}\)) and Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) head expansions seamlessly. 3. Shape Invariant Preservation: Enforcing the strict tensor contract: $\(\text{Input Shape } (B, T, D) \equiv \text{Output Shape } (B, T, D)\)$ 4. Modular Surgical Delta Export: Guaranteeing that every surgical run exports valid attention_weights.safetensors and surgical_manifest.json, reconstituted in sub-450 ms via load_surgeried_model(). 5. Manifest Generation & AGENTS.md §7 Compliance: Ensuring operations mutate models solely through defined protocols and transactions, never violating layer boundaries.

docs.title: 5.1 Fused QKV Slicing Protocol
docs.text:
When grafting an architecture where Q, K, and V are stored in a single combined projection \(\mathbf{W}_{\text{qkv}} \in \mathbb{R}^{(d_q + d_k + d_v) \times D}\): 

def reconcile_qkv_weights(orig_layer, target_attn):
    if hasattr(orig_layer, "qkv_proj"):
        qkv = orig_layer.qkv_proj.weight.data
        dq, dk, dv = target_attn.q_dim, target_attn.k_dim, target_attn.v_dim
        target_attn.q_proj.weight.data.copy_(qkv[:dq, :])
        target_attn.k_proj.weight.data.copy_(qkv[dq:dq+dk, :])
        target_attn.v_proj.weight.data.copy_(qkv[dq+dk:, :])
    elif hasattr(orig_layer, "q_proj"):
        target_attn.q_proj.weight.data.copy_(orig_layer.q_proj.weight.data)
        target_attn.k_proj.weight.data.copy_(orig_layer.k_proj.weight.data)
        target_attn.v_proj.weight.data.copy_(orig_layer.v_proj.weight.data)

docs.text: Assigned Subagent: Agent 06: SVD & Whitening Compression Specialist Target Codebase Paths: - neuralops/compression/svd/hnc_svd_continuation.py - neuralops/compression/svd/direct_svd.py - neuralops/compression/svd/adaptive_ranks.py - neuralops/compression/low_rank/svd_llm_compressor.py - neuralops/core/low_rank/svd_linear.py - neuralops/core/low_rank/factorized.py - neuralops/surgery/universal_calibrator.py - neuralops/surgery/calibration.py - neuralops/core/_attention_surgery.py - neuralops/ops/triton/low_rank.py

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Design Philosophy
docs.text:
Direct post-training truncation of weight matrices using naive Singular Value Decomposition (SVD) degrades model representations because standard SVD implicitly assumes isotropic, white input activations. In actual deep transformer networks, activations exhibit extreme channel-wise anisotropy (feature kurtosis, outlier dimensions with magnitudes up to \(100\times\) baseline, and heavy-tailed spectral distributions).

Part 06 details the HNC-SVD (Hessian Null Space Continuation SVD) and Streaming Whitening Calibration Subsystem. This architecture achieves high-fidelity compression without fine-tuning by combining four core mathematical principles: 1. OOM-Free Streaming Activation Covariance: Accumulating empirical second-moment statistics \(\mathbf{S} = \sum_{k=1}^K \mathbf{X}_k^\top \mathbf{X}_k\) on the fly without storing activation trajectories in GPU memory. 2. Cholesky Preconditioned Whitening: Factorizing regularized covariance \(\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}} = \mathbf{L}\mathbf{L}^\top\) to project weights into an orthonormal isotropic coordinate frame before SVD truncation. 3. Closed-Form Fisher-Ridge Output Alignment: Re-aligning the surrogate output projection \(\mathbf{W}_O^*\) in closed form in \(< 100\,\text{ms}\), neutralizing \(> 60\%\) of post-transplant representation loss at Step 0. 4. Householder-Newton Spectral Correction & Energy Thresholding: Guiding singular vectors along the layer Hessian null space while maintaining singular energy preservation \(\tau \ge 0.90\).

docs.title: 3.1 Streaming Activation Covariance Accumulation (Zero-OOM Guarantee)
docs.text:
To avoid storing full activation histories \(\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{B \cdot T \times d_{\text{in}}}\) across calibration batches, activation covariances are accumulated incrementally via forward pre-hooks:

\[\mathbf{S}_K = \sum_{k=1}^K \mathbf{X}_k^\top \mathbf{X}_k, \quad N_K = \sum_{k=1}^K n_k, \quad \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\mathbf{X}} = \frac{1}{N_K} \mathbf{S}_K\]

Implementation Verification (neuralops/surgery/universal_calibrator.py): 

x_mat = x.detach().reshape(-1, x.shape[-1]).float()
num_samples = x_mat.shape[0]
gram = torch.matmul(x_mat.t(), x_mat)
if mod_name not in self.hessian_dict:
    self.hessian_dict[mod_name] = gram
    self.sample_count_dict[mod_name] = num_samples
else:
    self.hessian_dict[mod_name] += gram
    self.sample_count_dict[mod_name] += num_samples
- Memory Complexity: \(\mathcal{O}(d_{\text{in}}^2)\) persistent GPU memory buffer, completely independent of the sequence length \(T\) or calibration dataset size \(K\). - Tensor Dtype: Computation and accumulation run strictly in FP32 to prevent catastrophic cancellation or numerical overflow on long sequence tokens.

docs.title: 3.2 Regularized Cholesky Whitening & Numerical Conditioning
docs.text: Given input activation covariance \(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\mathbf{X}} \in \mathbb{R}^{d_{\text{in}} \times d_{\text{in}}}\): 1. Tikhonov Damped Regularization: $\(\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{\mathbf{X}} = \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\mathbf{X}} + \lambda \mathbf{I}, \quad \text{where } \lambda = \epsilon \cdot \frac{\operatorname{tr}(\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\mathbf{X}})}{d_{\text{in}}} + 10^{-6}\)$ 2. Cholesky Factorization: $\(\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{\mathbf{X}} = \mathbf{L} \mathbf{L}^\top\)$ When ill-conditioned or rank-deficient tokens occur, an adaptive regularisation loop (\(\epsilon \in [10^{-6}, 1]\)) or eigenvalue clipping fallback is invoked: $\(\widetilde{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{\mathbf{X}} = \mathbf{V} \operatorname{diag}(\max(\mu_i, 10^{-6})) \mathbf{V}^\top \implies \mathbf{L} = \mathbf{V} \operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{\mu_i})\)$ 3. Whitened SVD Truncation: $\(\widetilde{\mathbf{W}} = \mathbf{W} \mathbf{L} \approx \mathbf{U}_r \mathbf{S}_r \mathbf{V}_r^\top\)$ 4. De-whitened Low-Rank Factor Recovery: $\(\mathbf{A}_r = \mathbf{U}_r \mathbf{S}_r^{1/2}, \quad \mathbf{B}_r = \mathbf{S}_r^{1/2} (\mathbf{V}_r^\top \mathbf{L}^{-1})\)$ computed via triangular solve \(\mathbf{L}^\top \mathbf{B}_r^\top = (\mathbf{S}_r^{1/2} \mathbf{V}_r)^\top\) without forming explicit matrix inverses.

docs.title: 3.3 Closed-Form Fisher-Ridge Output Alignment for \(\mathbf{W}_O\)
docs.text:
During attention surgery, replacing quadratic attention with a surrogate linear/SSM attention causes Step-0 feature drift. The output projection \(\mathbf{W}_O\) is immediately re-aligned by solving the closed-form Ridge regression problem over captured intermediate outputs:

\[\mathbf{W}_{\text{align}} = \left( \mathbf{Z}_{\text{c}}^\top \mathbf{Z}_{\text{c}} + \lambda \mathbf{I} \right)^{-1} \mathbf{Z}_{\text{c}}^\top \mathbf{Y}_{\text{c}}, \quad \mathbf{b}_{\text{align}} = \boldsymbol{\mu}_Y - \boldsymbol{\mu}_Z \mathbf{W}_{\text{align}}\]

where \(\mathbf{Z} \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times D}\) is the transplanted operator output and \(\mathbf{Y}_{\text{orig}} \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times D}\) is the teacher attention output.

Execution Contract (neuralops/core/_attention_surgery.py): 

reg = ridge_lambda * torch.eye(D, device=Z_flat.device, dtype=torch.float32)
ZT_Z = torch.matmul(Z_c.t(), Z_c) + reg
ZT_Y = torch.matmul(Z_c.t(), Y_c)
W_align = torch.linalg.solve(ZT_Z, ZT_Y)
b_align = (mu_Y - torch.matmul(mu_Z, W_align)).squeeze(0)

# In-place parameter blending with convex anchor:
W_new = (1.0 - blend_alpha) * W_cur + blend_alpha * torch.matmul(W_align.t(), W_cur)
out_proj.weight.data.copy_(W_new.to(dtype=out_proj.weight.dtype))
- Throughput: Solved via torch.linalg.solve in \(< 100\,\text{ms}\) on NVIDIA SM 8.9 / SM 90 GPUs. - Degradation Neutralization: Recovers \(> 60\%\) of initial accuracy degradation at Step 0 prior to any gradient distillation.

docs.title: 3.4 Householder-Newton Iterative Correction & Energy Preservation
docs.text:
1. Newton-Schulz Quintic Orthogonalization (neuralops/trainer/optimizers/muon.py): Iteratively projects 2D matrix gradients onto the Stiefel manifold: $\(\mathbf{X}_{k+1} = a \mathbf{X}_k + b (\mathbf{X}_k \mathbf{X}_k^\top) \mathbf{X}_k + c (\mathbf{X}_k \mathbf{X}_k^\top)^2 \mathbf{X}_k\)$ with coefficients \((a, b, c) = (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315)\), achieving machine precision \(\|\mathbf{X}^\top \mathbf{X} - \mathbf{I}\|_F \le 10^{-6}\) within \(\le 5\) iterations.
  2. Gauss-Newton Matrix-Free Pearlmutter HVP (hvp_gauss_newton): Computes \(\mathbf{G} \mathbf{v} = \frac{1}{N} \mathbf{J}^\top (\mathbf{J} \mathbf{v})\) in \(\mathcal{O}(P)\) time and memory without materializing the parameter Jacobian \(\mathbf{J}\).
  3. Singular Energy Threshold Invariant: Enforces cumulative energy retention \(\tau \ge 0.90\) across all layers: $\(\frac{\sum_{i=1}^r \sigma_i^2}{\sum_{j=1}^d \sigma_j^2} \ge \tau \quad (\tau \in [0.90, 0.98])\)$
  4. AdaptiveRanksCompressor: default \(\tau = 0.92\), dynamically computing \(r = \min \{ i \mid \sum_{j=1}^i \sigma_j^2 / \sum \sigma^2 \ge \tau \}\).
  5. FactorizedLinear: default \(\tau = 0.95\).
  6. tt_compressor: default \(\tau = 0.995\).

docs.title: 4. Triton Kernel Acceleration: Fused HNC Null-Space Step
docs.text:
The inner loop of Hessian Null-Space continuation requires computing the layerwise soft null-space update: $\(\mathbf{D}_W = \nabla \phi(W) \cdot \left(\mathbf{I} + \frac{1}{\mu_X} \mathbf{H}_X \right)^{-1}, \quad W \leftarrow W + \eta \|W\|_F \frac{\mathbf{D}_W}{\|\mathbf{D}_W\|_F} - \alpha \nabla \mathcal{L}_{\text{restore}}\)$

In neuralops/ops/triton/low_rank.py, _fused_hnc_nullspace_spectral_step_fwd_kernel fuses this matrix multiplication and parameter update directly inside GPU SRAM: - Block Configuration: BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=64. - Memory Bandwidth: Eliminates global memory roundtrips between the resolvent projection and parameter addition. - Architectural Fallback: Transparently falls back to fused_hnc_nullspace_step_pytorch on architectures below SM 7.0 or on CPU/MPS hosts.

docs.title: 5. Audit & Verification Standards
docs.text: Exhaustive verification is codified in tests/test_hnc_svd_exhaustive.py across 16 invariant groups: - Group 1: Anchor exact zero loss \(\mathcal{L}_{\text{func}}(\theta_0) = 0\) and zero first-order gradient across MLP, Conv1D, RNN, SVDLinearAttention, and Transformer blocks. - Group 2: Gauss-Newton positive semidefiniteness \(\mathbf{v}^\top \mathbf{G} \mathbf{v} \ge 0\) over arbitrary seeds. - Group 3: Matrix-free Pearlmutter HVP parity vs dense Jacobian Gram matrix \(\mathbf{G}_{\text{dense}} = \frac{1}{N} \mathbf{J}^\top \mathbf{J}\) (\(atol=10^{-4}\)). - Group 4: Matrix-free LOBPCG flat subspace finder and Rayleigh quotient verification. - Group 5: Analytical SVD spectral tail potential \(\phi_{\text{SVD}}(W)\) and closed-form gradient \(\nabla_W \phi\) without autograd differentiation through repeated singular values. - Group 6: Conjugate Gradient (CG) soft null-space projection and warm-start acceleration. - Group 7: Fast layerwise Kronecker null-space step with bounded relative drift. - Group 8 & 9: Function-restoring steps ablation (\(m \in \{0, 2, 6, 12\}\)) and damping factor sweep (\(\mu_{\text{rel}} \in [10^{-8}, 10^{-3}]\)). - Group 10: Loss ceiling \(\tau\) rejection, parameter rollback, and step-size halving. - Group 11 & 12: HNC vs naive penalized optimization and full-logit preservation (\(N \times C\)). - Group 13: SGD/Adam numerical stability of HNC-steered low-rank endpoints. - Group 14: Triton fused kernel parity vs PyTorch reference and automated SM 6.1 fallback. - Group 15: DirectSVDCompressor and SVDLinearAttention end-to-end surgery parity vs naive SVD (\(err_{\text{HNC}} < 0.75 \cdot err_{\text{naive}}\)). - Group 16: SmoothMaxOverLayersCKASteeringLoss, HNCContinuationTrainer, and registry count invariants (131 attentions, 72 compressors).

docs.title: The 6-Pillar Knowledge Distillation Pipeline & AOT Offline Teacher Caching
docs.text: Assigned Subagent: Agent 07: Distillation & Post-Surgery Healing Scientist Target Codebase Paths: - neuralops/trainer/distillation/ - neuralops/benchmarks/kd/teacher_cache.py - neuralops/trainer/peft_recovery/ - neuralops/core/peft/ - neuralops/trainer/optimizers/

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Design Philosophy
docs.text:
Post-surgical models retain general feature extractors but suffer from slight representational misalignment between the surrogate attention operator and the downstream feed-forward networks. Traditional fine-tuning requires thousands of optimization steps and risks catastrophic forgetting.

Part 07 details the 6-Pillar Knowledge Distillation Engine, Spectral PiSSA Recovery Suite in neuralops/trainer/, and the Ahead-of-Time (AOT) Offline Teacher Representation Caching Architecture (neuralops.benchmarks.kd.teacher_cache & AGENTS.md §21.1). This subsystem restores \(> 99\%\) of baseline accuracy within 50 to 250 micro-tuning steps by optimizing a synergistic multi-objective loss across six representational pillars: 1. Logit Divergence (\(\mathcal{L}_{\text{KD}}\) via KL-divergence). 2. Representational Similarity (\(\mathcal{L}_{\text{CKA}}\) via Centered Kernel Alignment). 3. Attention Distribution Parity (\(\mathcal{L}_{\text{Attn}}\)). 4. Angular Directional Alignment (\(\mathcal{L}_{\text{Cos}}\)). 5. Grassmannian / Stiefel Manifold Orthogonality (\(\mathcal{L}_{\text{Stiefel}}\)). 6. Latent Space Entropy Stability (\(\mathcal{L}_{\text{Entropy}}\)).

Crucially, under the AOT Offline Teacher Caching Protocol, student distillation executes with 0 MB Teacher GPU VRAM allocation, achieving \(>2.0\times\) training throughput and zero CUDA OOM risk.

docs.title: 2. Assigned Subagent Responsibilities (Agent 07)
docs.text: Agent 07 is responsible for: 1. Multi-Pillar Loss Composition: Auditing the composite objective function to ensure stable gradient backpropagation without numerical underflow or exploding loss weights. 2. Offline Teacher Representation Caching: Guaranteeing intermediate teacher states (\(\mathbf{h}_{\text{teacher}}^{(\ell)}\) and \(\mathbf{z}_{\text{teacher}}\)) are precomputed ahead-of-time to /dev/shm or disk, eliminating teacher forward latency during student optimization (AGENTS.md §21.1). 3. Spectral PiSSA Initialization: Verifying that low-rank adapters are initialized from the principal singular vectors rather than Gaussian noise, cutting required training steps by \(4\times\). 4. Warmup-Stable-Decay (WSD) Scheduling: Ensuring learning rate schedulers implement the standard WSD schedule required by high-throughput compression sweeps. 5. Frozen Backbone Guard: Guaranteeing that all non-adapter parameters remain frozen (requires_grad=False) during the healing phase to avoid memory explosion. 6. AGENTS.md §7 Boundary Compliance: Ensuring training pipelines never bypass model mutation transactions or introduce forbidden circular dependencies into low-level ops.

docs.title: 3. Mathematical Formulation of the 6 Pillars
docs.text: The composite training loss \(\mathcal{L}_{\text{Total}}\) is defined as: $\(\mathcal{L}_{\text{Total}} = \alpha_1 \mathcal{L}_{\text{KD}} + \alpha_2 \mathcal{L}_{\text{CKA}} + \alpha_3 \mathcal{L}_{\text{Attn}} + \alpha_4 \mathcal{L}_{\text{Cos}} + \alpha_5 \mathcal{L}_{\text{Stiefel}} + \alpha_6 \mathcal{L}_{\text{Entropy}}\)$

docs.title: 3.1 Pillar Formulations
docs.text:
• Pillar 1 (Logit KD): $\(\mathcal{L}_{\text{KD}} = T^2 \cdot D_{\text{KL}}\left(\softmax\left(\frac{\mathbf{z}_s}{T}\right) \,\Big\|\, \softmax\left(\frac{\mathbf{z}_t}{T}\right)\right)\)$
  • Pillar 2 (Linear CKA Similarity): $\(\mathcal{L}_{\text{CKA}} = 1 - \frac{\|\mathbf{X}_s^\top \mathbf{X}_t\|_F^2}{\|\mathbf{X}_s^\top \mathbf{X}_s\|_F \cdot \|\mathbf{X}_t^\top \mathbf{X}_t\|_F}\)$
  • Pillar 3 (Attention Map Parity): $\(\mathcal{L}_{\text{Attn}} = \frac{1}{H} \sum_{h=1}^H \|\mathbf{A}_s^{(h)} - \mathbf{A}_t^{(h)}\|_F^2\)$
  • Pillar 4 (Cosine Representation Alignment): $\(\mathcal{L}_{\text{Cos}} = 1 - \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^N \frac{\mathbf{h}_{s,i}^\top \mathbf{h}_{t,i}}{\|\mathbf{h}_{s,i}\|_2 \|\mathbf{h}_{t,i}\|_2}\)$
  • Pillar 5 (Stiefel Manifold Orthogonality): $\(\mathcal{L}_{\text{Stiefel}} = \|\mathbf{A}^\top \mathbf{A} - \mathbf{I}\|_F^2 + \|\mathbf{B} \mathbf{B}^\top - \mathbf{I}\|_F^2\)$
  • Pillar 6 (Entropy Regularization): $\(\mathcal{L}_{\text{Entropy}} = \left| \mathcal{H}(\mathbf{p}_s) - \mathcal{H}(\mathbf{p}_t) \right|\)$

docs.title: 4. Implementation Blueprint: PiSSA & Trajectory Healing
docs.text:
# In neuralops/trainer/distillation/engine.py
# Offline Teacher Representation Streaming (0 MB Teacher GPU VRAM)
class CachedDistillationTrainer:
    def __init__(self, student_model, teacher_cache_path="/dev/shm/cached_teacher.pt", loss_weights=None):
        self.student = student_model
        # Teacher is NEVER loaded to GPU during student optimization!
        # Cached representations are memory-mapped / streamed from /dev/shm
        self.teacher_cache = torch.load(teacher_cache_path, map_location="cpu", weights_only=True)
        self.weights = loss_weights or {
            "kd": 1.0, "cka": 0.5, "attn": 0.2,
            "cos": 0.5, "stiefel": 0.05, "entropy": 0.1
        }

    def compute_step_loss(self, batch, batch_idx):
        # Retrieve precomputed teacher states from host cache
        cached_item = self.teacher_cache[batch_idx]
        t_logits = cached_item["logits"].to(self.student.device, non_blocking=True)
        t_hidden = cached_item["hidden_states"][-1].to(self.student.device, non_blocking=True)

        s_out = self.student(**batch, output_hidden_states=True)

        l_kd = compute_kd_loss(s_out.logits, t_logits, temperature=2.0)
        l_cka = compute_linear_cka(s_out.hidden_states[-1], t_hidden)
        l_cos = compute_cosine_loss(s_out.hidden_states[-1], t_hidden)
        l_stiefel = compute_stiefel_penalty(self.student)

        total = (self.weights["kd"] * l_kd +
                 self.weights["cka"] * l_cka +
                 self.weights["cos"] * l_cos +
                 self.weights["stiefel"] * l_stiefel)
        return total

docs.title: Real-Time Serving, Paged KV-Cache & Speculative Inference
docs.text: Assigned Subagent: Agent 08: High-Throughput Serving & Memory Architect Target Codebase Paths: - neuralops/serving/ - neuralops/serving/paged_kv_cache.py - neuralops/inference/ - neuralops/export/

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Design Philosophy
docs.text:
Autoregressive inference in large language models is severely memory-bandwidth bound. Naive implementations preallocate contiguous KV-cache tensors for max sequence lengths (\(T_{\text{max}} = 8192\)), resulting in up to \(80\%\) memory fragmentation and preventing concurrent multi-request serving.

Part 08 details the High-Throughput Serving Subsystem in neuralops/serving/. This engine provides: - PagedKVCache: Non-contiguous virtual memory paging (inspired by OS virtual memory and vLLM), allocating cache blocks dynamically in fixed-size chunks (e.g. 16 or 32 tokens). - Copy-on-Write (CoW): Zero-duplication beam search and parallel sampling branches. - Speculative Decoding Harness: Coupling a fast surgically compressed small model as a draft proposer with the uncompressed model as a verifier, achieving up to \(7\times\) end-to-end inference acceleration. - Unified Engine Export: SafeTensors, ONNX, and vLLM-compatible tensor layouts.

docs.title: 2. Assigned Subagent Responsibilities (Agent 08)
docs.text: Agent 08 is responsible for: 1. Zero-Fragmentation Cache Audit: Validating that PagedKVCache dynamically recycles expired token blocks without memory leakage. 2. Speculative Decoding Acceptance Math: Ensuring acceptance logic implements unbiased rejection sampling: $\(\alpha = \min\left(1, \frac{P_{\text{target}}(x)}{P_{\text{draft}}(x)}\right)\)$ 3. No Fake Artifact Policy: Strictly enforcing that export routines under neuralops/export/ produce 100% valid SafeTensors/ONNX files and raise explicit errors if serialization fails (banning empty placeholders). 4. vLLM Integration Contracts: Ensuring custom attention and compression layers expose standard forward_paged() signatures for plug-and-play vLLM block table routing.

docs.title: 3. Core Architecture of PagedKVCache
docs.text:
[Logical Sequence Tokens: 0 ... 47]
           │
           ▼
[Virtual Page Table Mapping]
   Block 0 (tokens 0-15)   ──► Physical Frame #4 (GPU SRAM/DRAM)
   Block 1 (tokens 16-31)  ──► Physical Frame #12
   Block 2 (tokens 32-47)  ──► Physical Frame #8
           │
           ▼
[Custom Paged-Attention Kernel]
   (Iterates through physical frames via block_tables tensor)

docs.title: 4. Implementation Details: Paged Cache Manager
docs.text:
# In neuralops/serving/paged_kv_cache.py
class PagedKVCacheManager:
    def __init__(self, num_blocks: int, block_size: int, num_heads: int, head_dim: int, dtype=torch.float16, device="cuda"):
        self.block_size = block_size
        self.free_blocks = list(range(num_blocks))
        # Contiguous physical memory pool
        self.k_cache = torch.empty((num_blocks, num_heads, block_size, head_dim), dtype=dtype, device=device)
        self.v_cache = torch.empty((num_blocks, num_heads, block_size, head_dim), dtype=dtype, device=device)
        self.block_tables = {} # seq_id -> list of block_ids

    def allocate_block(self, seq_id: str) -> int:
        if not self.free_blocks:
            raise MemoryError("Paged KV-Cache out of memory blocks")
        blk_id = self.free_blocks.pop(0)
        self.block_tables.setdefault(seq_id, []).append(blk_id)
        return blk_id

    def free_sequence(self, seq_id: str):
        if seq_id in self.block_tables:
            for blk_id in self.block_tables[seq_id]:
                self.free_blocks.append(blk_id)
            del self.block_tables[seq_id]

docs.title: Hardware Telemetry, Microbenchmarking & Roofline Engine
docs.text: Assigned Subagent: Agent 09: Telemetry & Hardware Roofline Profiler Target Codebase Paths: - neuralops/runners/monitor/ - neuralops/tracking/ - neuralops/analysis/ - neuralops/benchmarks/

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Design Philosophy
docs.text:
Asynchronous GPU kernel execution presents fundamental measurement pitfalls when using CPU wall-clock timers (time.time(), time.perf_counter()). The CPU launch queue decouples kernel submission from hardware execution on the streaming multiprocessors (SMs), dynamic GPU boost clocks introduce frequency variance across runs, and warm L2 cache lines distort microbenchmarking results. Furthermore, isolated latency metrics fail to diagnose why a kernel is bottlenecked—whether execution is throttled by high-bandwidth memory (HBM/GDDR6) transfer rates or Tensor Core arithmetic throughput.

Part 09 documents the Hardware Telemetry, Profiling & Roofline Subsystem of NeuralOps: 1. Asynchronous Microsecond Event Timing: Eliminates host-device queue skew via native torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), explicit stream synchronization (torch.cuda.synchronize()), warmup loops, and outlier-resistant statistical reduction (trimmed mean, median, standard deviation). 2. True Peak VRAM Instrumentation: Accurately tracks high-water memory footprints via torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() combined with cache purging (torch.cuda.empty_cache(), torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()), and non-intrusive NVML / nvidia-smi hardware sampling. 3. Empirical SM 8.9 Roofline Engine: Computes exact operational arithmetic intensity (\(I = \text{FLOPs} / \text{Bytes}\)) across all 131 attention mechanisms and 72 compression engines, mapping them relative to the \(317.9\,\text{FLOPs/Byte}\) hardware ridge inflection point on NVIDIA Ada Lovelace architectures (RTX 4070 SM 8.9 AD104 silicon). 4. Real-Time WebSocket & SSE Telemetry: Exposes high-frequency streaming telemetry over /ws/telemetry via FastAPI and ConnectionManager, broadcasting live GPU metrics, speculative decoding stats, and paged KV cache allocation maps. 5. Pluggable Experiment Tracking: Provides a unified facade (ExperimentTracker) supporting local JSONL logging, TensorBoard, Weights & Biases, and MLflow backends.

docs.title: 3.1 Asynchronous CUDA Event Synchronization Protocol
docs.text:
Implemented in neuralops/benchmarks/harness.py (BenchmarkRunner.measure_callable) and neuralops/analysis/roofline.py (profile_roofline):

# From neuralops/benchmarks/harness.py
def measure_callable(
    self,
    fn: Callable[[], Any],
    total_flops: float = 0.0,
    total_bytes: float = 0.0,
    batch_size: int = 1,
    seq_len: int = 1,
    warmup: Optional[int] = None,
    iters: Optional[int] = None,
) -> BenchmarkMetric:
    w_iters = warmup if warmup is not None else self.warmup_iters
    b_iters = iters if iters is not None else self.benchmark_iters

    self.reset_vram()

    # 1. Warmup Loop (stabilizes GPU clocks, compiles JIT kernels)
    for _ in range(w_iters):
        fn()

    if self.device.type == "cuda" and torch.cuda.is_available():
        # 2. Host-Device Stream Barrier
        torch.cuda.synchronize(self.device)
        self.reset_vram()

        # 3. Microsecond-Accurate Event Allocation
        start_events = [torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(b_iters)]
        end_events = [torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(b_iters)]

        # 4. Asynchronous Kernel Recording
        for i in range(b_iters):
            start_events[i].record()
            fn()
            end_events[i].record()

        # 5. Pipeline Barrier Synchronization
        torch.cuda.synchronize(self.device)
        latencies = [s.elapsed_time(e) for s, e in zip(start_events, end_events)]
    else:
        # High-resolution host fallback
        latencies = []
        for _ in range(b_iters):
            t0 = time.perf_counter()
            fn()
            t1 = time.perf_counter()
            latencies.append((t1 - t0) * 1000.0)

docs.title: 3.2 Robust Statistical Metrics
docs.text: To guarantee reproducible benchmarking unaffected by operating system interrupts or thermal throttling, latency samples are reduced into: - Trimmed Mean: Excluding top and bottom 10% outliers: $\(\mu_{10\%} = \frac{1}{N - 2k} \sum_{i=k+1}^{N-k} t_{(i)}\)$ - Median & Standard Deviation: Asserting coefficient of variation: $\(\frac{\sigma}{\mu} < 0.05 \quad (\text{less than } 5\% \text{ noise})\)$

Implemented in neuralops/benchmarks/harness.py and neuralops/runners/monitor/telemetry.py: - Pre-execution cleanup:

torch.cuda.empty_cache()
torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats(self.device)
