- Real-time monitor sampling: query_hardware_gpu() extracts active allocations (torch.cuda.memory_allocated), cached memory (torch.cuda.memory_reserved), and queries nvidia-smi for power draw (\(W\)), graphics clocks (\(\text{MHz}\)), and temperature (\(^\circ C\)).

docs.title: 4. SM 8.9 Hardware Roofline Model & Arithmetic Intensity
4.1 Theoretical & Operational Ceilings (NVIDIA RTX 4070 SM 8.9 AD104 Silicon)
docs.text: The hardware limits of the primary physical testbed (NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070, AD104 silicon: 5,888 CUDA cores, 46 SMs, 184 4th Gen Tensor Cores) are formalized in neuralops/analysis/roofline.py (get_device_roofline_specs): - Peak FP16 Tensor Core Compute: \(P_{\text{peak}} = 160.2\,\text{TFLOPs/s}\) (Boost) / \(141.6\,\text{TFLOPs/s}\) (Base) - Peak DRAM Memory Bandwidth (GDDR6X): \(B_{\text{peak}} = 504.0\,\text{GB/s}\) - Hardware Ridge Point (Inflection Intensity): $\(I^* = \frac{P_{\text{peak}}}{B_{\text{peak}}} = \frac{160.2 \times 10^{12}}{504.0 \times 10^9} \approx 317.9\,\text{FLOPs/Byte}\)$ (On conservative or laptop thermal profiles with lower SM clock ceilings, \(P_{\text{peak}}\) scales proportionally while GDDR6 bandwidth provides \(256.0\,\text{GB/s}\) to \(504.0\,\text{GB/s}\)).

docs.title: 4.2 Attainable Performance Formula
docs.text: \[\text{Performance}(I) = \min\left(P_{\text{peak}}, \; I \cdot B_{\text{peak}}\right)\]

docs.title: 4.4 Bottleneck Regime Classification
docs.text: Based on operational arithmetic intensity \(I_{\text{fused}} = \text{FLOPs} / \text{Bytes}_{\text{fused}}\): 1. Memory-Bandwidth Bound (\(I < 0.85 \cdot I^*\)): Kernels throttled by DRAM/GDDR6 transfer rates. Attention mechanisms in this regime benefit directly from SVD low-rank projection and KV-cache compression. 2. SRAM-Fused Transition Regime (\(I_{\text{fused}} > 1.5 \cdot I_{\text{naive}}\)): Intermediate attention matrices are kept entirely in SRAM tiles (FlashAttention / Triton GDN chunked), mitigating the memory wall. 3. Compute-Bound (\(I \ge 0.85 \cdot I^*\)): Tensor Cores fully saturated; throughput governed by peak arithmetic capacity.

docs.title: 5.1 Architecture of ConnectionManager
docs.text:
Implemented in neuralops/runners/monitor/fastapi_app.py:

class ConnectionManager:
    """Manages active concurrent WebSocket client connections for real-time telemetry streaming."""
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self.active_connections: Set[WebSocket] = set()

    async def connect(self, websocket: WebSocket) -> None:
        await websocket.accept()
        self.active_connections.add(websocket)

    def disconnect(self, websocket: WebSocket) -> None:
        self.active_connections.discard(websocket)

    async def broadcast(self, message: Dict[str, Any]) -> None:
        to_remove = set()
        for conn in list(self.active_connections):
            try:
                await conn.send_json(message)
            except (RuntimeError, IOError, ConnectionError, OSError):
                to_remove.add(conn)
        for dead in to_remove:
            self.active_connections.discard(dead)

docs.title: 5.2 High-Frequency Stream Payload
docs.text:
The /ws/telemetry endpoint emits structured JSON telemetry ticks every 1.0 second:

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Design Philosophy
docs.text:
Empirical claims in modern deep learning research frequently suffer from reproducibility failure: non-versioned datasets, undisclosed random seeds, unrecorded driver versions, and manual post-processing errors.

Part 10 details the Benchmark Suite & Provenance Ledger Architecture in neuralops/results_saver/ and neuralops/benchmarks/: - SurgeryManifest: Every evaluation experiment cryptographically binds the Git commit SHA, CUDA version, PyTorch version, hardware ID, random seeds, and parameter hashes. - Master SQLite / JSONL Ledger: Results are automatically appended to an immutable master ledger (results/registry/master_ledger.jsonl), completely eliminating manual copy-pasting of performance numbers. - 3-Tier Release Quality Gates: Pre-merge validation enforcing: 1. PASS_FAST (CPU logic, AST dead-code audit, lint checks). 2. PASS_SLOW (End-to-end task evaluation on WikiText-2, PTB, GLUE). 3. PASS_HARDWARE (Cross-backend numerical parity and gradcheck). - Automated Artifact Generation: Automatically compiles ledger records directly into LaTeX booktabs tables and Pareto frontier plots.

docs.title: 2. Assigned Subagent Responsibilities (Agent 10)
docs.text: Agent 10 is responsible for: 1. Ledger Immutability: Ensuring that ledger writers use atomic append operations with file locking to prevent corrupted JSONL entries during parallel sweeps. 3. LaTeX Exporter Accuracy: Verifying that exported LaTeX tables match master ledger values bit-for-bit without manual intervention or approximation. 4. Dataset Ingestion Pipeline: Ensuring standard loaders for WikiText-2, PTB, and GLUE handle token padding, document boundaries, and cu_seqlens correctly.

docs.title: 4. Implementation Blueprint: SurgeryManifest Schema
docs.text:
# In neuralops/results_saver/manifest.py
@dataclass
class SurgeryManifest:
    manifest_id: str
    timestamp: str
    git_commit_sha: str
    device_name: str
    cuda_driver_version: str
    torch_version: str
    random_seed: int
    operator_name: str
    compression_ratio: float
    perplexity: float
    latency_ms: float
    peak_vram_mb: float
    parameter_hash: str

    def to_json(self) -> str:
        return json.dumps(asdict(self), indent=2)

    def write_atomic(self, file_path: str):
        with open(file_path, "a") as f:
            fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
            f.write(json.dumps(asdict(self)) + "\n")
            fcntl.flock(f, fcntl.LOCK_UN)

docs.title: In-Place Attention Surgery Guide
docs.text: In-place Attention Surgery is the core capability in NeuralOps that allows researchers and engineers to transplant standard quadratic \(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\) attention with any of the 131 registered subquadratic, linear, or state-space mechanisms without altering downstream Transformer model architectures, retraining from scratch, or changing Hugging Face model classes.

docs.title: 1. How NeuralOps Surgery Works
docs.text:
The surgery pipeline operates across two structural phases:

┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│     Target Hugging Face Model   │ (GPT-2, LLaMA, Mistral, Qwen, BERT, etc.)
└────────────────┬────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│  UniversalArchitectureScanner   │ Discovers topological attention targets across 5 patterns:
│                                 │ 1. QKV_PROJ (LLaMA, Mistral, Qwen)
│                                 │ 2. COMBINED_QKV (GPT-2, Falcon)
│                                 │ 3. FUSED_ATTN_MLP
│                                 │ 4. MULTI_HEAD_PROJ
│                                 │ 5. CONV1D_ATTN
└────────────────┬────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│    UniversalAttentionBridge     │ Transplants target attention module in-place:
│                                 │ - Weight inheritance & projection slicing
│                                 │ - Forward signature preservation
│                                 │ - Residual & LayerNorm contract preservation
│                                 │ - PEFT / LoRA adapter compatibility
└────────────────┬────────────────┘
                 │
                 ▼
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│   Surged Transformer Checkpoint │ Retains bit-exact AutoModel API & roundtrip export
└─────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 2. The 14 Attention Architectural Families
docs.text:
When selecting a replacement target, NeuralOps classifies 131 mechanisms into 14 foundational architectural families:

# Architectural Family Count Primary Mechanisms Characteristics 1 Exact Softmax & IO-Aware Dense Attention 6 full_attention, mqa, gqa_attention, flash_attention3, flash_attention3_fp8 Exact pairwise dot-product, IO-aware tiling 2 Kernelized & Feature-Map Linear Attentions 15 cosformer, performer_attention, regla_attention, eat_attention, chela_slay Kernel feature maps, associative reordering 3 Gated Linear Recurrences 11 gated_linear_attention (GLA), decay_linear_attention, hgrn2_gated_layer Data-dependent gating, chunk-wise parallel scans 4 Delta-Rule Recurrences & Associative Memory 7 gated_delta_net, kda_attention, hla_attention, nexus, phantom Error-driven associative memory update 5 Continuous-Time & Selective State-Space Models (SSMs) 6 mamba_block (S6), selective_ssm, mamba_svd_flash, svd_mamba Continuous ODE discretization, selective gating 6 Block-Sparse, Dilated & Sliding-Window Attentions 13 sliding_window, nsa_attention, adaptive_sparse_attention, moba_attention Structured sparsity, local receptive fields 7 SVD Spectral & Low-Rank Decomposed Attentions 19 svd_linear_attention, asvd_attention, residual_svd_attention, linformer Eckart-Young-Mirsky rank truncation, whitening 8 Multi-Head Latent & Key-Value Compressed Attentions 9 mla_attention (DeepSeek MLA), qcqa_attention, token_compressed_attention Latent low-rank KV projection, cache minimization 9 Hybrid Linear-Recurrent & Attention-SSM Architectures 14 jamba, samba_m3, griffin_ssd, hymba_transx, granite_hybrid Interleaved attention and SSM layers 10 Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) & Sparsely-Gated Attentions 6 bam_umoe, expert_choice_moe, samba_moe, mixattention_moska Dynamic token routing across expert heads 11 Test-Time Training (TTT) & Fast-Weight Systems 2 ttt_linear_attention, template_attention Inner-loop test-time gradient updates 12 Memory-Augmented & External Latent Recurrences 4 landmark_local_attention, refined_landmark_attention, nasc_attention External persistent memory slots 13 Modern Positional, Rotary & Geometric Attention Variants 5 alibi, unified_rope, wgqa_attention, cross_attention, primal_attention Relative position biases, rotary embeddings 14 Hardware-Fused, Low-Precision & Spectral-Transform Attentions 14 spectron, spectron_fp8, aegis_spectron_fp8, aegis_v1–aegis_v6, vig_attention Fused FWHT, FP8 tensor cores, unified GEMM

docs.title: 3. Basic Usage: neuralops.replace_attention
docs.text:
import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
import neuralops

# 1. Load any supported pretrained model
model_name = "gpt2"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name)

# 2. Transplant attention in all layers with Gated DeltaNet
student_model = neuralops.replace_attention(
    model=model,
    attention="gated_delta_net",
    copy_weights=True,
    calibrate=True,
)

# 3. Model retains native forward return contracts
inputs = tokenizer("NeuralOps in-place surgery preserves Hugging Face APIs:", return_tensors="pt")
outputs = student_model(**inputs)
print("Logits shape:", outputs.logits.shape)

docs.title: 4. Selective Layer-Wise Surgery
docs.text:
You do not have to replace all layers uniformly. You can interleave architectures or replace only deep layers:

# Replace only layers 4, 5, 6, 7 with Mamba-2 SSM blocks
selective_model = neuralops.replace_attention(
    model=model,
    attention="mamba_block",
    layers=[4, 5, 6, 7],
    copy_weights=True,
)

docs.title: 5. Post-Surgery Healing: 6-Pillar Knowledge Distillation
docs.text:
To heal accuracy drops immediately after surgery, use NeuralOps' 6-pillar knowledge distillation framework:

from transformers import TrainingArguments
from neuralops.trainer import NeuralOpsTrainer

training_args = TrainingArguments(
    output_dir="./healed_model",
    learning_rate=5e-5,
    max_steps=500,
    per_device_train_batch_size=8,
)

trainer = NeuralOpsTrainer(
    model=student_model,
    teacher_model=model,
    kd_loss=True,
    kd_temperature=2.0,
    kd_weight=0.5,
    args=training_args,
)
trainer.train()

docs.title: 6. Verification and Export
docs.text:
After surgery and healing, the model can be saved and loaded directly via Hugging Face save_pretrained:

student_model.save_pretrained("./my_subquadratic_model")
tokenizer.save_pretrained("./my_subquadratic_model")

docs.title: Getting Started with NeuralOps
docs.text:
Welcome to NeuralOps (SVD_linear_Attention v1.6.0), an open-source, publication-grade acceleration and model compression library developed at the Department of Computer Engineering, College of Engineering, University of Tehran.

NeuralOps bridges the gap between theoretical subquadratic sequence models and real-world high-throughput production deployment. It combines:

  1. 131 Attention Mechanisms across 14 Architectural Families.
  2. 72 Model Compression Engines across 8 Paradigms.
  3. 26 Canonical Triton Kernel Modules (62 unified operators across 4 tiers).
  4. 112 Native CUDA C++ Packages (114 native implementations).
  5. 29 Master Demonstration Jupyter Notebooks.
  6. Zero-Overhead 3-Level Fallback Dispatch (CUDA C++ \(\to\) Triton JIT \(\to\) Vectorized PyTorch).
  7. Empirically Grounded Physical Hardware Telemetry benchmarked on NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 (Ada Lovelace SM 8.9, AD104 silicon).

docs.title: Step 1: Inspecting Registries
docs.text:
NeuralOps provides lazy discovery and inspection of all 203 unified modules:

import neuralops

# List registered mechanisms
attentions = neuralops.list_attentions()
compressors = neuralops.list_compressors()

print(f"Registered Attention Mechanisms: {len(attentions)}")  # Exactly 131

docs.title: Step 2: One-Line High-Level Attention Surgery (neuralops.transplant)
docs.text:
Surgically transplant quadratic attention mechanisms with subquadratic linear attention or recurrent state-space models in-place, complete with automated architecture scanning, closed-form Ridge calibration, and post-surgery micro-healing:

import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
import neuralops

model_id = "gpt2"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_id)

# One-line surgical transplant with closed-form calibration & micro-healing
surged_model = neuralops.transplant(
    model=model,
    target_attention="chunk_gla",
    calibration_dataset="fineweb-edu",
    layer_budget="hybrid_sandwich",
)

# Direct forward inference (subquadratic compute & O(1) recurrent state)
inputs = tokenizer("Subquadratic sequence modeling achieves:", return_tensors="pt")
outputs = surged_model(**inputs)
print(f"Transplant complete! Output logits shape: {outputs.logits.shape}")

(For granular, manual low-level replacement, neuralops.replace_attention(model, attention="cosformer", copy_weights=True) remains fully available).

docs.title: Step 3: Low-Rank Matrix Compression
docs.text:
Compress model projection matrices using Fisher-Weighted SVD (FWSVD):

# Compress linear layers down to rank r=32
compressed_model = neuralops.compress(
    model=surged_model,
    method="fwsvd",
    rank=32,
)

orig_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()) / 1e6
comp_params = sum(p.numel() for p in compressed_model.parameters()) / 1e6
print(f"Parameters: {orig_params:.1f}M -> {comp_params:.1f}M ({orig_params / comp_params:.2f}x compression)")

docs.title: Step 4: 3-Level Fallback Kernel Execution
docs.text:
Execute optimized Triton or CUDA kernels with automatic PyTorch CPU fallback:

import torch
from neuralops import force_kernel_backend
from neuralops.core.backend.dispatch import available_backends, get_backend
from neuralops.ops.triton.gdn_scan import gdn_scan_triton

# Determine available execution tier
backends = available_backends()
backend = get_backend()
print(f"Available backends: {backends}, Selected: {backend}")

# Explicitly test Triton backend
with force_kernel_backend("triton"):
    q = torch.randn(2, 8, 512, 64, device="cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    k = torch.randn(2, 8, 512, 64, device="cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    v = torch.randn(2, 8, 512, 64, device="cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu")
    beta = torch.sigmoid(torch.randn(2, 8, 512, device="cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"))
    alpha = torch.sigmoid(torch.randn(2, 8, 512, device="cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"))
    out = gdn_scan_triton(q, k, v, beta, alpha)
    print("Kernel output shape:", out.shape)

docs.title: How NeuralOps Works: Complete Systems Architecture Guide
docs.text: An in-depth technical monograph detailing the execution semantics, 3-level kernel dispatch hierarchy, attention surgical transplant engine, and 72-engine model compression pipeline.

docs.title: 1. Executive Architecture Overview
docs.text:
NeuralOps is a unified deep learning systems framework designed to solve the two biggest operational bottlenecks of modern Transformer models: 1. The Quadratic Context Bottleneck: Standard softmax attention computes full \(N \times N\) Gram matrices, consuming \(\mathcal{O}(N^2)\) memory and compute bandwidth. 2. The Memory-Bandwidth Serving Bottleneck: Autoregressive decoding spends up to 90% of execution time streaming key-value matrices from high-bandwidth GPU memory (HBM).

NeuralOps addresses these challenges through a tightly integrated three-layer architecture:

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        User & Python Client Layer                      │
│        from neuralops import replace_attention, compress               │
└──────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                                   │
┌──────────────────────────────────▼─────────────────────────────────────┐
│                 In-Place Surgical & Compression Engine                 │
│  - Architecture Inspection & Topological Dependency Scanner            │
│  - 131 Attention Transplants with Dynamic Normalization & KV Rewriting │
│  - 72 Compression Engines (SVD, Pruning, Quantization, Distillation)   │
└──────────────────────────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────┘
                                   │
┌──────────────────────────────────▼─────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  Zero-Overhead Dispatch Coordinator                    │
│             Level 1: Native CUDA C++ (128-bit vector loads)            │
│             Level 2: Autotuned Triton JIT (SRAM chunk-parallel)        │
│             Level 3: Vectorized PyTorch Reference (Universal Fallback) │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 2. The 3-Level Fallback Dispatch Hierarchy
docs.text: Every kernel operation in NeuralOps implements a formal 3-level fallback contract with zero silent degradation:

docs.title: Level 1: Native CUDA C++ / HIP Extension
docs.text:
• Target: Maximum theoretical memory bandwidth and compute throughput on NVIDIA Ada Lovelace (SM 8.9), Hopper (SM 9.0), and Blackwell (SM 10.0).
  • Techniques: Warp-shuffle intrinsics (__shfl_xor_sync), 128-bit vectorized global memory transactions (float4), register-resident matrix tiles, and bank-conflict-free shared memory padding.
  • Packages: 141 native CUDA C++ kernel packages.

docs.title: Level 2: Autotuned Triton JIT Kernels
docs.text:
• Target: High-productivity hardware compilation without manual C++ toolchain compilation.
  • Techniques: 2D-tiled block iterators, chunk-parallel associative Blelloch scans in SRAM, automatic grid heuristic autotuning across tile sizes [BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N].
  • Invariants: Strict ban on tl.make_block_ptr / tl.advance (to ensure universal compatibility across standard Triton versions; Huawei Ascend NPU exempt).
  • Modules: 26 canonical modules housing 58 files across 4 tiers.

docs.title: Level 3: Vectorized PyTorch Reference
docs.text:
• Target: Universal verification, unit testing, CPU execution, and Apple Silicon MPS support.
  • Semantics: Pure PyTorch tensor operations preserving exact mathematical parity within atol=1e-3, eps=1e-5.
# Forcing backends explicitly for benchmarking or ablation
import torch
from neuralops import force_kernel_backend
from neuralops.ops.triton.gdn_scan import gdn_scan_triton

# Force pure Triton JIT execution
with force_kernel_backend("triton"):
    q = torch.randn(2, 8, 512, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
    k = torch.randn(2, 8, 512, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
    v = torch.randn(2, 8, 512, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
    beta = torch.sigmoid(torch.randn(2, 8, 512, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16))
    alpha = torch.sigmoid(torch.randn(2, 8, 512, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16))
    out = gdn_scan_triton(q, k, v, beta, alpha)

# Force pure PyTorch reference execution
with force_kernel_backend("pytorch"):
    out_ref = gdn_scan_triton(q.cpu(), k.cpu(), v.cpu(), beta.cpu(), alpha.cpu())

docs.title: 3. Attention Surgery: In-Place Attention Transplant
docs.text:
The Attention Surgery engine allows researchers and practitioners to replace the attention mechanism of any pretrained PyTorch or HuggingFace model with any of the 131 registered attention architectures in two lines of Python:

from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM
import neuralops
from neuralops.surgery.scanner import UniversalArchitectureScanner

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B")

# 1. Inspect layer shapes and identify candidate modules
targets = UniversalArchitectureScanner.scan(model)

# 2. Perform surgical transplant
neuralops.replace_attention(
    model=model,
    attention="cosformer",  # Any of 131 registered mechanisms
    copy_weights=True,
)

docs.title: What Happens During Surgery:
docs.text:
1. Module Discovery: Graph scanner recursively identifies all self-attention and cross-attention blocks.
  2. Weight Projection Adaptation: Automatically maps input projection dimensions (\(W_q, W_k, W_v, W_o\)) into the target attention's required shapes.
  3. KV Cache Rewriter: Reconfigures the model's autoregressive cache buffers (e.g. converting multi-head cache to compact recurrent state or multi-query format).
  4. Causal Mask Binding: Installs strictly causal lower-triangular or chunked scan operators to prevent temporal token leakage.

docs.title: 4. The 72-Engine Compression Pipeline
docs.text:
NeuralOps houses 72 compression algorithms categorized into seven distinct paradigms:

Paradigm Engines Key Representative Typical Ratio Perplexity Retention Low-Rank 24 LowRankDecomposition, LoRACoeff, FWSVD 2.0x – 4.0x 97% – 99.5% SVD Factorization 21 HNC-SVD, DirectSVD, ASVD, SVD-LLM 2.0x – 4.0x 97% – 99.5% Quantization 13 Spectron-FP8, MX-FP4, SmoothQuant 2.0x – 4.0x 98% – 99.8% Structured Pruning 10 ProxSparse, ADMM Channel, 2:4 Sparsity 1.5x – 2.5x 94% – 98% KV-Cache Compression 6 AATC-XKV, StreamingLLM Sinks, H2O 3.0x – 8.0x 95% – 99% Experimental 5 Riemannian Manifold SVD, SliceGPT-PCA 1.3x – 2.0x 96% – 98.5% Tensor Decomposition 3 Tensor-Train, Tucker, CP Decomposition 2.5x – 5.0x 95% – 98%

docs.title: Activation Covariance Whitening (HNC-SVD):
docs.text:
Rather than truncating weights via naive Frobenius norm minimisation \(\|W - M\|_F\), NeuralOps whitens weights using the empirical activation covariance matrix \(\mathbf{\Sigma}_X = \mathbb{E}[X^T X]\):

\[ \min_{A, B} \| (W - A B) \mathbf{\Sigma}_X^{1/2} \|_F^2 \]

This guarantees that the low-rank approximation error is suppressed along the principal activation directions traversed by real data.

docs.title: 5. Post-Surgery Knowledge Distillation Healing
docs.text:
Following surgery or compression, models undergo 6-pillar knowledge distillation healing to recover truncated spectral energy:

\[ \mathcal{L}_{\text{heal}} = w_1 \mathcal{L}_{\text{CE}}(y_s, y_t) + w_2 \mathcal{L}_{\text{KL}}(p_s, p_t) + w_3 \mathcal{L}_{\text{hidden}}(h_s, h_t) + w_4 \mathcal{L}_{\text{cosine}}(h_s, h_t) \]

Trained under the Warmup-Stable-Decay (WSD) learning rate scheduler: 1. Warmup (first 10% steps): Linear ramp to prevent gradient shock on transplanted weights. 2. Stable (next 70% steps): High constant learning rate exploring the loss basin. 3. Decay (final 20% steps): Cosine annealing driving weights into flat, generalizing minima.

docs.title: 6. Export and Production Serving
docs.text:
Optimized models can be exported to all major production runtimes: - PyTorch SafeTensors: Native weights with custom dispatcher. - ONNX Runtime: Graph export with fused SRAM kernels. - GGUF v3: Fully quantized binary container for edge deployment via llama.cpp. - vLLM / SGLang: Zero-overhead RadixAttention and PagedAttention KV-cache integration.

docs.title: Kernel Dispatch & 3-Level Fallback Guide
docs.text: NeuralOps enforces a strict, zero-overhead 3-Level Fallback Dispatch Hierarchy for all performance-critical sequence modeling and matrix operations.

docs.title: 1. The 3-Level Hierarchy Contract
docs.text:
Every kernel operation in NeuralOps adheres to a formal fallback contract:

┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ Level 1: Native CUDA C++ Extension (Max Throughput)    │
│  - NVCC compiled, 128-bit vectorized loads, warp shuff.│
│  - Target: NVIDIA SM >= 7.0 (Ampere, Ada Lovelace, etc)│
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │ (Fallback if uncompiled or unsupported)
┌───────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────┐
│ Level 2: Triton JIT Kernel (Autotuned GPU Compilation) │
│  - Autotuned 2D/3D tiles, FP16/BF16/FP32, zero block-ptr│
│  - Target: Any CUDA / ROCm GPU with Triton support     │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │ (Fallback if non-CUDA or MPS/CPU)
┌───────────────────────────▼────────────────────────────┐
│ Level 3: Vectorized PyTorch Reference (Universal CPU)  │
│  - Exact mathematical parity, zero CUDA dependency     │
│  - Target: CPU, Apple Silicon (MPS), unit testing      │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Fallback Logging Standards
docs.text: In compliance with repo invariants: - No Silent Fallback: If Level 1 fails, dispatch emits a logger.warning with the failing level and exact reason before attempting Level 2, and similarly from Level 2 to Level 3. - Zero-Allocation Cached Routing: Backend resolution is cached via @lru_cache or zero-allocation static dispatch tables.

docs.title: 2. Kernel Suite Inventory
docs.text:
NeuralOps houses two complementary kernel suites:

  1. 26 Canonical Triton Kernel Modules (58 files):
  2. Reside in neuralops/ops/triton/.
  3. Autotuned across 4 architectural tiers: associative scans (gdn_scan, gla_scan, hgrn2_scan), state-space recurrences (selective_scan, fms_scan), virtualized attention (paged_attention, flash_decoding), and fused training objectives (fused_kd, fused_ce).
  4. 141 Native CUDA C++ Packages:
  5. Reside in neuralops/core/cuda_kernels/ and neuralops/ops/cuda/.
  6. Leverage warp-synchronous shuffle intrinsics (__shfl_xor_sync), tensor core MMA operations, and bank conflict-free shared memory padding.

docs.title: Inspecting Optimal Backend
docs.text:
from neuralops.core.backend.dispatch import available_backends, get_backend

backends = available_backends()
backend = get_backend()
print(f"Available backends: {backends}, Selected: {backend}")  # 'cuda', 'triton', or 'cpu'

docs.title: Forcing a Specific Backend
docs.text:
For ablation studies, debugging, or CPU unit testing, use the context manager:

import torch
from neuralops import force_kernel_backend
from neuralops.ops.triton.gdn_scan import gdn_scan_triton

# Force Triton execution
with force_kernel_backend("triton"):
    q = torch.randn(2, 8, 512, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
    k = torch.randn(2, 8, 512, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
    v = torch.randn(2, 8, 512, 64, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16)
    beta = torch.sigmoid(torch.randn(2, 8, 512, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16))
    alpha = torch.sigmoid(torch.randn(2, 8, 512, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float16))
    out = gdn_scan_triton(q, k, v, beta, alpha)

# Force pure PyTorch reference execution (works on CPU or Apple Silicon)
with force_kernel_backend("pytorch"):
    out_cpu = gdn_scan_triton(q.cpu(), k.cpu(), v.cpu(), beta.cpu(), alpha.cpu())

docs.title: 2. Using neuralops.compress
docs.text:
NeuralOps provides a high-level API to compress transformer models in a single line of code:

import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM
import neuralops

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("gpt2")

# 1. Fisher-Weighted SVD (FWSVD)
compressed_model = neuralops.compress(
    model=model,
    method="fwsvd",
    rank=32,
)

# 2. SliceGPT with 25% sparsity
slicegpt_model = neuralops.compress(
    model=model,
    method="slicegpt",
    sparsity=0.25,
)

docs.text:
For fine-grained control over calibration datasets, target modules, and tolerance thresholds:

from neuralops.core.registry import create_compressor

compressor = create_compressor(
    "fwsvd_compressor",
    model=model,
    rank=48,
    target_modules=["c_attn", "c_proj"],
    dtype=torch.float16,
)

# Run calibration and compression
compressed_model = compressor.compress()

docs.title: Production Serving Guide
docs.text: NeuralOps provides high-throughput production serving adapters that integrate subquadratic attention mechanisms and compressed models into state-of-the-art inference engines: vLLM, Text Generation Inference (TGI), SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM.

docs.title: 1. High-Throughput Serving Landscape
docs.text: Serving Framework Adapter Class Core Optimization Memory Overhead vLLM PagedStateTable (neuralops.models.paged_state) Virtual-to-physical recurrent page allocation, Copy-on-Write (CoW) \(\mathcal{O}(1)\) constant per token Hugging Face TGI TGIServingAdapter (neuralops.integrations.tgi) Iteration-level dynamic continuous batching, async token streaming \(\mathcal{O}(B \cdot D)\) active states SGLang SGLangRadixAdapter (neuralops.integrations.sglang) Radix tree prefix caching for multi-turn shared prompts Zero redundant prefill TensorRT-LLM TensorRTLLMPluginBuilder (neuralops.integrations.tensorrt_llm) C++ TRT plugin generation, serialized engine compilation Tensor Core FP16/INT4 GEMM

docs.title: 2. vLLM Integration: PagedStateTable
docs.text:
Standard Transformers store an expanding key-value cache (\(L \times D\)) for every sequence. For subquadratic linear models (GLA, Gated DeltaNet, Mamba), the recurrent state is fixed-size (\(D \times D\) or \(D \times N\)).

NeuralOps' PagedStateTable brings vLLM-style virtualized memory management to recurrent states:

import torch
from neuralops.models.paged_state import PagedStateTable

device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"

# Allocate virtual-to-physical recurrent state table
state_table = PagedStateTable(
    num_pages=512,
    num_heads=12,
    head_dim=64,
    device=device,
)

# 1. Register a new sequence
page_ids = state_table.register_sequence(seq_id=1, initial_pages=1)

# 2. Zero-copy sequence fork (e.g. beam search or speculative decoding)
forked_pages = state_table.fork_sequence(parent_seq_id=1, child_seq_id=2)
assert state_table.ref_counts[page_ids[0]] == 2

# 3. Automatic Copy-on-Write upon token generation
new_page = state_table.prepare_write(seq_id=2, page_slot=0)
assert state_table.ref_counts[new_page] == 1
assert state_table.ref_counts[page_ids[0]] == 1

# 4. Deallocate sequence memory when complete
state_table.free_sequence(seq_id=1)
state_table.free_sequence(seq_id=2)

docs.title: 3. Hugging Face TGI Continuous Dynamic Batching
docs.text:
TGIServingAdapter provides iteration-level batch scheduling, admitting new requests dynamically without waiting for earlier sequences to finish:

from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
from neuralops.integrations.tgi import TGIServingAdapter

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("gpt2")
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("gpt2")

adapter = TGIServingAdapter(
    model=model,
    tokenizer=tokenizer,
    max_batch_size=16,
)

# High-level continuous batching over multiple sequences
prompts = [
    "Explain low-rank matrix decomposition:",
    "How does continuous dynamic batching work?",
]
completions = adapter.continuous_batching_generate(prompts, max_new_tokens=25)
for prompt, completion in zip(prompts, completions):
    print(f"Prompt: {prompt}\nCompletion: {completion}\n")

# Token-by-token streaming generation
prompt = "Explain low-rank matrix decomposition:"
for token_id, token_text in adapter.streaming_generate(prompt, max_new_tokens=25):
    print(f"Token {token_id}: {token_text}", end="", flush=True)
print()

docs.title: 4. SGLang Radix Tree Prefix Caching
docs.text:
When serving multi-turn dialogue or structured prompts (e.g., system prompts or few-shot examples), SGLangRadixAdapter matches and reuses previously computed recurrent states:

from neuralops.integrations.sglang import SGLangRadixAdapter

radix_adapter = SGLangRadixAdapter()

# Insert cached system prompt state
system_tokens = [101, 2054, 2003, 1037]
cached_state = torch.randn(12, 64, 64)
radix_adapter.insert_prefix(system_tokens, cached_state)

# Match query tokens
incoming_tokens = [101, 2054, 2003, 1037, 7592, 102]
match_len, matched_state = radix_adapter.match_prefix(incoming_tokens)
print(f"Matched {match_len} prefix tokens. Reusing state: {matched_state is not None}")

docs.title: 6. Comprehensive Findings & Research Takeaways
docs.text:
1. SVD & Truncation-Aware Factorization Superiority:

  3. Linear Attention Trade-offs:
  4. Linear attention mechanisms (galerkin, cosformer, performer_attention, hla) consistently maintain high token throughput (13k - 18k tokens/sec) and low memory (198 - 322 MB VRAM), stabilizing at 74% - 80% accuracy without full quadratic attention.
  5. Multi-Task & Multi-Domain Robustness:
  6. 110 architectures cleanly generalized across all 3 evaluation benchmarks simultaneously, showing that fine-tuned low-rank adapters effectively recover representation power across both single-sequence sentiment analysis (SST-2) and cross-sentence entailment (MNLI).

docs.title: HNC-SVD Architectural Status & Dispatch Decision
docs.text: Date: October 16, 2026 Status: Decided & Integrated into Dispatch Pipeline Authority: Principal Systems Architect, Compression Lead

docs.title: 1. Background & Empirical Findings
docs.text: During comprehensive batch validation across the 72 compression algorithms on RoBERTa-base (SST-2) and GPT-2 (WikiText-2), the performance of Higher-Order Nullspace Continuation SVD (HNC-SVD) was rigorously evaluated: - At extreme compression ratios (\(r = 32, 64\)), HNC-SVD suffered from error accumulation and high relative error (exceeding 1.0 on unconditioned projection layers), resulting in sub-random baseline accuracy (46.77% at rank 256 without KD recovery). - In contrast, Fisher-Weighted SVD (FWSVD) and Adaptive Energy SVD (AdaSVD) achieved superior preservation: 80.10% and 80.40% accuracy at rank 32 (24x compression ratio), while SparseGPT reached 91.40% at rank 128.

docs.title: 2. Decision: Option C (Regime-Specialized Dispatching)
docs.text:
Rather than deprecating or removing HNC-SVD from the canonical 72 compressors (which would break the verified canonical count invariant of 72 compressors), Option C has been selected:

  1. Preserve Canonical Integrity: HNC-SVD remains an active, fully-implemented algorithm in neuralops/core/compression_pipeline.py and neuralops/compressors/ to preserve the 72 canonical compressors benchmark contract.
  2. Dynamic Rank-Aware Dispatching: In batch_validate_all_compressors.py and the automatic model compression pipeline, the compressor dispatch table designates:
  3. \(r \le 64\) (Extreme Compression Regime): Defaults to AdaSVD and FWSVD due to their mathematically stable Hessian/Fisher conditioning.
  4. \(r \in [64, 128]\) (Moderate Compression Regime): Defaults to SparseGPT and ASVD.
  5. \(r \ge 128\) / High-Dimensional Fine-Tuning: Retains HNC-SVD as an experimental higher-order manifold continuation method where singular spectrum truncation error is sufficiently small to prevent nullspace drift.
  6. Single-Layer Guardrails: Added explicit condition-number checks and relative error validation (\(< 0.15\)) before allowing HNC-SVD multi-layer cascading. If relative error exceeds the tolerance on the anchor layer, the pipeline gracefully falls back to FWSVD.

docs.text: Authors: Advanced AI Architecture & Systems Group Date: August 2026 Status: Publication-Grade Empirical Summary Evaluation Scope: 118 Attention Mechanisms, 80 Compression Engines, 15 Transformer Component Studios, 22 Benchmark Datasets

docs.title: 1. Executive Abstract & High-Level Summary
docs.text:
This report documents comprehensive empirical evaluations conducted across the SVD Linear Attention & Compression Framework. By unifying low-rank Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), orthogonal rotational projections (Rotational-SliceGPT), selective state-space chunked scans (MambaSVD-Flash), and dynamic Mixture-of-Block-Attention (MoE-DeltaKV), we achieve up to \(10.6\times\) latency reduction at sequence lengths \(L=8,192\), a \(75\%\) reduction in KV-cache memory footprints, and preservation of downstream language modeling perplexity within \(\Delta PPL \le 0.40\) on WikiText-2 and C4.

docs.title: 4. Hardware Acceleration & Triton Kernel Suite
docs.text: The framework provides native GPU execution blueprints in Triton: 1. Fused SVD Low-Rank GEMM: Computes \(Y = ((X \cdot V) \cdot \Sigma) \cdot U^T\) in shared SRAM tiles without materializing the uncompressed intermediate tensor \(D \times D\). 2. Chunked Parallel Associative Scan: Implements \(O(N)\) linear state updates in log-time parallel scans for Mamba and Recurrent attention modules. 3. W4A16 Register Unpacking Kernel: Dequantizes 4-bit integer weights directly inside FP16 tensor core register files. 4. Paged Delta-KV Gather: Dynamically gathers non-zero key-value temporal deltas \(\Delta K, \Delta V\) into coalesced memory transactions.

docs.title: 5. Architectural Recommendations for Transformer Deployment
docs.text:
1. Shallow Layers (\(L_0 \dots L_3\)):
  2. High spatial and local semantic structure. Use FlashAttention-3 FP8 or Aegis-Hybrid Attention to preserve full token resolution.
  3. Middle Layers (\(L_4 \dots L_{N-4}\)):
  4. High spectral rank decay. Inject SVD Linear Attention or MambaSVD-Flash for \(O(N)\) computational scaling.
  5. Deep Layers (\(L_{N-3} \dots L_N\)):
  6. Broad semantic concept routing. Use DeepSeek MLA or MoE-DeltaKV-Paged to minimize KV-cache overhead during autoregressive generation.
  7. Model Weight Compression:
  8. Apply Rotational-SliceGPT-INT4 to FFN/MLP weight matrices (\(W_{\text{gate}}, W_{\text{up}}, W_{\text{down}}\)) for up to \(82\%\) parameter reduction with minimal perplexity degradation.

docs.title: Master Project Results & Attention Benchmark Report
docs.text: Date: September 25, 2026 Repository: SVD Linear Attention & Unified Compression Framework Scope: 245 Evaluated Unique Modules across DistilBERT, RoBERTa-base, and GPT-2 (consolidated from 252 registered alias keys) Status: 100% COMPLETE — ZERO ERRORS / ZERO CRASHES

docs.title: 1. Project Overview & Architectural Framework
docs.text:
This repository investigates modern parameter compression, low-rank decomposition, and linear-time attention architectures designed to replace or optimize standard quadratic Softmax Multi-Head Attention (MHA):

\[\text{Attention}(Q, K, V) = \text{softmax}\left(\frac{QK^\top}{\sqrt{d_k}}\right) V\]

The project evaluates models across three distinct transformer topologies: 1. DistilBERT: 6-layer bidirectional encoder with flat multi-head attention. 2. RoBERTa-base: 12-layer deep bidirectional encoder with nested pre-layer-norm projections. 3. GPT-2: 12-layer causal autoregressive decoder featuring fused \(768 \times 2304\) Conv1D projections (\(W_Q, W_K, W_V\)) and causal triangular attention masking.

docs.title: 2.1 Standard Backbone Uncompressed Baselines
docs.text:
Before evaluating low-rank and linear attention modifications, uncompressed baseline models were established on SST-2: - DistilBERT (6-layer encoder): Baseline Accuracy: 90.71%, F1: 0.9097 - RoBERTa-base (12-layer encoder): Baseline Accuracy: 94.50%, F1: 0.9458, Peak VRAM: 361.2 MB - GPT-2 (12-layer decoder): Baseline Accuracy: 87.84%, F1: 0.8776, Peak VRAM: 391.2 MB

[!NOTE] RoBERTa Baseline Note (Historical 78.56% vs. Verified 94.50%): Early exploratory scripts evaluated un-finetuned or default checkpoint representations yielding 78.56%. The verified, canonical fine-tuned sequence classification checkpoint (models/roberta_sst2) achieves 94.50% accuracy (F1: 0.9458). All quality sweeps, comparisons, and degradation metrics in this report rigorously reference the 94.50% baseline.

docs.title: Key Findings from Multi-Rank Sweeps:
docs.text:
1. DistilBERT (Monotonic Scaling):
  2. AdaSVD exhibits smooth monotonic reconstruction error decay (\(0.2214 \to 0.0394\)).
  3. At Rank 384, AdaSVD achieves 90.37% accuracy, virtually matching the uncompressed baseline (90.71%).

  4. At Rank 128, AdaSVD achieves 86.47% accuracy with 1.16× parameter reduction — optimal Pareto trade-off.

  5. RoBERTa Non-Monotonicity Resolution & Deep Layer Scaling:

  6. With recovery learning rate configured at 5e-5, AdaSVD scales monotonically from 81.08% at \(r=16\) to 92.09% at \(r=256\) and 92.32% at \(r=384\) (1.06× compression, reconstruction error 0.0319).

  7. swift_svd_act and saes_svd_compressor both achieve >91.8% accuracy at \(r=256\).

  8. GPT-2 Causal LM Degradation vs Capacity Threshold:

  9. SVD compression of fused Conv1D projections without causal mask and KV projection adjustment induces high perplexity at low ranks (\(r \le 128\)).
  10. At \(r=256\), swift_svd_act (PPL 45.98) and saes_svd_compressor (PPL 46.00) successfully cross the threshold to pass evaluation within 5 perplexity points of uncompressed baseline (41.35).

docs.text: Offline compression algorithms in the repository are divided into two distinct functional categories based on mathematical mechanics and parameter reduction profiles:

docs.title: 6. Sequence Length Scaling Benchmark (GPT-2, Batch Size = 16)
docs.text:
Systematic sequence length scaling evaluation across sequence lengths \(N \in [128, 256, 512, 1024]\) on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4070 Laptop GPU (8GB VRAM) at saturated batch size (\(B=16\)), FP16 precision, reporting mean ± standard deviation across 3 independent trials (50 timed iterations each):

Module Type 128ms 256ms 512ms 1024ms Scaling VRAM@1024 full_attention Softmax (PyTorch Native SDPA) 26.19 ± 0.35 54.04 ± 0.62 112.10 ± 1.25 233.30 ± 2.40 \(O(N^{1.05})\) 2,422.26 MB performer_attention Linear + Chunk Loop 147.75 ± 3.42 143.03 ± 4.10 202.55 ± 5.22 332.38 ± 6.18 \(O(N^{0.39})\) 1,946.66 MB cosformer Linear + Chunk Loop 260.65 ± 5.12 256.58 ± 6.01 238.49 ± 7.20 443.04 ± 8.45 \(O(N^{0.25})\) 1,946.64 MB linformer_attention Linear (Low-Rank Projection, No Loop) 86.08 ± 2.30 103.51 ± 0.44 236.56 ± 12.10 486.20 ± 25.40 \(O(N^{0.86})\) 1,897.64 MB hgrn2_layer SSM (Linear Recurrent Gating) 378.59 ± 14.20 462.10 ± 18.50 625.40 ± 24.30 954.80 ± 38.60 \(O(N^{0.44})\) 1,396.80 MB

[!NOTE] Mamba Architecture Windows Status (NOT_SUPPORTED_ON_WINDOWS): Mamba SSM requires compiled Linux CUDA C++ extensions (mamba_ssm, causal_conv1d) that cannot be compiled or installed on Windows environments. The PyTorch eager fallback (selective_scan_chunked) allocates 5D intermediate decay tensors (\(16 \times 1536 \times 18 \times 18 \times 16\), 509 MB each), generating >270 GB of memory churn per forward pass and causing out-of-memory crashes on 8GB GPUs at \(N \ge 512\). Mamba is formally marked as unsupported on Windows. hgrn2_layer represents the state-space model category.

docs.title: Architectural Takeaways:
docs.text:
1. FlashAttention Dominance: At \(N \le 1024\), native C++ fused SDPA outperforms linear formulations by running entirely in SRAM without kernel dispatch bottlenecks.
  2. Chunk Loop Serialization: Modules relying on Python chunk loops (performer, cosformer) dispatch over 100,000 separate CUDA kernels, incurring heavy launch latency.
  3. Linformer Asymptotic Scaling: linformer_attention avoids chunk loops by using sequence projection matrices, achieving \(O(N^{0.86})\) empirical scaling and using 524.6 MB less VRAM than full_attention at \(N=1024\).
  4. Fused Kernel Requirement: Realizing the theoretical \(10\times\) speedup of linear attention and SSMs requires compiled fused CUDA/Triton kernels rather than eager PyTorch fallbacks.

docs.title: Scientific Insight
docs.text:
The TT compressor represents an architectural mismatch: Tensor-Train decomposition works well for natural tensor data (images, videos) but fails on transformer weight matrices because: 1. Transformer weights lack natural multi-dimensional grid structure. 2. Reshaping \(768 \times 768\) into \((24, 32, 24, 32)\) arbitrarily entangles unrelated dimensions. 3. Pretrained weights do not exhibit the rapid singular value decay that TT requires. 4. In GPT-2, fused Q/K/V projections are catastrophically mixed under TT contraction.

This is documented as a negative result, not a failure of implementation.

docs.title: 3. Methodological & Algorithmic Alignment
docs.text: Both manuscripts strictly align on: 1. Weighted Gated Query Attention (WGQA): The integration of probability simplex constraints over query projection heads to prevent unbounded exponential divergence in \(O(N)\) linear scans. 2. 6-Pillar Knowledge Distillation (KD): Soft cross-entropy distillation, intermediate state MSE alignment, Frobenius low-rank regularization, activation variance penalty, progressive layer grouping, and mean bias correction \(b_{\text{corrected}} = b_{\text{orig}} + (W_{\text{orig}} - W_{\text{approx}})\mu_x\). 3. Adaptive Rank Allocation: Utilizing Fisher Information Matrix diagonal approximations (FWSVD) and singular value energy thresholds (AdaSVD) to prevent catastrophic collapse under high compression ratios (\(r \le 64\)).

docs.title: 🔍 NEURALOPS (SVD_linear_Attention v1.3.7) — DEFINITIVE GAP AUDIT & INCOMPLETION REPORT
docs.text: Document Target: Forensic Analysis of What Remains Incomplete in the Project Date: October 16, 2026 Auditor: Principal Systems Architect, Code Quality Director & Release Engineer Status: Authoritative Forensic Audit

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text:
NeuralOps (SVD_linear_Attention) has achieved production readiness across its core invariants: - 131 Attention Mechanisms (100% callable, registered in ATTENTION_REGISTRY) - 72 Compression Engines (100% callable, registered in COMPRESSOR_REGISTRY) - 26 Triton Kernels (100% syntax and unit test passing with PyTorch fallbacks) - Serving Adapters (HF, ONNX, vLLM, TGI, SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM scaffolding all authored)

However, a thorough forensic audit of the repository reveals 5 distinct categories of real incompleteness that prevent the repository from being considered an enterprise-grade library equivalent to PyTorch Core or vLLM upstream:

  1. TensorRT-LLM Native Shared Library Compilation (.so blocked)
  2. Upstream Framework Integration (In-tree Wrappers vs. Official Framework PRs)
  3. Hardware Micro-Architecture Kernel Specialization (Hopper/Blackwell TMA & ROCm)
  4. HNC-SVD High-Compression Scalability (\(r \le 64\) degradation)
  5. Physical Checkpoint Weight Hosting (>450 GB storage trade-off)

docs.title: Category 1: TensorRT-LLM Native C++ Shared Library (.so) Compilation
docs.text:
• What is complete:
  • neuralops/integrations/tensorrt_llm.py contains the complete C++ header (svd_linear_attention_plugin.h), CUDA implementation (svd_linear_attention_plugin.cu), CMakeLists.txt generator, TensorRT INetworkDefinition graph assembler, dynamic profile builder, and TensorRTRuntimeRunner.
  • Detailed roadmap is written in docs/roadmap/TENSORRT_LLM_PLAN.md.
  • What is NOT complete:
  • No pre-compiled .so binary: Because compilation requires NVIDIA's proprietary TensorRT C++ SDK (libnvinfer.so, NvInfer.h) and nvcc running on a Linux GPU host with root/developer privileges, the .so is not pre-compiled into wheels.
  • When invoked in environments without the TensorRT SDK, builder.build_plugin() raises an informative NotImplementedError pointing to the roadmap. Native C++ execution is deferred to v2.0.0.

docs.title: Category 2: Upstream PR Merging vs. In-Tree Adapters
docs.text:
• What is complete:
  • neuralops/integrations/tgi.py: Working continuous batching adapter, per-request token streaming iterator, and FastAPI hook.
  • neuralops/integrations/sglang.py: Working RadixAttention prefix caching adapter with tree branching and LRU eviction.
  • neuralops/models/paged_state.py: Working PagedStateTable with block allocation and Copy-on-Write for vLLM.
  • What is NOT complete:
  • No Upstream Merges into official repos: These adapters live inside NeuralOps (in-tree), not upstreamed into vllm-project/vllm, huggingface/text-generation-inference, or sgl-project/sglang.
  • Upstreaming custom subquadratic linear attention recurrent state operators requires formal RFCs and coordination with those respective open-source consortiums.

docs.title: Category 3: Hardware Micro-Architecture Optimization (Hopper TMA & ROCm)
docs.text:
• What is complete:
  • 26 Triton JIT kernels tuned for NVIDIA Ampere (SM 8.0) and Ada Lovelace (SM 8.9).
  • Pure PyTorch CPU / Apple Silicon MPS fallbacks for 100% of kernels.
  • What is NOT complete:
  • Hopper (SM 9.0) & Blackwell (SM 10.0) TMA: The kernels do not yet leverage hardware Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA) asynchronous copy descriptors (triton.language.extra.cuda.experimental_device_tensor_memory_accelerator), leaving 20–40% theoretical throughput on the table for H100/B200.
  • AMD ROCm (MI200/MI300) Autotuning: While Triton compiles to ROCm, the autotuning configs (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, num_warps) are optimized for NVIDIA warp sizes (32 threads) rather than AMD wavefront sizes (64 threads).

docs.title: Category 4: HNC-SVD Low-Rank Regimes (\(r \le 64\))
docs.text:
• What is complete:
  • Homotopy Numerical Continuation SVD mathematical equations and Riemannian nullspace step kernels are implemented.
  • Passes all 74 mathematical invariant tests.
  • Works stably for rank \(r \ge 128\).
  • What is NOT complete:
  • Catastrophic accuracy collapse at \(r \le 64\): Without progressive KD recovery, compressing deeply stacked networks (e.g. 72 linear layers across RoBERTa) using HNC-SVD at \(r=32\) causes relative output errors \(> 1.0\), resulting in 46.77% SST-2 accuracy (worse than random guessing).
  • The project currently handles this via Option C dispatching (falling back to adasvd or fwsvd for \(r \le 64\)), but the intrinsic mathematical error accumulation of pure HNC-SVD at extreme compression ratios remains unsolved.

docs.title: Category 5: Hugging Face Hub Static Model Weights
docs.text:
• What is complete:
  • Lightweight model cards with full surgery and inference code snippets created in docs/model_cards/.
  • Zero-shot in-place surgery (neuralops.replace_attention(model, "...")) capable of converting any Hugging Face checkpoint on-the-fly locally.
  • Baseline model tahamajs/distilbert-svd-attention hosted on the Hub.
  • What is NOT complete:
  • Pre-computed static weights for all 131 attention mechanisms across 8 backbones: Hosting static pre-trained checkpoints for \(131 \times 8 \approx 1,048\) combinations would require \(>450\text{ GB}\) of cloud storage. The project relies on local zero-shot surgery rather than hosted multi-terabyte model weights.

docs.title: Tutorial 1: End-to-End Quickstart
docs.text: This tutorial walks through loading a pre-trained transformer model, executing drop-in subquadratic attention surgery, compressing weights with calibrated low-rank SVD, and serving generation requests with continuous iteration-level dynamic batching in NeuralOps v1.6.0.

docs.title: 1. Installation
docs.text:
Install NeuralOps and its dependencies:

pip install "neuralops[core]"

For GPU acceleration with Triton JIT and native CUDA extensions:

pip install torch triton transformers accelerate

docs.title: 2. Complete Runnable Pipeline
docs.text:
The following script executes an end-to-end transformation in pure Python:

import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
import neuralops
from neuralops.integrations.tgi import TGIServingAdapter

device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
print(f"NeuralOps v{neuralops.__version__} initialized on {device}")

# 1. Load Pretrained Hugging Face Checkpoint
model_name = "gpt2"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_name).to(device)

# Ensure tokenizer has padding token defined
if tokenizer.pad_token is None:
    tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token

# 2. In-Place Attention Surgery: Replace O(L^2) Attention with Linear Cosformer
print("Performing in-place attention surgery...")
model = neuralops.replace_attention(
    model=model,
    attention="cosformer",
    copy_weights=True,
)
print("Surgery complete. Verified attention layers transplanted.")

# 3. Low-Rank Weight Compression: Fisher-Weighted SVD
print("Applying low-rank SVD compression...")
compressed_model = neuralops.compress(
    model=model,
    method="fwsvd",
    rank=32,
)
print("Compression complete. Parameters updated in-place.")

# 4. Continuous Batching Serving Runtime
print("Initializing continuous batcher...")
adapter = TGIServingAdapter(
    model=compressed_model,
    tokenizer=tokenizer,
    max_batch_size=8,
)

# Stream generated tokens in real time
prompt = "Subquadratic attention enables"
print(f"Generating from prompt: '{prompt}'")
print("Response: ", end="", flush=True)

for token_id, token_text in adapter.streaming_generate(prompt, max_new_tokens=20):
    print(token_text, end="", flush=True)
print("\n[Done]")

docs.title: 3. What Just Happened?
docs.text:
1. Topology Discovery: UniversalArchitectureScanner identified all attention projections (c_attn, c_proj) in gpt2.
  2. Endoskeletal Surgery: UniversalAttentionBridge transplanted cosformer linear attention in-place across all 12 transformer layers, preserving original projection weights, residuals, and layer normalization contracts.
  3. Calibrated SVD: fwsvd factorized projection matrices down to rank \(r=32\).
  4. Streaming Inference: TGIServingAdapter scheduled generation iterations through dynamic continuous batching, streaming decoded tokens with zero batch fragmentation.

docs.title: Tutorial 2: Hardware Roofline Profiling & Triton Kernel Efficiency
docs.text: Empirical roofline analysis models operational throughput (TFLOPS) as a function of arithmetic intensity (FLOPs/byte) relative to physical hardware compute ceilings and memory bandwidth boundaries on NVIDIA Ada Lovelace and Hopper GPUs.

docs.title: 1. Roofline Theory for Subquadratic Recurrences
docs.text:
Standard quadratic attention (\(\mathcal{O}(L^2)\)) accesses \(\mathcal{O}(B \cdot H \cdot L \cdot D)\) memory per attention layer but materializes an intermediate \(\mathcal{O}(B \cdot H \cdot L^2)\) attention matrix in global HBM, creating a severe memory-bandwidth bottleneck for sequence lengths \(L \ge 2048\).

Subquadratic linear attention reformulates the attention computation using associative recurrent state accumulation: $\(S_t = S_{t-1} + K_t^T V_t \in \mathbb{R}^{D \times D}\)$ $\(O_t = Q_t S_t \in \mathbb{R}^{D}\)$

By processing tokens in chunks of size \(C=64\) directly within GPU shared memory (SRAM), NeuralOps eliminates global memory roundtrips, shifting execution from the memory-bandwidth bound regime into the compute-bound regime.

docs.title: 3. Profiling Your Model with NeuralOps
docs.text:
You can profile any attention layer or custom module using neuralops.analysis.roofline.profile_roofline:

import torch
import neuralops
from neuralops.analysis.roofline import profile_roofline

# 1. Run automated roofline measurement for Gated DeltaNet
report = profile_roofline(
    module_or_name="gated_delta_net",
    batch_size=2,
    seq_len=2048,
    embed_dim=768,
    num_heads=12,
    dtype="float16" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "float32",
    warmup=10,
    rep=20,
)

print(f"Device:                  {report.device_name} ({report.sm_version})")
print(f"Arithmetic Intensity:   {report.arithmetic_intensity_fused:.2f} FLOPs/byte")
print(f"Achieved Throughput:    {report.achieved_tflops:.2f} TFLOPS")
print(f"Speedup vs PyTorch:     {report.speedup_x:.2f}x")
print(f"Operational Bottleneck: {report.bottleneck_regime}")

docs.title: Multi-Sequence Scaling Sweep
docs.text:
Profile scaling across sequence lengths to identify where the module transitions across the hardware ridge point:

seq_lengths = [512, 1024, 2048, 4096]

print(f"{'SeqLen':>8} | {'Intensity (FLOPs/B)':>20} | {'Throughput (TFLOPS)':>20} | {'Speedup':>10} | {'Regime':>15}")
print("-" * 82)

for sl in seq_lengths:
    rep = profile_roofline(
        module_or_name="gated_delta_net",
        batch_size=2,
        seq_len=sl,
        embed_dim=768,
        num_heads=12,
        warmup=5,
        rep=10,
    )
    print(
        f"{sl:>8} | "
        f"{rep.arithmetic_intensity_fused:>20.2f} | "
        f"{rep.achieved_tflops:>20.2f} | "
        f"{rep.speedup_x:>9.2f}x | "
        f"{rep.bottleneck_regime:>15}"
    )

docs.title: Tutorial 3: Serving Adapters & Production Deployment
docs.text: NeuralOps serving adapters provide multi-framework interfaces for high-throughput concurrent inference across Hugging Face Transformers, vLLM, Text Generation Inference (TGI), SGLang, and TensorRT-LLM in v1.6.0.

docs.title: 1. Hugging Face Drop-In Attention Surgery
docs.text:
Transplant any of NeuralOps' 131 attention mechanisms into an existing pre-trained Hugging Face model in-place:

import torch
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM
import neuralops

# 1. Load pre-trained model
model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("gpt2")

# 2. In-place surgery: replace dense multi-head attention with Gated DeltaNet
model = neuralops.replace_attention(
    model=model,
    attention="gated_delta_net",
    copy_weights=True,
)

# 3. Model retains standard Hugging Face AutoModel API
inputs = torch.randint(0, 50257, (1, 32))
outputs = model(inputs)
print("Logits shape:", outputs.logits.shape)

docs.title: 2. vLLM PagedStateTable (Recurrent Memory Virtualization)
docs.text:
Manage subquadratic recurrent states with block-virtualized GPU memory and Copy-on-Write semantics:

import torch
from neuralops.models.paged_state import PagedStateTable

device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
table = PagedStateTable(num_pages=1024, num_heads=12, head_dim=64, device=device)

# 1. Allocate initial recurrent page for root prompt
parent_pages = table.register_sequence(seq_id=1, initial_pages=1)
p0 = parent_pages[0]

# 2. Zero-copy sequence fork (e.g. beam search or parallel multi-candidate sampling)
child_pages = table.fork_sequence(parent_seq_id=1, child_seq_id=2)
assert table.ref_counts[p0] == 2

# 3. Automatic Copy-on-Write: child sequence gets private copy upon token decoding
new_p0 = table.prepare_write(seq_id=2, page_slot=0)
assert new_p0 != p0
assert table.ref_counts[p0] == 1
assert table.ref_counts[new_p0] == 1

# 4. Deallocate sequence memory upon request completion
table.free_sequence(seq_id=1)
table.free_sequence(seq_id=2)

docs.title: 3. Hugging Face TGI Continuous Batching & Streaming
docs.text:
Deploy models under continuous iteration-level batching with true token-by-token streaming:

from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
from neuralops.integrations.tgi import TGIServingAdapter

model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained("gpt2")
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("gpt2")
adapter = TGIServingAdapter(model=model, tokenizer=tokenizer, max_batch_size=16)

# Synchronous batch generation
completions = adapter.continuous_batching_generate(
    ["Explain subquadratic attention.", "What is low-rank factorization?"],
    max_new_tokens=25,
)
for comp in completions:
    print("Completion:", comp)

# Token-by-token streaming generator
for token_id, token_text in adapter.streaming_generate("Transformers scale by", max_new_tokens=15):
    print(token_text, end="", flush=True)
print()

docs.title: 4. SGLang Radix Tree Prefix Caching
docs.text:
Reuse historical KV and recurrent states across requests sharing system prompts or multi-turn dialogues:

import torch
from neuralops.integrations.sglang import SGLangRadixAdapter

adapter = SGLangRadixAdapter(model=None, tokenizer=None, max_cached_tokens=4096)
dummy_recurrent_state = torch.randn(2, 4, 16, 16)  # [B, H, D, D]

# 1. Cache common system prompt tokens
system_tokens = [101, 2054, 2003, 1037]
adapter.insert_prefix(system_tokens, dummy_recurrent_state)

# 2. Query prefix match on new user prompt
user_query_tokens = [101, 2054, 2003, 1037, 50256, 1999]
matched_len, cached_state = adapter.match_prefix(user_query_tokens)

print(f"Matched Prefix Tokens: {matched_len} / {len(system_tokens)}")
assert matched_len == 4
assert cached_state is not None

docs.title: 5. TensorRT-LLM Plugin Generation
docs.text:
Export custom C++ CUDA plugin definitions and serialized deployment manifests for NVIDIA TensorRT-LLM:

from neuralops.integrations.tensorrt_llm import TensorRTLLMPluginBuilder

builder = TensorRTLLMPluginBuilder(model=None, precision="float16")

# Generate standalone C++ / CUDA plugin files and CMakeLists.txt
generated_files = builder.generate_cpp_plugin_source("build/trt_plugins")
for name, path in generated_files.items():
    print(f"Generated: {name} -> {path}")

# Build serialized engine deployment manifest
manifest_path = builder.export_engine(engine_path="build/engines/model.engine")
print("Exported TensorRT-LLM engine manifest:", manifest_path)

docs.title: [RFC] Subquadratic Recurrent State Prefix Caching for SGLang RadixAttention
docs.text:
• RFC Target: sgl-project/sglang
  • Author: Taha Majlesi (neuralops maintainers)
  • Status: Proposed / Upstream RFC
  • Date: October 2026

docs.title: 1. Motivation
docs.text:
SGLang introduced RadixAttention, which maintains an in-memory Radix Tree over token sequences to reuse KV cache across multiple generation requests sharing common prefixes (e.g., system prompts, few-shot examples, multi-turn dialogues).

Standard RadixAttention stores \((K, V)\) tensor slices along radix edges. When using subquadratic linear attention models (e.g. Gated DeltaNet, RWKV-6, SVD Linear Attention), caching full sequence \((K, V)\) tokens wastes memory. Instead, caching the fixed-dimensional cumulative recurrent state \(S_t\) at prefix boundary nodes enables instantaneous \(O(1)\) prefill reuse without re-scanning historical tokens.

docs.title: 2. Proposed Architecture: SGLangRadixAdapter
docs.text:
We propose integrating SGLangRadixAdapter (neuralops.integrations.sglang.SGLangRadixAdapter) into SGLang's radix cache manager:

                  Root Node [Empty]
                  /               \
       System Prompt [Tokens 1..32] -> Cached State S_32
             /                 \
Few-Shot A [Tokens 33..64]   Few-Shot B [Tokens 33..64]
 -> Cached State S_64              -> Cached State S_64

docs.title: Key Technical Contributions
docs.text:
1. Recurrent State Node Caching: Radix tree nodes store recurrent_state: torch.Tensor alongside standard token IDs.
  2. Dynamic Prefix Branching & Splitting: Automatically splits node token arrays and computes intermediate states when new requests diverge mid-token chunk.
  3. Thread-Safe LRU Eviction: Manages VRAM footprint through an eviction queue targeting leaf nodes, guarded by Python threading RLock.

docs.title: 3. Reference Implementation & Tests
docs.text: Full production-grade implementation is located at neuralops/integrations/sglang.py with 7 unit tests in tests/test_framework_serving_adapters.py.

docs.title: [RFC] Native Linear Attention Continuous Batching Adapter for HuggingFace TGI
docs.text:
• RFC Target: huggingface/text-generation-inference
  • Author: Taha Majlesi (neuralops maintainers)
  • Status: Proposed / Upstream RFC
  • Date: October 2026

docs.title: 1. Motivation
docs.text: Text Generation Inference (TGI) provides ultra-high throughput continuous batching and token streaming for standard causal transformer models. However, when deploying compressed SVD attention models or non-softmax linear recurrent layers, standard flash-attention KV-cache prefill/decode logic incurs unnecessary cache resizing and memory allocation.

docs.title: 2. Proposed Architecture: TGIServingAdapter
docs.text:
We propose upstreaming the TGIServingAdapter protocol (neuralops.integrations.tgi.TGIServingAdapter) into TGI's router and generation engine:

[HTTP / gRPC Client] ---> [TGI Webserver / FastAPI Router]
                                    |
                                    v
                         [TGIServingAdapter]
                      (Continuous Batching Loop)
                         /          |          \
              Request 1          Request 2          Request 3
           (Active Prefill)   (Decode Token 4)   (Decode Token 19)

docs.title: Key Technical Contributions
docs.text:
1. Dynamic Slot Management: Handles heterogeneous prompt lengths without padding cross-talk by maintaining per-request continuous recurrent buffers.
  2. True Token-by-Token Streaming (TGIStreamingIterator): Yields decoded text chunks immediately as individual tokens are sampled, adhering to the Server-Sent Events (SSE) format expected by Hugging Face Hub clients.
  3. Stop Sequence & Repetition Penalty Enforcement: High-efficiency in-flight checking against user-specified stop tokens and max sequence limits.

docs.title: 3. Reference Implementation & Tests
docs.text: Reference implementation resides at neuralops/integrations/tgi.py with 7 dedicated unit tests verified in tests/test_framework_serving_adapters.py.

docs.title: [RFC] Integration of NeuralOps Paged Recurrent State Cache in vLLM
docs.text:
• RFC Target: vllm-project/vllm
  • Author: Taha Majlesi (neuralops maintainers)
  • Status: Proposed / Upstream RFC
  • Date: October 2026

docs.title: 1. Motivation
docs.text:
vLLM's PagedAttention revolutionized transformer inference by partitioning standard multi-head attention KV caches into fixed-size virtual blocks. However, emerging subquadratic architectures (e.g. Gated DeltaNet, GLA, RetNet, RWKV, Mamba, and SVD Linear Attention) maintain fixed-dimensional recurrent state tensors \(S_t \in \mathbb{R}^{B \times H \times D \times D}\) rather than token-accumulating \(O(T)\) KV matrices.

When deploying hybrid or pure subquadratic models in vLLM, allocating contiguous \(O(T)\) buffers wastes GPU VRAM and violates vLLM's memory management paradigm.

docs.title: 2. Proposed Architecture: PagedStateTable
docs.text:
We propose integrating PagedStateTable (neuralops.models.paged_state.PagedStateTable) as an official vLLM state management backend for linear recurrent models:

+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                        vLLM BlockManager                          |
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                  |
         +------------------------+------------------------+
         |                                                 |
         v                                                 v
Standard Attention                                Linear Recurrence
(K, V) Tokens Paging                           Fixed Block PagedStateTable
[Block Size: 16 tokens]                        [Block: H x D x D state]

docs.title: Key Capabilities
docs.text:
1. Virtual Page Allocation: Maps dynamic sequence IDs to non-contiguous recurrent state blocks in physical GPU memory.
  2. Copy-on-Write (CoW): Enables \(O(1)\) zero-copy sequence forking for parallel sampling and beam search. When a sequence branches, child sequences share the parent page until the first autoregressive recurrent step.
  3. Constant VRAM Overhead: Bounded memory footprint regardless of prompt or generation length.

docs.title: 3. Reference Implementation
docs.text: The complete PyTorch and CUDA-compatible implementation is provided in neuralops/models/paged_state.py and benchmarked in tests/test_vllm_and_sglang_plugins.py.
